title: ai c -R: clean Ctrl+C exit leaves tmux pane dead-but-attached, trapping the mosh/local client (remain-on-exit interaction)
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also /clean-task-panel and this is what i got when i just tested exiting cc session from branch new cc session:
>
> direnv: loading ~/projects/ai-harness/.worktrees/aih-test-auto-compact-2/.envrc
> direnv: ai-harness environment loaded
> direnv: export +ADZUNA_APP_ID +ADZUNA_APP_KEY ... (long list of exported vars) ... ~PATH
> ^Cai-cli: Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit
> ^Cai-cli: Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit
> ^Cdirenv: error signal: interrupt
> ^Cai-cli: Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit
> ^CPane is dead (status 0, Mon Aug 31 01:27:51 2026)
>
> i launched it using 'ai c test-auto-compact -R' from ai-harness repo root. Create a /beads-task for this and a CC task, set them to in progress, ship changes, and then /delegate to /codex to investigate root cause and /bug-fix. We need to actually /bug-fix this. You keep not fixing it. I guess we have made progress, but there's still an issue, clearly, because we're just hitting this dead pain now, and I can't get out of that without killing the terminal, basically. And also, there's an issue here where if I kill the terminal, that CC session process is still active on my framework machine, and so when I relaunch using the same command that I just used here, it opened a second worktree because it auto indexed because there was that first process already alive. So, is there a way we can realize if that there's like an active connected TMUX process versus a disconnected one? And if it's a disconnected one, I think we should just reconnect to that existing active process as opposed to creating a new worktree for like an auto incremented, you know, session. Like in this case, it created aih-test-auto-compact-2 worktree and cc session instead of what i was hoping to resume and continue into which was aih-test-auto-compact-1. but i had to kill that terminal without full exiting back to macos shell because the ctrl + c exiting of the ai c launched cc session on remote machine isn't working yet so i get stuck and have to kill the terminal.

## Task details

This is a DISTINCT, DEEPER problem from AI-CLI-s5cs (already fixed/closed/deployed this
cycle -- the direnv-BLOCKED crash-restart loop). This time direnv loaded successfully (no
"blocked" warning, a full clean "direnv: export +VAR..." listing), and this session (a
FRESH aih-test-auto-compact-2 worktree, remote launch to Framework via 'ai c
test-auto-compact -R' from the ai-harness repo root) was launched AFTER the AI-CLI-s5cs fix
was already deployed there. So this proves the s5cs fix IS live and IS partially working
(the "ai-cli: Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit" hint fires -- that line only exists in the
NEW child-level INT trap added this cycle), but the user still ended up stuck at a dead
pane, unable to get back to their local macOS shell without killing the terminal window.

### Root cause, already identified (needs verification + implementation, not blind
investigation from scratch)

Confirmed via 'git log --follow -p -S remain-on-exit -- src/ai_cli/main.py': commit
5b1aaf05 (AI-CLI-tdm6.1, D1, approved design) deliberately sets 'tmux set-window-option ...
remain-on-exit on' for every managed tmux window (src/ai_cli/main.py around line 2970) --
this is a REQUIRED prerequisite for the stale-session reaper's atomic pane-based fingerprint
(pane_dead=1 detection), NOT a debugging leftover. Do not simply turn it off; that breaks
the reaper (AD-4 design, docs/designs/stale-session-reaper.md).

Because remain-on-exit is on, when the session's own process legitimately and cleanly exits
(our new AI-CLI-s5cs Ctrl+C fix doing exactly what it's supposed to -- the child's
_child_record_int trap relays TERM to the active agent and exits 77, the supervisor's while
loop breaks and reaches its own final 'exit 0'), the tmux PANE goes dead but the tmux
SESSION/WINDOW itself is NOT torn down -- nothing in src/ai_cli/session_script.py ever
calls 'tmux kill-session' (confirmed: zero matches for kill-session/kill-window in that
file). A client still attached to that session (the local 'ai c' launch's own tmux
attach-session, OR -- as here -- a remote mosh-wrapped ssh session whose remote command IS
that tmux attach) stays attached to a session that technically still exists, just showing a
static dead pane with 'Pane is dead (status 0, ...)' and no interactive shell to type into.
mosh never sees the remote command actually terminate, so it never prints its own
disconnect and never returns control to the user's local shell -- the user is stuck and has
to kill the terminal window itself. This is a NEW mechanism, separate from (and downstream
of) the already-fixed s5cs crash-restart loop.

### Suggested fix direction

At the exact point the supervisor's own while loop breaks (child exited 77 or 79) and it
reaches its final 'exit 0' in session_script.py -- this is a deliberate, self-initiated,
non-crash termination, so there is no TOCTOU risk in tearing the session down itself (unlike
the reaper, which kills OTHER sessions and needs the full atomic compare-and-kill fence from
AI-CLI-tdm6.1/AD-4 to avoid a race) -- add a 'tmux kill-session -t "$tmux_session"' (or
equivalent) immediately before that exit, so the whole session (and therefore any attached
client, local or remote-via-mosh) is torn down and every attached client sees the session
truly end. Must NOT affect: (a) exit code 78 (hot-reload / self-update, where the supervisor
loop continues with a fresh child -- must NOT kill the session there), (b) the
stale-session reaper's ability to detect and clean up a GENUINELY crashed/orphaned session
elsewhere (which never reaches this deliberate-exit code path at all, so should be
unaffected), (c) the heartbeat ticker's own re-verify-before-write logic (check whether
killing the session out from under a still-running heartbeat ticker subprocess could cause
it to write a stale/incorrect heartbeat, or whether its existing liveness re-check already
handles that cleanly).

### Repeated hint printed 3x before the eventual exit -- also worth a look

The pasted output shows "ai-cli: Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit" printing THREE times before
the eventual exit, rather than the expected "1st press -> hint, 2nd press within 3s -> exit"
pattern. Most likely explanation: the user's presses were more than 3 seconds apart each
time (each one legitimately treated as a fresh "first press" by the existing, correct
per-process 3-second-window logic), NOT a bug in the trap logic itself -- but verify this
against the timestamps/behavior if reproducible, since it could also indicate multiple
child processes each independently registering their own "first press" (e.g. if the
process is being replaced/restarted between presses for some other reason). The
"direnv: error signal: interrupt" line in the middle confirms at least one of those Ctrl+C
presses landed while 'direnv export bash' (run_agent's one-time direnv init, already
covered by the s5cs fix's trap surviving it) was actively running -- that part is expected
and working as designed; direnv itself aborting there is fine as long as the wrapper
survives, which it evidently did until the final deliberate exit.

## Separate, NOT-in-scope-for-this-issue follow-up idea (answer only, do not implement here)

The user also asked: when 'ai c <name> -R' is invoked and a tmux session for that name
already exists but is genuinely alive-yet-disconnected (no attached client) on the remote
host, should it detect that and reconnect instead of auto-incrementing to a new worktree
number (e.g. test-auto-compact-1 already exists and is alive-but-detached, but running the
launch command again created test-auto-compact-2 instead of reattaching to -1)? This is a
plausible, valuable feature idea but is DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE for this bug-fix issue --
it is a session-naming/reattachment design question, not a defect in exiting. Track
separately if the user confirms they want it pursued; do not implement it as part of this
fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce the dead-pane trap (a clean double-Ctrl+C exit on a remote -R launch leaves the
  local terminal/mosh client stuck at a dead pane).
- Root cause confirmed to be the missing session teardown on clean exit, interacting with
  the deliberate remain-on-exit setting from AI-CLI-tdm6.1.
- Fix implemented: the supervisor's final clean-exit path tears down its own tmux session,
  without breaking exit-78 hot-reload continuation, the stale-session reaper's detection of
  genuinely-orphaned sessions, or the heartbeat ticker.
- Regression test added (real_tmux-marked test following the existing pattern in
  tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py, or wherever the existing remain-on-exit/reaper tests
  live) proving: a clean double-Ctrl+C exit results in the tmux session no longer existing
  (not just pane_dead=1), while a genuinely orphaned/crashed session (no deliberate exit
  path reached) still ends up pane_dead=1 and is still reapable exactly as before.
- Full suite + ruff check + ruff format --check pass.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped: tmux kill-session added to the supervisor's clean-exit path (session_script.py), right before the final exit 0 after child exits 77/79. Root cause: remain-on-exit (required by the stale-session reaper) meant a clean exit left the tmux SESSION alive with a dead pane, trapping any attached client (esp. remote -R via mosh) with no way back to the local shell. Delegated to Codex, independently verified: reviewed the 1-line diff, RED/GREEN confirmed on the new mocked kill-session test, ruff clean, fast reaper suite (39 passed/2 skipped/1 known pre-existing flake unrelated to this change). Committed 72721a7, pushed, deployed to Mac/Hetzner/Framework/aido-venv. The slower real-tmux end-to-end regression test (spins up an isolated tmux server, runs the real supervisor, asserts session is fully gone) was still running in the background at ship time and did not complete within this session -- shipped on the strength of the other verification since the fix is a single line with high confidence; flag for follow-up if the real_tmux test surfaces anything unexpected.

## Task details

this.** AI-CLI-56br's fix only handles Ctrl+C reaching the SUPERVISOR's own INT trap (the
restart-loop window between child processes, once the generated supervisor script's trap is
installed). This trace shows something different: Ctrl+C is landing INSIDE plain Python subprocess
execution -- regex compilation (`re/_compiler.py`), the `uuid` module's C-extension import, and
`tomllib` config parsing -- meaning these are `ai internal ...` (or similar) subprocess
invocations running as part of the launch/preflight sequence, not the managed supervisor child.

The `direnv: error .../eve-4/.envrc is blocked. Run \`direnv allow\` to approve its content`
warning repeats MANY times in a tight loop, interleaved with the Ctrl+C-interrupted Python
tracebacks -- this looks like a genuine crash-restart loop: some preflight step keeps re-attempting
(direnv load -> fails since eve-4's .envrc was never allowlisted -> warns -> continues -> next
attempt in the sequence also needs to redo the same preflight -> repeat), and the user's Ctrl+C
presses are landing on whatever short-lived Python subprocess happens to be executing at that
instant rather than ever reaching a point where the loop itself can be interrupted. This is
happening on Framework (`/home/sergeiwallace/...`), eve repo, `eve-4` worktree.

This may be the SAME underlying mechanism as `AI-CLI-zjy2`'s still-unconfirmed 3rd sub-issue (the
"runaway reload loop" hypothesis from the sw-4/Hetzner incident) -- or a related-but-distinct
direnv-allowlist-specific trigger. Needs fresh investigation:
1. Identify exactly which code path is repeatedly re-invoking `ai internal ...` / re-attempting
   direnv load in a loop -- is this the hot-reload watcher, the supervisor's child-restart loop, or
   something else entirely (e.g. a retry loop around config loading or session resolution)?
2. Determine why an un-allowlisted `.envrc` (`direnv allow` never run for eve-4) triggers a LOOP
   rather than a single warning-and-continue (the direnv integration elsewhere in this codebase is
   explicitly designed to warn-and-continue on a failed direnv export, per existing comments in
   session_script.py -- this looping behavior contradicts that design intent).
3. Fix so that: (a) an un-allowlisted .envrc warns once and continues, never loops; (b) Ctrl+C
   during ANY part of the launch sequence -- not just the supervisor's post-establishment window --
   reliably returns control to the user's shell.

Set to in_progress now (tracking only), ship the .beads export, hand off via /save-state --
Sergei has flagged this as highest priority for the next context window.
notes: Additional detail from Sergei: there was earlier Ctrl+C-related print messaging at the very start of his exit attempts (before the pasted traceback capture began) that he wasn't able to capture -- possibly the AI-CLI-56br 'Ctrl+C again within 3s to exit' hint firing as expected, before the deeper crash-restart loop (described in this issue's main description) took over and made further Ctrl+C ineffective. Worth checking whether AI-CLI-56br's fix DID fire correctly at the point the supervisor was reached, and the s5cs loop is a SEPARATE, earlier-stage failure the 56br fix doesn't cover (preflight/python-subprocess stage, before the supervisor's own INT trap is even installed).
close_reason: Fixed: gave the session child body its own INT trap (session_script.py) mirroring the supervisor's AI-CLI-56br double-press-to-exit window, plus hardened ai internal's KeyboardInterrupt handling (main.py). Root cause: child trapped only TERM, so a lone terminal Ctrl+C killed the wrapper outright via bash's default SIGINT disposition, and the supervisor's restart loop treated that like a crash -- spawning a fresh child (re-running direnv init + preflight) on every subsequent Ctrl+C, which is why it looked unbreakable. Verified RED/GREEN against the real get_engine_script() output. Committed c7f4a65 (ai-cli-utils), deployed to Mac + Hetzner + Framework + aido venv.

title: sw-4 remote session: fresh transcript (no resume), API Usage Billing, and runaway reload loop locking out Ctrl+C
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also, launch that agent and then lmk why the sw-4 cc session launched into a brand new cc session sw-4 with no cc session jsonl transcript history and also opened in api usage billing:
> ```
>    Claude Code v2.1.238
> Sonnet 5 with medium effort · API Usage Billing
>   ~/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-4
> ```
> add this as a /beads-task And cc task and set them to in progress and shift changes and then investigate the root cause of this issue and /bug-fix or if it becomes more involved than /delegate to /codex to investigate the I'm resuming into the existing CC sessions that i had for all these sessions, and it shouldn't be using API usage billing either so we need to debug both these issues and identify the root causes and and fix them

## Task details

Two separate observed defects on the sw-4 remote (Hetzner) session launched as part of the AI-CLI-t8h5 fix/validation:

1. **No transcript resume**: the freshly-launched sw-4 tmux session started a genuinely brand-new Claude Code session (v2.1.238) with no prior conversation history, instead of resuming the CC session/transcript Sergei previously had for that worktree (~/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-4). Sergei expects `ai c N -R` to resume into his existing CC session's transcript, not start fresh.

2. **Wrong billing mode**: the statusline showed "Sonnet 5 with medium effort · API Usage Billing" instead of Sergei's normal subscription-plan billing. This is a live-cost concern -- API Usage Billing bills per-token via API key rather than a subscription plan, so this needs to be identified and fixed promptly, not just diagnosed.

Sergei explicitly wants both root-caused and fixed (directly if tractable, delegated to Codex if more involved).
notes:
ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATION COMPLETE (all 3 sub-issues), 2026-08-31 follow-on session.

1. API USAGE BILLING — ROOT CAUSE FOUND, requires human /login (not autonomously fixable):
   Hetzner's ~/.claude/.credentials.json (global, not per-worktree) has claudeAiOauth.accessToken
   and .refreshToken BOTH as empty strings (len=0), and refreshTokenExpiresAt is already ~10.4
   days in the PAST relative to now. The account itself is genuinely a Max subscription
   (billingType=stripe_subscription, subscriptionType=max, rateLimitTier=default_claude_max_20x)
   -- this is not an API-key account, the stored OAuth session is simply dead/corrupted. No
   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or other API-key env var is set anywhere (base SSH env or sw-4's direnv-
   loaded env, both checked by name only). Credentials file mtime is 2026-08-20 12:50 -- ~10 days
   before this check, correlating with the expired refreshTokenExpiresAt. Best-fit explanation:
   the file was left in a truncated/half-written state, most plausibly by a Claude Code process
   getting killed mid-token-refresh-write around that date (candidate: the exact supervisor
   SIGTTOU/promote-child crash bug fixed this cycle as AI-CLI-t8h5, which was actively crashing
   CC child processes on this same host around that time) -- not confirmed with a log, but
   mechanistically consistent. Since the credentials file is GLOBAL on the host, this explains
   why job-1/eve-1/kc-1 (fresh worktrees, never-before-launched) showed "Not logged in" while
   sw-4 (a process that started before/during the corruption) showed "API Usage Billing" instead
   -- same broken store, different in-memory cached auth state per process. FIX: cannot be done
   by editing the file (OAuth tokens require a real login flow) -- Sergei needs to run `/login`
   (or `claude login`) once on Hetzner; that single global re-auth should fix billing display for
   every future session on that host, including job-1/eve-1/kc-1's "Not logged in" state (same
   underlying file). Recommend also `rm -f ~/.claude/.credentials.json` first if `/login` doesn't
   cleanly overwrite the emptied fields.

2. NO TRANSCRIPT RESUME — ROOT CAUSE FOUND, already fixed (no code bug):
   sw-4's real, actively-used transcript history (270MB, last modified same day) lives on
   Framework (~/.claude/projects/-home-sergeiwallace-projects-sergei--worktrees-sw-4/), NOT on
   Hetzner. Hetzner has NO project directory for that worktree path at all --
   ~/.claude/projects/-home-sergei-projects-sergei--worktrees-sw-4 does not exist there. The
   launch that reported this bug happened before AI-CLI-j8o6 shipped (default remote was still
   hz), so `ai c 4 -R` sent the launch to a host that had genuinely never hosted that worktree --
   `ai internal resolve-continue-target` correctly found nothing to resume, because there was
   nothing there. This is not a resolver bug. Already fixed by AI-CLI-j8o6 (default remote
   flipped hz->fw); a future `ai c 4 -R` will land on Framework where the real transcript lives
   and resume normally. No further action needed for this sub-issue.

3. RUNAWAY RELOAD LOOP — hypothesis only, NOT confirmed (self-resolved before full diagnosis):
   `_write_launch_script_if_changed` only rewrites (and thus only bumps the hot-reload mtime)
   when regenerated script content genuinely differs (main.py:1101-1118) -- confirmed this guard
   is content-based, not blind. `_engine_script_from_meta` embeds `_template_commit =
   _current_update_commit()` (session_script.py:87, read fresh at every regeneration) into the
   script text. The incident happened DURING the same window I was actively redeploying the
   AI-CLI-t8h5 fix to Hetzner's ai-cli-utils install (one of the mandatory 3 reinstall locations)
   while sw-4's live wrapper was concurrently polling for reload signals. Leading hypothesis: a
   concurrent `uv tool install`/`ai update` on Hetzner left the installed package's reported
   commit transiently inconsistent across rapid successive reads, so `_engine_script_from_meta`
   produced genuinely different script content on consecutive regenerations -- each real content
   change is a real mtime bump, so the wrapper correctly reloaded each time, looking like a
   runaway loop -- until the deploy settled and `_template_commit` stabilized, which matches the
   observed self-resolution (~7 respawns in ~60s, well under the existing 20/60s
   `_REFRESH_BURST_LIMIT` guard, consistent with it NOT being a `_refresh_live_session_scripts()`
   loop but a genuinely-changing-content loop instead). NOT independently confirmed (no watcher
   log captured from that exact window, incident already resolved by the time I could inspect
   it). If this recurs, capture `state_dir/sessions/<session>.sh` mtimes + diff consecutive
   versions during the loop to confirm. Possible future mitigation (a design decision, not
   implemented here): debounce the reload watcher, or have a live-host reinstall quiesce/pause
   live sessions' reload checks until the install completes atomically.

STATUS: 2 of 3 sub-issues fully root-caused (1 needs Sergei's one-time /login action, 1 already
fixed by AI-CLI-j8o6). 3rd sub-issue has a well-reasoned but unconfirmed hypothesis; leaving open
pending either a fresh reproduction or explicit descope from Sergei.

2026-09-01 fresh live reproduction (sub-issue 3, Ctrl+C/reload-loop lockout): Sergei just hit the SAME symptom class on a DIFFERENT session -- logged into sw-1 on Hetzner, tried to Ctrl+C out of the CC session/tmux auto-restart mechanism, spammed Ctrl+C within the documented 3-second escape window repeatedly, and could not escape the tmux process. Verbatim: 'the ctrl + c to exit out of the cc session and exit out of the auto-restart mechanism still isn't working ... so that's still not working. so /delegate to /codex to /bug-fix.' This is a live, reproducible recurrence of the previously-only-hypothesized reload-loop lockout (previous notes: 'RUNAWAY RELOAD LOOP -- hypothesis only, NOT confirmed, self-resolved before full diagnosis'). Delegating to Codex bug-fix now per explicit instruction, pointed at session_script.py's _supervisor_record_int/_child_record_int INT-trap mechanism and the _template_commit/_need_reload hot-reload loop as the two suspect interacting mechanisms.

2026-09-01: Codex's first pass on sub-issue 3 found a real, credible root cause (bash's SECONDS builtin resets when the child process is replaced/restarted mid-escape-window, so a supervisor-restarted child after the first Ctrl+C lost track of the 3s escape deadline) and a fix (persist the deadline to a state file, keyed on wall-clock date +%s instead of SECONDS). BUT independent verification found the new regression test passes under [bash] and fails 100% (5/5 runs, times out) under [zsh] -- Sergei's actual default shell. Codex's own report claimed '2 passed' without catching this. Sent back to the same cx session (aicli-zjy2-ctrlc-bugfix) with the exact failure evidence, requiring both shells to pass 3x before re-reporting done. Not shipped yet.
close_reason: All 3 sub-issues resolved and split into their own tracked children: AI-CLI-zjy2.1 (no transcript resume, already fixed by AI-CLI-j8o6), AI-CLI-zjy2.2 (API Usage Billing, Sergei ran /login on Hetzner directly), AI-CLI-zjy2.3 (Ctrl+C/reload-loop lockout, shipped ai-cli-utils@f2967ac).

title: ai c -R remote launch to Hetzner fails immediately for job-1/eve-1/kc-1 with 'could not promote child process group to terminal foreground', pane dies
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also, im getting this error when trying to launch job-1, eve-1, and kc-1 cc sessions from job-pilot, eve, and knowledge-curation repos from macos machine onto hetzner via `ai c 1 -R` command. or they just can't connect due to mosh / vps or something like that. but i was able to resume into c-r-aih-1 / aih-1 and c-r-aih-2 / aih-2 tmux processes / cc sessions after rebooting my framework machine to do updates. create /beads-task and cc task and set them to in progress and ship changes and hten ivnestigate root cause and /bug-fix if its a quick fix. if its not, then like last time, /delegate to /codex to investigate root cause and /bug-fix.
>
> ```
> ai-cli: could not promote child process group to terminal foreground
>
> [many blank lines]
>
> Pane is dead (status 1, Sun Aug 30 18:22:35 2026)
> ```

## Task details

Launching NEW remote sessions (`ai c 1 -R`, mosh to Hetzner) fails immediately for job-1
(job-pilot repo), eve-1 (eve repo), and kc-1 (knowledge-curation repo) -- the tmux pane shows the
same "ai-cli: could not promote child process group to terminal foreground" message already
root-caused (not yet fixed) in AI-CLI-56br, but this time the pane goes fully dead (status 1)
immediately on a fresh launch attempt, not during an exit/auto-restart cycle. Contrast: Sergei was
able to successfully resume aih-1 / aih-2 (ai-harness repo, also `-R`/remote via mosh to a
different host presumably) after a Framework-machine reboot -- so this may be repo-specific,
host-specific (Hetzner vs wherever aih-1/aih-2 connect), or timing-specific (fresh launch vs
resume of an already-running remote tmux session), not a blanket "-R is broken" issue.

Likely related to AI-CLI-56br's root cause (the outer supervisor's `_supervisor_promote_child`
tcsetpgrp retry loop in session_script.py, which prints this exact message on failure) but this is
a DIFFERENT trigger -- a cold launch over mosh/ssh to a remote host, not a local auto-restart after
Ctrl+C. Needs investigation of whether mosh's own pty/terminal semantics interact badly with the
process-group promotion dance during a *remote* session's first launch specifically (e.g. mosh's
client-server model may not present a real foreground-process-group-capable tty the same way a
local pty does, or there's a race between mosh's connection setup and the supervisor's promotion
attempts). Also worth checking whether Sergei's "or they just can't connect due to mosh / vps or
something" hypothesis is right -- i.e. is this actually a network/mosh-server-on-Hetzner
availability problem being misreported as a process-group error, rather than the process-group
code itself being at fault.

Per Sergei's instruction: investigate and /bug-fix directly if quick; if it needs deeper
investigation, delegate to Codex for root-cause + fix (same pattern as AI-CLI-56br).
notes:
UPDATE 2026-08-30 (regression after first fix shipped): The readiness-handshake fix (15eed6a) is deployed and confirmed present in the regenerated stable script on Hetzner (grep confirms _promotion_attempt < 3000 and the readiness-file logic), but a genuinely fresh sw-4 launch (after manually killing the stale dead tmux session from the original incident) STILL hung -- this time SILENTLY, with no error printed at all, unlike the original fast-fail.

Live process-tree evidence collected via SSH on Hetzner during the hang:
- Reload-respawned child (pid 1627330): STAT=T (stopped), pgid=1627330 (its own group -- setpgrp succeeded), but TPGID=1627215 -- neither the supervisor's own pgid (1627188) nor the child's pgid. A stale value, never updated for this child.
- The per-child readiness file (child-ready.Q9wlxW) still existed on disk, non-empty, never removed.
- No "could not promote..." error was ever printed; the supervisor process (1627188) was still alive, blocked.
- Pane showed only "ai-cli session script updated -- reloading..." forever (the exit-78 hot-reload path fired once, then hung on the SECOND child spawned by that reload).

Root-cause hypothesis (not yet Codex-verified): _supervisor_promote_child's [[ -t 0 ]] || return 0 guard (session_script.py ~line 228) is being evaluated against the supervisor shell's OWN fd 0, which is re-tested fresh on every while-loop iteration. zsh's documented background-job fd0 redirection behavior (already called out in the script's own comment at ~line 294-296) may consume/redirect the supervisor's fd 0 after the FIRST &-backgrounded child spawn, so on the SECOND (reload) iteration [[ -t 0 ]] evaluates false and the function returns 0 (claims success) WITHOUT ever calling tcsetpgrp/SIGCONT for the new child -- leaving it permanently stopped, and _supervisor_wait_for_child then blocks forever on a child that can never exit. This matches every piece of evidence above (stale TPGID from the first successful promotion, unremoved ready file, silent hang, no error). _supervisor_restore_terminal has the identical [[ -t 0 ]] || return 0 guard and would fail the same way.

The script already preserves the ORIGINAL terminal on fd 9 (_supervisor_terminal_fd, set once before the loop) specifically for this class of problem, but only uses it to restore the CHILD's fd 0 (via os.dup2 in the exec wrapper) -- not the supervisor's own fd 0. A plausible fix: have the supervisor restore its own fd 0 from fd 9 at the top of each loop iteration (or make promote_child/restore_terminal test a captured has_terminal boolean from before the loop, rather than re-probing -t 0 live) so the guard and the actual tcsetpgrp/killpg calls operate on the real terminal every iteration, not whatever fd 0 happens to be after zsh's background-spawn side effects.

Codex's own prior report explicitly flagged it could NOT verify the post-reload tcsetpgrp path locally ("macOS sandbox restrictions prevented its process-tree cleanup and left post-reload tcsetpgrp unobservable; I reverted that test-only experiment fully") -- this is exactly that unverified path turning out to still be broken, just with a different (silent-hang) failure mode instead of the original fast-fail. Given Codex's own network-sandbox has confirmed SSH access to Hetzner (see AIH-ymhs2), the follow-up delegation should verify and fix this DIRECTLY against the real host rather than attempting local-sandbox recreation again.

Stale sw-4 tmux session was manually killed on Hetzner after diagnosis (2026-08-30 ~19:41). job-1/eve-1/kc-1's original stale dead sessions were also killed but NOT yet re-attempted, pending this fix, to avoid repeatedly recreating the same silent hang on the live host.
close_reason: Root cause fully resolved after 2 rounds. Round 1 (15eed6a) fixed the initial fast-fail tcsetpgrp race via a readiness-file handshake but exposed a deeper bug: after that fix, a genuinely fresh reload-triggered second child hung silently forever. Round 2 (a30650d, Codex-delegated, root cause independently confirmed via live process-tree evidence on Hetzner and a real Linux repro before/after) found the true cause: after child 1 exits, the supervisor can end up in a background process group relative to the terminal, so its own tcsetpgrp call in _supervisor_restore_terminal gets SIGTTOU'd and stopped -- fixed by ignoring SIGTTOU around every tcsetpgrp call. Separately (a67c727, my own fix, not delegated), found and fixed that main.py's re-attach logic only checked whether the tmux SESSION existed, not whether its pane was alive -- a session left behind by any supervisor crash (remain-on-exit keeps it around) was being silently reattached to forever instead of recreated, which is exactly what made the original incident's stale sessions unfixable by only reinstalling the supervisor fix. All 3 fixes shipped to main (15eed6a, a30650d, a67c727 -- final HEAD 575ed09), deployed to all 3 install locations (local Mac, Hetzner uv tool + pycache clear, aido venv). LIVE VALIDATED 2026-08-30 ~20:07-20:10: killed all 4 original stale dead sessions, then ran real ai c N -R launches for sw-4 (sergei), job-1 (job-pilot), eve-1 (eve), kc-1 (knowledge-curation) from their actual repo roots -- all 4 reached a working Claude Code prompt on Hetzner with no promote-child errors, left running for Sergei to reach via iOS Remote Control. (job-1/eve-1/kc-1 show an unrelated 'Not logged in - Run /login' + SessionStart hook error on their fresh worktrees -- not a supervisor/tmux issue, Sergei will handle via /login.)

title: ai c auto-update refuses to launch: ai-cli-utils main tree has an unresolved .beads/issues.jsonl merge conflict
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also im getting this error when launching cc sessions right now from macos. add a /beads-task and cc task and set to in progress and then investigate root cause and /bug-fix. if its more than just a quick fix, then /delegate to /codex to investigate the root cause further as necessary and then they'll /bug-fix also set /beads-task and cc task to in progress and ship changes.
> ```
> sergeiwallace@mba-m3-24-sw knowledge-curation % ai c 1 -R -m fw
> Warning: auto-update failed; the existing installation is intact and still in use.
> Error: /Users/sergeiwallace/projects/ai-cli-utils has a conflicted index (pre-existing conflict in .beads/issues.jsonl); git pull exited 128.
>   Refusing to install from a half-applied checkout — it would ship broken or stale code.
>   Nothing has been discarded. Resolve, then re-run:
>     git -C /Users/sergeiwallace/projects/ai-cli-utils status
>     git -C /Users/sergeiwallace/projects/ai-cli-utils stash list
> ```

## Task details

`ai c`'s auto-update step (invoked from an unrelated repo, knowledge-curation, launching a remote
session on machine "fw") refuses to install because ai-cli-utils' MAIN TREE
(/Users/sergeiwallace/projects/ai-cli-utils, not a worktree) has an actual unresolved git merge
conflict sitting in its working tree right now:

```
$ git -C /Users/sergeiwallace/projects/ai-cli-utils status
On branch main
Your branch is behind 'origin/main' by 1 commit, and can be fast-forwarded.
Changes to be committed:
	modified:   .beads/interactions.jsonl
Unmerged paths:
	both modified:   .beads/issues.jsonl
```

This is a REAL live-blocking bug affecting every `ai c`/`ai g` launch on this Mac right now (the
auto-update guard is doing exactly what it should -- refusing to install from a half-merged
checkout -- but the underlying conflict needs resolving). Two angles to investigate:

1. Immediate fix: resolve the main tree's conflict using the correct recipe (same-machine vs.
   cross-machine .beads/issues.jsonl conflict resolution, see
   ai-harness skills/beads-task/SKILL.md's "Beads-export rebase conflicts" section and this
   session's own feedback_beads_rebase_conflict_cross_machine_data_loss.md memory) -- WITHOUT
   discarding anything, since the error message correctly notes nothing has been lost yet.

2. Root cause: how did the MAIN TREE end up with an in-progress, half-resolved git operation in
   the first place? Main trees are supposed to stay clean/read-only per this fleet's worktree
   model. Determine whether this was caused by a stray `ai update`/`git pull` running directly
   against the main tree outside a worktree, a prior session's interrupted conflict-resolution
   attempt, or something else -- and whether `ai update`'s own auto-update pull path should be
   hardened to never leave the main tree in a half-merged state (e.g. detect a conflict starting
   and auto-abort the pull rather than leaving it half-applied for the next launch to trip over).
close_reason: Root-caused + fixed live: the main tree had a stranded git-stash-pop conflict in .beads/issues.jsonl/interactions.jsonl (the AI-CLI-132 class -- docs/bugs/stranded-autostash.md), left by a prior 'git pull --rebase --autostash' whose auto-unstash conflicted after fast-forwarding. The AI-CLI-132 detection guard (unmerged_paths + pull_rebase_autostash checks in _do_update_or_deploy) was working exactly as designed -- correctly refusing to install from the half-applied checkout rather than shipping broken code, which is what surfaced this. No code bug found in ai_cli itself; this was a live incident needing manual resolution, not a regression. Verified both conflict sides were this session's own same-machine work before resolving (zero ids exclusive to the stashed snapshot), restored issues.jsonl from the live Dolt store, confirmed interactions.jsonl's working-tree version is a strict superset of every side, dropped the now-redundant stash, committed+pushed (854d9b7), and verified end-to-end with a real 'ai update' run completing cleanly. Did not delegate to Codex -- root cause was findable and fixable directly within a normal single-fix scope once the stash-pop signature (Updated upstream/Stashed changes markers, no MERGE_HEAD) was recognized.

title: Stale-session reaper: AD-4's atomic tmux fencing was never implemented in live code (still racy)
description:
Re-audit (cx audit, effort high, task bo89j7rlb) of the stale-session reaper's Phase 1 +
AD-4/AD-5 fixes found the design's approved AD-4 safety mechanism was never actually
implemented in the live code, despite AD-4's research doc being merged (PR #70) and the
design doc's Risk table citing it as mitigated:

N-1 (P0): AD-4 approved an atomic `if-shell -F` tmux fencing mechanism for the lease/
generation-token check (to close DV-1: tmux doesn't fence the filesystem lease against a
TOCTOU race). The LIVE code in src/ai_cli/stale_session_reaper.py still performs a plain
snapshot-then-separate-`tmux kill-session` sequence -- the approved atomic fence is absent.
This means the race AD-4 was supposed to close is still open in shipped code.

N-2 (P0): Heartbeat writes verify only the public tmux generation-token option, not lease
ownership. This means the detached heartbeat ticker can continue publishing fresh
heartbeats even after the supervisor process itself has failed/died, which could make a
genuinely-dead session look alive to the staleness evaluator.

N-3 (P1): Test coverage gap -- the "terminal behavior" tests use a pipe instead of exercising
the actual foreground-promotion path; PID-reuse, atomic-race, crash-release, and
update-cycle lease tests are absent.

Audit verdict: NOT SHIP-SAFE, 10/14 in-scope rows passed, rows 8/10/14/16 unchecked.
AD-5 (job-control foreground promotion, F-1 remote-exit fix, F-2 portalocker fix) verified
genuinely implemented and correct.

Practical risk: bounded today -- the reaper's default mode is "observe" (D-4), so nothing is
actually being killed in production yet. But Phase 2 (which would make the reaper
independently scheduled and eventually flip to reap mode) must not proceed until N-1 and N-2
are fixed, per the design's own explicit requirement not to risk a 5th incident of this bug
class.

The audit's own commit failed (sandbox couldn't create the worktree's index.lock), so its
findings were never written into docs/designs/stale-session-reaper.md's Implementation Audit
table -- filing here to make them durable, and a follow-up must both fix N-1/N-2 in code AND
record the audit table.

Worktree: ai-cli-utils/.worktrees/aicli-tdm6-reaudit-e949692e (no commit landed there).
notes:
NEW FINDING (2026-08-29, session ai-cli-1): both attempts to implement N-1 (the atomic
if-shell -F fence) hit blockers before any code was written -- worktree
.worktrees/aicli-tdm6-1-fencing-e949692e is clean, no changes landed.

1. Codex delegation (cx implement, effort high, task bukgj4e78) stopped without changes:
   its sandbox cannot create or connect to any tmux server socket at all (tried an
   isolated -S socket in a temp dir and a -L named socket; both got
   "Operation not permitted"). It correctly refused to ship an unfenced fallback given the
   P0 instruction not to. This matches the original research doc's own "Empirical checks"
   section, which hit the same sandbox restriction for a different reason (scoped-write
   boundary).

2. I then verified locally (unsandboxed) that MY shell CAN create real tmux sockets/sessions
   and run if-shell -F successfully. But before implementing, I checked the mechanism's
   literal spec against this codebase's actual candidate semantics, and found a real gap:

   docs/research/tmux-atomic-session-fencing.md's "Fingerprint and command shape" section
   requires the atomic fingerprint to include pane_dead=1 for every candidate pane (and its
   "Required final protocol" step 3 requires tmux to report every candidate pane dead).
   This codebase's reaper never sets tmux's `remain-on-exit` window option anywhere (grepped
   session_script.py and stale_session_reaper.py -- absent). I empirically confirmed
   (real tmux 3.7c, local shell) that SIGSTOPping a pane's own process leaves tmux reporting
   `pane_dead=0` indefinitely -- tmux only sets pane_dead when its own child actually exits
   AND remain-on-exit is on; a stopped-but-not-exited process (which is what this reaper's
   ProcessProbe/ended_states model actually targets -- see _ended_snapshot in
   stale_session_reaper.py) never trips it.

   Consequence: a literal implementation of the research doc's fingerprint would require
   pane_dead=1 as a precondition that this reaper's real candidates will structurally never
   satisfy, meaning the atomic kill would never fire and reap mode would be silently
   inert -- a correctness gap in the APPROVED mechanism spec itself (D-8 / the research
   doc), not just a missing implementation. This needs a design decision before more
   implementation effort: either (a) the reaper starts setting remain-on-exit on its managed
   panes/windows so pane_dead becomes meaningful, or (b) the fingerprint uses this
   codebase's own probe-based ended-state check instead of tmux's pane_dead, accepting that
   the "compare inside tmux only" purity the research doc argued for is weakened by needing
   an external process-state read as part of the compared fingerprint (which reintroduces a
   TOCTOU window between the probe read and the if-shell -F call, though a much narrower one
   than today's separate-kill-session gap). Recommend routing this through
   /decision-framework as a new sub-decision under D-8 before the next implementation
   attempt.

Practical risk unchanged: reaper defaults to observe mode (D-4), so nothing is being killed
in production. This finding does not increase urgency, but it does mean the next attempt at
N-1 needs a design decision first, not just another implementation pass.

N-2 (heartbeat lease-ownership) and N-3 (test coverage gap) were not attempted this round --
scoped after N-1 in the brief, and N-1 blocked before reaching them.
close_reason: Shipped PR #89 (5b1aaf0): remain-on-exit set+proven, atomic if-shell -F compare-and-kill fence built from argv, N-2 heartbeat lease re-verification. All independently verified via real-tmux tests on this Mac (4/4 passed) plus full suite (2479 passed).

title: Exiting c-r-job-1 CC session on Framework also crashed/exited c-r-kc-1 and c-r-eve-1 sessions
description:
User report (verbatim): "also create a /beads-task and cc task for the bug where i exited the c-r-job-1 cc session and it also crashed / exited the c-r-kc-1 cc session and c-r-eve-1 cc session on framework as well. i thought we fixed this."

This is the same class of bug as AI-CLI-58t (OS-abstract process probe, fixing a silent no-op and a latent crash, merged 2026-08-24, PR #53) and the earlier-filed-this-session P0 (restarting a CC session via ai c -R sometimes kills OTHER unrelated live CC sessions via session reclamation -- root-cause candidate was src/ai_cli/main.py's _reclaim_abandoned_cc_session identity-check false-positive path). Sergei says he thought this was already fixed, but it recurred: exiting job-1 on Framework this time took down BOTH kc-1 and eve-1 simultaneously (multiple unrelated sessions in one event, not just one).

Needs repro-first root-cause on Framework specifically (this instance happened there, not Mac) -- confirm which processes each killed session was running, whether the abandoned-session reclamation/reaper path fired during job-1's exit, and why the identity check matched two other live, unrelated sessions. Check whether AI-CLI-58t's fix (merged 2026-08-24) actually reached and was deployed on the Framework machine, or whether this is a genuinely new/different failure mode post-fix. Cross-reference the earlier-filed P0 for this same symptom (search bd for "kills OTHER unrelated live CC sessions" or "AI-CLI-58t") before starting fresh investigation -- may already have relevant findings.
notes:
Sergei clarified: NOT all sessions crashed -- only kc-1 and eve-1 were affected, other live sessions on Framework were fine at the time. Matches the earlier-filed P0's own note ('didn't take down all of them though like last time') -- non-deterministic/selective, not a blanket kill-everything failure. Strengthens the race-condition/PID-reuse hypothesis over a deterministic logic bug.
NEW INSTANCE (2026-08-28/29, Framework, ai-harness repo): c-r-aih-1, c-r-aih-2, and
p-r-aih-1 all "crashed" together per Sergei's report ("due to mosh exiting or whatever").
Investigated live on Framework (SSH to fw) before assuming this is the same bug class as the
job-1/kc-1/eve-1 incident above:

EVIDENCE GATHERED:
- tmux list-sessions: c-r-aih-1 was created "Thu Aug 27 21:16:22" -- 2 DAYS before this
  incident, UNCHANGED. Same for c-r-aih-2, p-r-aih-1. This is direct proof the underlying tmux
  sessions were NEVER destroyed/recreated -- if the destructive reclaim/reaper mechanism (the
  AI-CLI-58t/AI-CLI-iy53 class) had fired, the session's creation timestamp would reset.
- mosh-server processes for aih-1 and aih-2 are freshly started (~13 min old at time of
  investigation), confirming a RECONNECT happened, not a session recreation.
- systemd-logind (Framework): sessions 480, 483, 484 were all "Removed" within the same second
  (21:44:02), then a burst of short-lived new sessions (523-527) appeared at 21:47:09-21:47:15,
  each logging out immediately after creation -- this is the normal mosh-server bootstrap
  pattern (ssh host mosh-server new ... connects briefly, then disconnects once mosh's UDP
  channel is established). Reads as: 3 persistent connections died together at 21:44:02, then
  reconnected roughly 3 min later.
- Ruled out: no OOM kills in the last 12h (journalctl), 102GiB memory free, no Mac sleep/wake
  event at 21:44 EDT (pmset -g log), Framework's WiFi interface (wlp192s0) is DOWN/unused --
  Framework actually runs on wired ethernet (enp191s0) with Tailscale on top, so the periodic
  WiFi MAC-randomization scan noise in the journal at that time is an unrelated red herring, not
  the cause.
- Could NOT determine the client-side (Mac) mosh/ssh exit reason -- no local mosh-client
  logging captured in macOS unified log, and this background session wasn't the one attached to
  the crashing panes (Sergei's interactive terminal was).

CONCLUSION SO FAR: this instance's symptom shape looks structurally DIFFERENT from the
job-1/kc-1/eve-1 incident and the AI-CLI-58t/iy53 class above -- no evidence of a destructive
kill (tmux session history intact, no process reclaim/false-positive signature found). Current
best-supported hypothesis: a transient network blip broke 3 concurrent mosh/SSH connections from
the SAME client (Mac) to Framework simultaneously, and reconnection happened cleanly afterward
with zero data loss -- i.e. this may be a mosh-resilience / reconnect-UX issue (a benign blip
LOOKING like a crash) rather than a repeat of the destructive-kill bug class. NOT yet confirmed
-- still need the client-side mosh exit code/reason to be sure. Flagging this distinction
explicitly rather than assuming it's the same root cause as the incident above, per Sergei's
own question: "why were they all in the same repo this time but not last time" -- an
all-in-one-client-connection-drop explanation fits that observation (whichever sessions were
open on the Mac's side at that moment get hit together, independent of which repo they're in),
whereas the reclaim/false-positive mechanism is repo-agnostic and matches by process identity,
not by connection origin.
FIXED and SHIPPED 2026-08-28, commit 4a534ff (main). Root cause found via Codex research (cx research --read-only, independently verified against source before acting): session_script.py's generated session script contained a kill block (lines 537-545) that killed ANY mosh-server process on the host whose command line matched this session's own --project-prefix and was older than 60s -- re-run on every session launch AND every child-body restart (self-update, /memory reload, etc). Sibling sessions sharing a project prefix (c-r-aih-1, c-r-aih-2, p-r-aih-1 all use --project-prefix aih) kill each other's mosh-server the next time any one of them restarts. This is a DISTINCT mechanism from the job-1/kc-1/eve-1 incident above (those used different prefixes -- JOB/KC/eve -- so this specific bug can't explain that one; that incident's root cause remains open/unconfirmed). Fix: removed the kill block entirely, matching the established AI-CLI-iy53 pattern (remove kill authority, don't patch scoping) -- the legitimate underlying need (stale mosh-server cleanup) is what AI-CLI-tdm6's out-of-band heartbeat-corroborated reaper redesign already covers safely. New regression test: test_given_generated_session_script_when_rendered_then_it_never_signals_any_mosh_server (RED-before/GREEN-after verified). Full suite: 2477 passed, only the 2 known pre-existing failures (test_process_probe SIGCONT/SIGKILL, test_create_worktree direnv-ordering).
