title: Design revision 5 + fix: AD-5 topology (synchronous foreground child, detached heartbeat ticker) + F-1/F-2
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> AD-5: Is option B the better long-term foundational best practice system design, code design approach? [...discussion, user agreed with recommendation A after pushback...] Okay, let's go with option A. And then what's next? Can we /delegate to /codex to /implement or /auto-flow or whatever the case may be?

## Task details

AD-5 resolution (option A): fix DV-3 from the Phase 1 implementation audit
(docs/audits/stale-session-reaper-implementation-audit.md) by running the agent child
synchronously in the true foreground (no shell backgrounding via the ampersand operator) and
moving ONLY the heartbeat ticker to a detached, non-interactive companion process. This
preserves D-10's one-supervisor-holds-the-lease-for-its-lifetime property while restoring
correct terminal signal/stdin behavior for the interactive child (real probes showed
backgrounded jobs lose process-group SIGINT in both bash and zsh, and Bash additionally
replaces backgrounded stdin with EOF).

Bundled in the same pass (independent of AD-4's outcome, not gated on any open decision):
- F-1 (P1): remote normal child exit terminates the supervisor instead of restarting -- fix so
  ordinary status-0 exits loop for both local and remote sessions; only local-final-exit or
  remote-recovery-complete should break the loop.
- F-2 (P2): supervisor silently inert when the lock utility is unavailable (confirmed absent on
  this supported macOS host) -- provide a cross-platform lock mechanism (portalocker is already
  a project dependency) or explicitly scope supported evidence platforms, with a visible
  reason/status surface.

Held for later (per the audit's own recommendation, after fixes are verified):
- IC-1 (P2): fill the Design Overview stub -- do this only after re-audit confirms the fixes.

Sequence: (1) design doc revision specifying the new topology plus F-1/F-2 fixes, (2)
implementation fix in session_script.py (and any other affected files) matching the revised
design, (3) independent verification (real pytest run, ruff, re-run the bash/zsh signal probes
that found DV-3), (4) ship, (5) re-audit once AD-4's research also lands.
notes: Shipped PR #71 (268970b7). Second dispatch used job-control foreground promotion (tcsetpgrp+SIGCONT after child self-SIGSTOP, interruptible wait restored for the supervisor) -- resolves DV-3 without the first attempt's supervisor-signal-responsiveness regression. Independently verified: read the full diff, ran the target test file 5x (4x 21/21, 1x 20/21 -- one test flaky under parallel load only, filed separately as AI-CLI-mc4b), ran all 5 regression suites (313/313), ruff clean. Design doc updated to match. F-1/F-2 carried forward.

title: 4th occurrence: launching any ai-cli-utils session (ai p -R -m fw this time) kills unrelated live remote CC sessions on Framework
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> So I just launched a Pi session to be on a remote framework machine. i launched it from ai-harness repo root on macos with 'ai p -R -m fw' and then it appears it killed my c-r-aih-1 and c-r-aih-2 cc sessions / tmux processes. why does this keep happening? File a /beads-task for this and a cc task, and then /delegate /codex to identify the root cause and /bug-fix this. We need to make this stop happening. I'm tired of this happening. i just see the output:
> '[mosh is exiting.]'
>
> that's for c-r-aih-2. and this is what i see as output in c-r-aih-1 after it exited:
> sergeiwallace@mba-m3-24-sw ai-harness % ai c 1 -R -m fw
> No VPN -- connecting via mosh...
> [mosh is exiting.]
> (repeats on every reconnect attempt)
>
> Why does this keep happening? We need to make this stop happening.

## Task details

This is the 4TH occurrence of this bug class. History, all investigated by prior sessions:

1. AI-CLI-p2qj (fixed a223fe5) -- stopped cleanup_stale_sessions from killing unrelated live sessions based on stale tmux client-attachment metadata.
2. AI-CLI-58t (fixed via PR #53) -- made the abandoned-CC-session reclamation process probe cross-platform (was Linux-only /proc, silently a no-op on macOS before; introduced psutil-based Process.create_time()/Process.status() checks).
3. AI-CLI-pzjy (fixed 1532f49, THIS SESSION, same day) -- root-caused a THIRD, separate code path: _has_live_tmux_session()/_sweep_orphaned_claude_bg_spares() never recognized remote tmux names (c-r-<name>/g-r-<name>), only c-<name>/g-<name>, so a live remote session's own bg-spare process got misjudged orphaned and killed.
4. THIS occurrence -- happened AFTER AI-CLI-pzjy's fix shipped and was independently verified with a genuine regression test. So the pzjy fix, while real and correctly verified, does NOT fully close this bug class.

## Strongest lead, not yet chased down by any prior fix

AI-CLI-7cyn (fixed 549abe9, ALSO shipped this session, same day as pzjy) reintroduced a DIFFERENT, more powerful reaper inside cleanup_stale_sessions() (src/ai_cli/session.py): it runs 'tmux list-panes -a' GLOBALLY (every tmux session on the machine, not just the one being launched), groups pane PIDs by session name, and for any session where probe.has_ended(pane_pid) returns True for EVERY pane leader PID, it runs 'tmux kill-session -t session_name' unconditionally -- no remote-name-matching involved at all, so pzjy's fix cannot have touched this path. This function is invoked on every session launch (cleanup_stale_sessions(config) is called near the top of the shared _session_command() launcher that ai c/ai g/ai p/ai cx all funnel through -- confirmed cmd_p calls the exact same _session_command("p") as cmd_c).

Hypothesis: probe.has_ended(pane_pid) (src/ai_cli/process_probe.py, from AI-CLI-58t) is returning a FALSE POSITIVE for a live pane-leader PID under some condition reachable when launching a NEW session -- possibly a Framework/Linux-specific edge case (PID reuse, a shell-vs-exec mismatch in session_script.py's launch template where the pane's leader process forks instead of exec'ing into the actual agent process, or a race between the new session's tmux list-panes snapshot and another session's process state).

## What's needed

1. Read ALL prior bug docs and fixes before touching anything: AI-CLI-p2qj, AI-CLI-58t, AI-CLI-pzjy, and AI-CLI-7cyn's actual diff (549abe9, in src/ai_cli/session.py's cleanup_stale_sessions()). Understand why each prior fix did NOT close this class, so the same mistake isn't repeated a 5th time.
2. Prioritize investigating cleanup_stale_sessions()'s probe.has_ended() global-kill loop (549abe9) FIRST -- this is the one path with zero evidence clearing it so far, and it is architecturally the most dangerous (kills ANY session on the machine, not just a specific name-matched one).
3. Specifically check: does session_script.py's launch template exec into the agent process (pi/claude/codex) from the pane's shell, or fork a child? If it forks, the pane's PID-tracked "leader" may legitimately look ended shortly after launch while the real work continues in a child -- exactly the false-positive shape that would explain this bug firing specifically around NEW session launches.
4. Reproduce first if at all possible (a controlled repro is far stronger evidence than reading code) before declaring a fix.
5. Fix the root cause. If the true fix is "cleanup_stale_sessions()'s global kill-session loop is fundamentally unsafe and should never unconditionally kill sessions it didn't just verify are FULLY dead via multiple corroborating signals," say so and propose the safer design rather than patching around one more false-positive case.
6. Write a regression test that ACTUALLY exercises the failure (per the pzjy precedent: revert the fix, confirm a real process/session gets killed; restore, confirm it survives) -- not just a unit test on the diff.
7. Report clearly: what the actual root cause was, why AI-CLI-p2qj/AI-CLI-58t/AI-CLI-pzjy/AI-CLI-7cyn's fixes didn't prevent it, and why this fix is different/robust enough to actually close the class this time.
notes:
UPDATE (same incident, moments later): confirmed BIDIRECTIONAL. After the Pi launch killed c-r-aih-1/c-r-aih-2, Sergei relaunched aih-2 and aih-1 (via ai c -R -m fw), and THAT relaunch immediately killed the just-launched p-r-aih-1 (Pi) session:

sergeiwallace@mba-m3-24-sw ai-harness % ai p -R -m fw
No VPN -- connecting via mosh...
[mosh is exiting.]

This rules out anything Pi-specific or CC-specific: ANY session launch (ai c or ai p) can kill ANY OTHER live session on the same machine, regardless of engine type. This is strong direct confirmation of the global-sweep hypothesis already in this issue's description -- cleanup_stale_sessions()'s tmux list-panes -a loop (549abe9/AI-CLI-7cyn) runs on every launch of every engine and can kill any session on the machine that probe.has_ended() misjudges as dead, not something scoped to the specific session being launched.
close_reason:
Fixed and shipped ed17415 + deployed to both Mac and Framework via ai update (0.8.0.post20260827212615 / 0.8.0.post20260827212631). Root cause: AI-CLI-7cyn (549abe9, shipped hours earlier the same day) reintroduced an unsafe global reaper inside cleanup_stale_sessions() -- listed every tmux pane on the machine, treated a single point-in-time probe.has_ended(pane_pid) result as authority to kill, and ran tmux kill-session on any session where that check said yes. None of the three prior fixes (AI-CLI-p2qj, AI-CLI-58t, AI-CLI-pzjy) touched this path -- confirmed bidirectional and engine-independent this incident (ai p killed live CC sessions; the CC relaunch then killed the just-launched Pi session), which architecturally could only be this global-kill mechanism, not any of the three narrower, name/identity-scoped paths the prior fixes closed.

Fix: cleanup_stale_sessions() no longer reads pane PIDs, imports no process probe, and categorically never calls tmux kill-session during launch cleanup -- removes the unsafe authority entirely rather than tightening the liveness check one more time. Verified independently: reviewed the full diff, confirmed process_probe usage elsewhere (session_adopt.py, main.py's separately-scoped _reclaim_abandoned_cc_session) is untouched and correctly out of scope, reverted only this fix via a scoped stash and confirmed the new regression test fails for real (a live kill-session call actually fires), restored and confirmed it passes, ran the full test suite myself (2576 passed, 13 skipped, only the 2 pre-existing AI-CLI-gqgy/AI-CLI-t4aq failures, unrelated), ruff clean.

title: Exiting/restarting one ai-cli-utils-launched remote CC session still kills OTHER unrelated live remote CC sessions (3rd occurrence)
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

also, when I exited the sw-4 / c-r-sw-4 CC session, there was a launch from my Mac OS onto my
framework machine. When I exited that it also took down job-1 / c-r-job-1 cc session and also
kc-1 / c-r-kc-1 cc session for some reason. So that issue is still happening where if I exit one
remote SSH connected CC session that was launched from the ai-cli-utils repo command, it's taking
down other ones for some reason. So add a /beads-task for that and link it to the other beats
tasks we filed for this and then add a CC task for this and set it to in progress and then
/delegate to /codex to investigate root cause and /bug-fix. and make sure they actually fix it
this time because this keeps persisting, even though we've tried to fix it like two times
already, I think. So there's something still happening. So we need to make sure this is
systematically robustly fixed at the root cause and it doesn't happen anymore. And also surface
to me at the end a summary of what actually is the root cause and why this keeps happening and
what we've done to fix it before and why it didn't work and what we're doing now and make sure
that the /codex agent reviews all the existing bug docs for those and what we tried to do
previously and make sure we understand why it didn't work and we actually address the root cause
this time and fix it systematically and robustly.

## Task details

THIRD reported occurrence of a cross-session kill on session exit/restart, specifically on
REMOTE (SSH, Framework machine) CC sessions launched via 'ai c -R'/remote-machine flow from
ai-cli-utils. Symptom this time: exiting 'c-r-sw-4' (Framework, launched from Mac) also killed
'c-r-job-1' and 'c-r-kc-1' (both also Framework, unrelated sessions).

## Prior related work (read all of this before investigating)

1. **AI-CLI-p2qj** (closed, commits a223fe5 "fix(AI-CLI-p2qj): stop cleanup_stale_sessions from
   killing unrelated live sessions" and ffaa48a "chore(beads): close AI-CLI-p2qj (cross-session
   tmux kill, fix reverified on main)") -- removed a naive tmux-attach-state-based reaper from
   'cleanup_stale_sessions()' in src/ai_cli/session.py that judged staleness purely from tmux's
   own session_attached/session_last_attached metadata, which cannot distinguish "client
   disconnected, process still alive" from "genuinely dead".
2. **AI-CLI-58t / AI-CLI-session-reclamation-linux-only-zusn** (closed, PR #53,
   commit 46dda09 "OS-abstract process probe, fixing a silent no-op and a latent crash") --
   made src/ai_cli/main.py's '_reclaim_abandoned_cc_session'/'_cc_session_is_live' cross-platform
   via 'process_probe.py' (previously Linux-only /proc reads, silently a no-op on macOS/Windows).
   This is a STRONG regression candidate: before this fix, reclamation could never actually kill
   anything on macOS; after it, it is live there (and everywhere), including sending
   SIGKILL/SIGCONT to what it identifies as an abandoned session's process.
3. **This session (2026-08-27) separately rebuilt 'cleanup_stale_sessions()'** (AI-CLI-7cyn,
   commit 549abe9) to use 'process_probe.probe_for().has_ended()' liveness on tmux pane PIDs,
   replacing the AI-CLI-p2qj-era removed logic. This is a DIFFERENT function from
   '_reclaim_abandoned_cc_session' -- confirm whether it's implicated here too, since it also now
   sends 'tmux kill-session' based on liveness classification.

## Current code (src/ai_cli/main.py, read in full before hypothesizing)

'_cc_session_is_live()' walks every '~/.claude/sessions/*.json' record and, for each one
classified "abandoned" by '_cc_record_liveness()', calls '_reclaim_abandoned_cc_session()' ONLY
when 'record.get("sessionId") == transcript.stem' (i.e. this_session -- the docstring explicitly
says "Scoped to the session being resumed: this walk visits every record, so ending someone
else's abandoned process here would turn each launch into a fleet-wide reaper"). On its face this
guard should already prevent cross-session kills. Since it demonstrably does NOT in practice (3rd
occurrence, always on REMOTE/SSH-launched sessions specifically), investigate whether:

- Two distinct live sessions can end up with the SAME sessionId recorded in their own
  '~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json' (a session-ID collision/reuse bug elsewhere -- e.g. '-r'/
  '--continue' regenerating a session without properly invalidating the old record, or a race
  writing multiple pid.json files against the same transcript UUID).
- The REMOTE/SSH launch path (grep for remote-specific session handling in
  src/ai_cli/session_script.py, src/ai_cli/transport.py, and any -R/remote-machine flag handling
  in main.py) runs a DIFFERENT reclamation code path than local launches, possibly without this
  guard, or with a bug in how it resolves 'transcript.stem' on the remote host.
- 'cleanup_stale_sessions()' (the tmux-pane-PID-based reaper, separately touched this session for
  AI-CLI-7cyn) is actually the real culprit for THIS symptom (tmux session names being killed),
  not '_reclaim_abandoned_cc_session' (which kills a CC process, not a tmux session per se) --
  distinguish which mechanism actually fired using real evidence (logs, timing, the exact stderr
  message each path prints) rather than assuming.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause identified with EVIDENCE (not a plausible-sounding theory) for why exiting one
  remote-launched CC session can kill a different, unrelated remote CC session's tmux session
  and/or process.
- A regression test that reproduces the actual mechanism (not just re-testing the already-passing
  this_session guard, which is not what's failing).
- A fix addressing the root cause, not another surface patch -- given this is the 3rd occurrence
  despite two prior "fixes", the fix must explain why AI-CLI-p2qj and AI-CLI-58t's changes did NOT
  fully close this, specifically.
- Full report: what is the root cause, why did the two prior fixes not fully address it, what is
  being done now, and why THIS fix is robust against the same class of bug recurring a 4th time.
notes: Delegated to cx implement --effort high, isolated worktree .worktrees/aicli-pzjy-bugfix-e949692e (branch wt-aicli-pzjy-bugfix-e949692e, fresh off origin/main caf16b2), background task bza1nda96. Brief requires evidence-based root cause (not a theory), explanation of why AI-CLI-p2qj and AI-CLI-58t's fixes didn't fully close this, a regression test for the actual mechanism, and full report.
close_reason: Shipped 1532f49: root cause was a THIRD, previously-untouched code path (_sweep_orphaned_claude_bg_spares/_has_live_tmux_session in session.py). A remote session's Claude state record carries only the plain --name (e.g. sw-4), but its tmux session is named c-r-sw-4; the bg-spare sweep's fallback candidate set only ever tried c-<name>/g-<name>, never c-r-<name>/g-r-<name>, so a live remote session's bg-spare process was misjudged orphaned once past orphan_bg_spare_timeout and got terminated+killed, taking the unrelated session down. AI-CLI-p2qj and AI-CLI-58t both touched different code paths and never exercised this one. Fix: recognize c-r-/g-r- prefixes too. Regression test independently verified to actually reproduce the bug (fails with the fix reverted -- real process gets killed). Full test_session.py: 137 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure. ruff clean.

title: Restarting a CC session (ai c -R) sometimes kills OTHER unrelated live CC sessions via session reclamation
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also, when i exited aih-1 cc session to restart the cc session, it took down a few other cc sessions for some reason like eve-1 and aih-2 cc session. why is that? add a /beads-task and cc task for this bug. it didn't take down all of them though like last time. /delegate to /codex or sonnet to investigate root cause and /bug-fix and set cc task to in progress

## Task details

This is the second occurrence ("like last time") of unrelated live CC sessions being killed when a
different session exits/restarts. Strong root-cause candidate: src/ai_cli/main.py's
_reclaim_abandoned_cc_session (see AI-CLI-58t, closed via PR #53, 'OS-abstract process probe, fixing
a silent no-op and a latent crash', merged 2026-08-24). Before that fix, session reclamation was
Linux-only (/proc-based) and was a SILENT NO-OP on macOS -- it could never actually kill anything
there. After the fix, it now uses psutil cross-platform (Process.create_time()/Process.status()) and
is LIVE on macOS, including sending SIGKILL/SIGCONT to what it identifies as an abandoned session's
process. If the abandoned-session identity check (start-tick/PID comparison) has a false-positive
path -- e.g. misjudging a live sibling session as abandoned, or a race during the exiting session's
own teardown misidentifying a DIFFERENT session's process -- exiting one session could now kill
others where it previously silently could not. This may be a regression introduced by AI-CLI-58t's
own fix rather than a pre-existing bug that finally became reachable.

Needs full repro-first root-cause: confirm which specific process each killed session (eve-1, aih-2)
was running, whether _reclaim_abandoned_cc_session (or the SIGKILL/SIGCONT path) was invoked during
aih-1's exit, and why the identity check matched a live, unrelated session. 'Didn't take down all of
them this time, unlike last time' suggests non-deterministic/race-condition behavior
(timing-dependent PID/start-tick matching), not a deterministic logic bug -- prioritize
race-condition and PID-reuse hypotheses.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce (or explain precisely why it cannot be reproduced deterministically).
- Root-cause the exact code path that killed eve-1/aih-2 during aih-1's exit/restart.
- Fix + regression test that prevents a live, unrelated session from ever being reclaimed.
- Note whether AI-CLI-58t's fix (PR #53) is implicated.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped a223fe5: removed cleanup_stale_sessions()'s cross-session tmux kill-session sweep entirely, which had zero verification the target session belonged to the launching session. Full suite green (2574 passed/13 skipped, 2 known pre-existing failures unrelated), ruff clean. Re-verified this cycle: no kill-session call remains in cleanup_stale_sessions. Follow-up for a proper liveness-based reap tracked separately as AI-CLI-7cyn.

title: ai ws pull silently leaves a worktree mid-rebase (detached HEAD, conflict markers) on a real pull --rebase conflict
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also, can you sync these worktrees as appropriate: [screenshot of VS Code worktree list showing
> ahead/behind counts for aido-1, aih-v6kf9-implement, AIH-provider-transaction-broker-epkw, sw-1..6,
> aih-1, aih-2, aih-i5ina-implement] ... why would they collide? you're the only cc session working
> on this machine. go ahead and do whatever you need to do to get all of them synced between local
> and remote and commit and push back as appropriate.

## Task details

Ran 'ai ws pull --workspace mba-m3-24-sw.code-workspace' (a dry-run first showed a safe plan). The
real run reported success for every worktree, but 3 of them -- ai-harness's aih-2 and
aih-i5ina-implement, ai-core's aih-v6kf9-implement -- were left in an INTERRUPTED REBASE: detached
HEAD, '.git/worktrees/<name>/rebase-merge/' present, and real unresolved conflict markers (UU/AA
files, e.g. aih-i5ina-implement had 23 conflicted files including 'projects-wide-session-config/
CLAUDE.*.md' and 'GEMINI.*.md', aih-v6kf9-implement had 21 including 'pyproject.toml'). These are
other live sessions' (aih-2, and presumably whoever's working aih-v6kf9-implement) active
worktrees -- this could have caused real, hard-to-diagnose confusion or data loss if not caught and
reverted before those sessions next touched their worktrees.

Root cause (confirmed via source read, 'src/ai_cli/workspace.py'): ws_pull's worktree loop calls
'_pull_rebase(wt)' as a bare statement and discards its (rc, output) return value entirely:

    if _is_dirty(wt):
        dirty_wts.append(wt.name)
        total_dirty += 1
    else:
        if not dry_run:
            _pull_rebase(wt)          # return value discarded, no failure handling
        clean_wts.append(wt.name)
        total_pulled += 1

A worktree is only checked for dirtiness BEFORE the pull. Nothing checks whether 'git pull
--rebase' actually succeeded. On a real conflict, 'git pull --rebase' leaves the repo mid-rebase
with a detached HEAD and conflict markers -- and this code still reports the worktree as
successfully pulled (adds it to clean_wts/total_pulled, printed in the normal '+  name1  name2'
success line), with zero indication to the operator that anything went wrong.

Recovery performed manually this session (verified safe): each affected worktree's original
branch ref (wt-aih-2, wt/aih-i5ina-implement, wt/aih-v6kf9-implement) was still 100% intact
(rebase only creates new commits on a detached HEAD; it never advances the branch ref until
success), so 'git rebase --abort' in each fully restored the worktree to its exact pre-pull state
with zero data loss. This is a NEAR MISS, not an actual data-loss incident -- but the tool gave no
warning and would not have prompted anyone to run that recovery if it hadn't been independently
investigated.

Notable: the codebase already has a robust, verified pull-rebase primitive elsewhere
('src/ai_cli/git_repair.py's pull_rebase_autostash()', whose own docstring says "Run 'git pull
--rebase --autostash' and verify what it actually did") that ws_pull's simpler '_pull_rebase' does
not use. Also main.py (~line 2740-2770) has a related existing failure-handling comment
referencing "AIH-443 Shape B: git pull --rebase --autostash exits 0 even when its ... [did not
finish cleanly]" -- suggesting this class of bug has been hit and partially addressed elsewhere in
this exact codebase already, just not in ws_pull's worktree loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worktree whose 'git pull --rebase' hits a real conflict is DETECTED as a failure by ws_pull,
  not silently counted as pulled.
- On that failure, the worktree is left in a SAFE, CLEAN state: reattached to its original branch
  at its original commit, no interrupted rebase, no conflict markers (e.g. via 'git rebase
  --abort' or equivalent, verified).
- ws_pull's printed output clearly reports the failure per-worktree, distinct from the existing
  "dirty, skipped" and "not tracking origin/main" lines, and does not count it in total_pulled.
- Regression test: a worktree whose pull --rebase will genuinely conflict (diverged local +
  diverged origin touching the same content) ends up reattached, clean, on its original commit
  after ws_pull runs against it, with the failure detectable in the function's output/return.
- Full test suite passes (only the 2 known pre-existing AI-CLI-gqgy failures acceptable).

## Design

Investigate reusing git_repair.py's pull_rebase_autostash() (already handles a related
"exits 0 but did not finish cleanly" verification pattern) before writing a new check from
scratch -- see task details above for the exact function/module to read first.
close_reason: Fixed: ws_pull's worktree loop now captures git pull --rebase's return code; on failure it runs git rebase --abort, verifies the worktree is fully restored (original branch reattached, original commit, clean status, no rebase-merge state), and reports it as a distinct failure line excluded from the pulled count (return code now 1 on any failure). Delegated to Codex (cx implement-network); independently re-verified: full suite 2574 passed/13 skipped (only the 2 known pre-existing AI-CLI-gqgy failures, +1 new regression test), ruff clean. Root cause and full incident detail in the issue description -- this was a live near-miss this session (3 other-session worktrees left mid-rebase with detached HEAD, fully recovered manually with zero data loss before this fix shipped).

title: ai sync's conflict-marker detection used a bare substring search and corrupted a real memory file whose prose quoted marker characters
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

Discovered while dogfooding AI-CLI-ezcr (Codex-first memory-merge): running `ai sync resolve` for real against a live conflict corrupted `ai-harness/memory/feedback-inspect-the-beads-mirror-before-staging-it.md` to the literal text "File not found in the working tree: ..." — a Codex response, not real content.

## Task details

Root cause: `apply_pull_files`'s `has_conflict_markers` check and `_resolve_memory_conflict_file`'s classification both used a bare substring search (`"<<<<<<<" in content`), not anchored to line-start. The corrupted file is a memory note ABOUT conflict-marker hygiene, and its own prose/code-example legitimately contains the literal substrings `<<<<<<<` and `>>>>>>>` (e.g. `grep -c '^\(<<<<<<<\|=======\|>>>>>>>\)' .beads/*.jsonl`), so it was misclassified as a genuine conflict, sent to the LLM merge path with a 'resolve these conflict markers' prompt despite having none, and the LLM's non-conforming response (which happened to contain neither marker substring) passed the too-loose 'no markers left' validation and got written over the real content. The same false-positive risk existed on the Gemini-only path before today too — it was just never exercised (always failed to no-API-key, leaving the safe unresolved-conflict fallback) until Codex made merges actually succeed for the first time.

Fixed alongside AI-CLI-ezcr, in the same commit: added `_has_conflict_markers()`/`_leaves_conflict_marker()` using line-anchored regex (real git conflict markers are always written at the start of their own line, e.g. `<<<<<<< HEAD`), replaced all 4 substring-check call sites, and added a guard so `_llm_merge_memory_conflict()` returns content unchanged (skipping the LLM entirely) when it has no genuine markers. Restored the corrupted target file from the (unaffected) staging-repo copy. Regression tests cover: real markers detected correctly, prose-quoted marker characters NOT misclassified (both for input classification and output-rejection), and the no-real-markers short-circuit never invoking either LLM backend.
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit as AI-CLI-ezcr (Codex-first memory-merge): added line-anchored _has_conflict_markers()/_leaves_conflict_marker(), replaced all 4 substring-check call sites, added a no-real-markers short-circuit. Corrupted file restored from the unaffected staging-repo copy. 4 new regression tests, full sync test suite + ruff green.

title: ai-cli-utils project-registry writer omits path field, reproduces SW-890 outage class
description:
Two write sites in src/ai_cli/config.py append [[projects]] stanzas to sergei.toml (or the resolved main-project registry file) with name/task_prefix/type/active but never write path, even though the full project directory path is in scope at both call sites. sergei.toml's own guard comment marks path as REQUIRED alongside name -- a missing path is the exact SW-890 failure class that crashed the ai-core MCP startup and froze the whole memory substrate for months. Found live: ai-harness-lite and nyc-events stanzas in sergei.toml were missing path, hand-fixed in a separate commit (7265d840), but the generator that produced them is still broken and will reproduce this on the next unregistered-project prompt.

Site 1: _append_projects_entry, src/ai_cli/config.py:575-581 -- builds the entry f-string from root (a full Path) and prefix, but never interpolates path = "{root}". Called by _prompt_and_persist_prefix (config.py:630-642), the last tier of resolve_project_prefix (config.py:645), triggered when ai c/session launch needs a task prefix for an unregistered project and prompts interactively. Write target resolves via _registry_write_target (config.py:589-601) -> _get_project_registry_path (config.py:782-789) -> main_dir / f"{name}.toml", i.e. sergei.toml when main_project = sergei.

Site 2: inline in validate_registry_completeness, src/ai_cli/config.py:911-913 -- appends entries via a plain file .write() in a loop, also omitting path even though the scanning loop just above (config.py:872-877) iterates projects_dir.iterdir() and has the directory d (the full path) in scope. Runs from main.py:1761-1767, invoked automatically before an unqualified ai c session launch, prompting per unregistered directory found under projects_dir.

Fix: interpolate path = "{root}" (site 1) and path = "{d}" (site 2, normalized consistently with how other entries in sergei.toml write path, e.g. ~/projects/<name> vs an absolute path -- check existing convention) into both entry-writing f-strings/write calls, so every newly-registered project stanza carries path from the moment it's created.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: _append_projects_entry (config.py:575-581) writes a path field for the new [[projects]] entry, derived from the root argument already in scope. AC-2: the inline entry-writer in validate_registry_completeness (config.py:911-913) writes a path field for each new entry, derived from d already in scope in the loop above. AC-3: the written path value follows the same normalization convention as existing sergei.toml entries (spot-check: does the registry use ~/projects/<name> or an absolute path -- match it, don't introduce a third convention). AC-4: a regression test exists for both write sites asserting the written TOML text/parsed entry contains a non-empty path field. AC-5 (failure-path): a test confirms that if root/d cannot be resolved to a usable path, the function fails loudly (matching the file's own documented behavior of load_config skipping-with-a-loud-error on a missing path) rather than silently writing an empty or malformed path value.
close_reason: Fixed and landed on origin/main at b19ad966. _append_projects_entry (site 1) now normalizes to ~/projects/<name> when under home, else absolute, and raises ProjectPrefixError before writing if the path doesn't resolve; validate_registry_completeness's inline writer (site 2) now threads the scanned Path through instead of only keeping the name string. Verified: 94 focused + full suite 2312 passed / 0 failed in the real environment, ruff clean. Delegated to Codex implement (gpt-5.6-terra, medium effort, session bdupu690z).

title: Private BMS repo names committed into this public package — hygiene guard is red and blocks all pushes
description:
tests/test_public_repo_hygiene.py::test_given_the_shipped_package_and_its_tests_when_scanned_then_no_private_names_remain FAILS on main. The guard (added for BUG-005) is working correctly — real private names are now in the tree:

  src/ai_cli/config.py:480  # (e.g. bms-semantic-knowledge-graph and bms-mdbase-knowledge-agent both -> "bms").
  src/ai_cli/config.py:483  "bms-semantic-knowledge-graph": "kg",
  tests/test_project.py:140,145,148  _get_project_prefix_by_name("bms-semantic-knowledge-graph")
  tests/test_session.py:1288 patch("pathlib.Path.cwd", ... / "bms-semantic-knowledge-graph")

Introduced by 21cd44d 'fix(CORE-121): resolve bms-semantic-knowledge-graph sessions to kg prefix' (authored on another machine/session, arrived here via a fast-forward merge). Two separate violations of the public-package standard in that commit: the private repo names themselves, AND a private tracker id (CORE-121) in a public commit message. The commit message cannot be rewritten now that it is on origin/main; note it and move on.

P0 because it is a pre-push gate failure: it blocks EVERY push to this repo from every machine until fixed, and it is a genuine privacy leak in a package published to PyPI.

FIX DIRECTION (needs a decision, do not guess): the hardcoded name->prefix mapping is the wrong shape for a public package. Options: (a) move the mapping into user config (~/.config/ai-cli-utils/config.toml [[projects]]), which the code already supports per test_project.py's own toml fixture — the hardcoded dict may be redundant; (b) keep a mapping but derive it generically; (c) genericize the test fixtures only, if the src mapping is truly needed. Prefer (a) — 'config over code', and it removes the leak at the root rather than renaming it.

DO NOT bypass the guard or weaken its pattern to make this pass.
close_reason: Fixed in 4268f62: the hardcoded project-name -> task-prefix map moved from src/ai_cli/config.py to a [project_prefixes] table in config.toml (option (a), config-over-code), removing the private repo names from src/ and 4 test call sites. Verified behavior-preserving on this machine with a probe that could have failed: kg/aih/core prefixes all still resolve correctly (via the project registry, which the fallback chain consults after the now-empty override table). title: Fix stranded-autostash: ai update discards a lying exit code and latches the repo behind forever
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: T
comments.text:
Shipped in ai-cli-utils 5cacff5 + cda724f (branch worktree-aih443-shapeb, merged to main).

MECHANISM: `git pull --rebase --autostash` exits 0 when its automatic stash pop conflicts. Measured on git 2.55.0 (macOS) and 2.43.0 (Linux), fast-forward and rebasing pulls alike. Negative control on the same harness: a rebase-BODY conflict exits 1, so the harness can see failure.

CALLERS (ours): main.py _do_update_or_deploy did not bind the code at all (check=False) and its conflict scan only read src/**/*.py — the live conflict was in .gitignore. The ai c N worktree launch gated on returncode != 0, which never fires.

LATCH: once conflicted, later pulls exit 128 and were also discarded. Filed separately as AI-CLI-135.

FIX: pull_rebase_autostash() measures repo state either side of the pull (new unmerged paths, new stash ids, no operation in progress) instead of trusting the exit code.

PROOF: old gate MISSED and new guard CAUGHT the identical genuine conflict; disabling either clause turns the regression tests red; disabling the ai update branch makes it exit 0 and install from the conflicted checkout.

TESTS: 1867 -> 1887 passed, 7 skipped.

Cross-family review by Codex found 6 issues, all real, all fixed in cda724f — including one HIGH where the pre-existing cleanup would have destroyed a user's in-progress conflict resolution, and one HIGH where the bug doc leaked a routable host into a PUBLIC repo.

REMOTE HOST: un-stranded, 0 behind, clean index. All four stashes left INTACT — see AI-CLI-136.

title: DONE 2026-07-20: test suite can no longer leak real tmux/agent sessions
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-117]` **DONE 2026-07-20: test suite can no longer leak real tmux/agent sessions** — Root cause of AI-CLI-116's `c-hm-1`/`g-myproject-1` incident was three local-project launch tests that mocked final `os.execvp` but let earlier `subprocess.run(["tmux", ...])` calls execute. Added explicit subprocess mocks and test-only `pytest-leak-guard-` session names, plus an autouse process guard that loudly rejects unmocked `tmux`, `claude`, `gemini`, or `direnv` calls through `run`, `Popen`, or `execvp`; session teardown removes only names with that test prefix. Eight focused regression tests cover the guard, patch layering, cleanup, and affected launch paths. Driver review (Claude, post-Codex-implementation) initially over-narrowed the `real_tmux` marker's allowance to `subprocess.run` only, which broke the isolated-socket integration suite — `libtmux` uses `subprocess.Popen` internally for every tmux command against that socket. Corrected: `run`/`Popen` both honor the marker (needed for the isolated-socket teardown + libtmux's own calls), `execvp` never does (no test needs a real `execvp("tmux", ...)`, and letting one through would silently replace the pytest worker instead of failing loudly). Verified: full suite 1853 passed, 0 skipped, and `tmux list-sessions` diffed byte-identical before/after the run — the actual acceptance check Codex's own sandbox couldn't perform (no tmux socket access there). Related: AI-CLI-116 (detection/cleanup for the original leaked sessions), AI-CLI-97 (prior subprocess isolation guard pattern).
close_reason: Closed

title: `[AI-CLI-113]`'s worktree-`.envrc` auto-allow never actually fires — `direnv status --json`'s `allowed` field is not a reliable trust signal
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-114]` **`[AI-CLI-113]`'s worktree-`.envrc` auto-allow never actually fires — `direnv status --json`'s `allowed` field is not a reliable trust signal** — Root cause: `state.foundRC.allowed` did not reflect whether direnv could execute the repository `.envrc`, so the root trust guard returned before auto-allowing an identical worktree file. Fixed: probe the worktree with `direnv exec <worktree> true` first and return when already usable; only after a failure probe the root with the same command, then allow only a byte-identical worktree `.envrc`. The generated launcher now recognizes the literal blocked error from that failed `direnv exec` stderr rather than querying status JSON. The targeted-launch registry symptom remains non-reproducible; a `cli()` regression with a real registry TOML and unregistered directory verifies discovery is never called for a named launch. README clarifies the executable-root trust policy. 5 new/updated regression tests; 1837 tests collected, focused session/main suite 183 passed; ruff clean on touched Python files. title: Bug: auto-restart falls back to shell on a blocked worktree `.envrc`, then `ai c` relaunch hangs on an unrelated unregistered-project prompt
description: `[P0]` `[AI-CLI-113]` **Bug: auto-restart falls back to shell on a blocked worktree `.envrc`, then `ai c` relaunch hangs on an unrelated unregistered-project prompt** — Root cause: Git checks a tracked `.envrc` into a new worktree without creating direnv's path-specific approval, while every launch eagerly scanned and interactively synced all projects before resolving a named target. Registry prompts now write atomically and propagate Ctrl-C immediately; `cli()` gained a top-level `KeyboardInterrupt` handler (Click's `standalone_mode=False` doesn't convert a raw Ctrl-C from `input()` into `click.exceptions.Abort` on its own, so without this a stray interrupt printed a Python traceback instead of exiting cleanly). close_reason: Fixed (af4ab41). title: Reaper: restore record-only direct-supervisor SIGINT semantics (DV-3 + N-1) + real terminal/PTY test matrix
description: docs/audits/stale-session-reaper-implementation-audit.md I-03 (Round 3, current, findings-pending-fix). DV-3: the signal-model gate approves an invalid asynchronous-shell topology -- the terminal regression uses a pipe + shared process group instead of a real terminal, and the real-PTY promotion tests explicitly skip Bash. N-1: current code makes a SECOND direct supervisor SIGINT invoke the same child-terminating path as SIGTERM (src/ai_cli/session_script.py:269-299), violating the design's explicit record-only/no-relay contract for direct supervisor SIGINT (docs/designs/stale-session-reaper.md:89) -- history attributes this to commit d348f6e. This is very likely the concrete root cause of AI-CLI-uyev (test_given_agent_exits_on_first_ctrl_c_when_child_restarts_then_second_ctrl_c_exits_session[bash/zsh] both fail with 'supervisor child did not become ready', confirmed reproducing at clean HEAD) -- investigate and fix together, confirming or refuting the hypothesis with real evidence rather than assuming it. Also investigate AI-CLI-wyit (test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed hangs indefinitely) as part of the same signal/topology investigation, since it lives in the same file/feature area (tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py, src/ai_cli/session_script.py) -- may or may not share root cause, confirm either way. Full verification commands and exact recommendations are in the audit doc's N-1/DV-3 finding writeups; read them in full before starting.
notes: Round 2 launched: cx implement (effort xhigh, --sandbox danger-full-access) in .worktrees/ai-cli-qt1e-reaper-signal (continuing on top of Round 1's good uncommitted diff), investigating the real-Claude-session-launch fallthrough + remaining real-tmux test failures. Full sandbox access granted per Sergei's explicit request.
close_reason: Fixed in 2 rounds. Round 1 (already-merged in this issue's base): _supervisor_record_int() made record-only, no longer calls _supervisor_term() on a 2nd direct SIGINT (fixes N-1's design-contract violation). Round 2 (5e0bb80): root-caused and fixed the real finding -- tmux panes inherit env from the long-lived tmux SERVER, not the client that runs 'tmux new-session', so a test's env override was invisible to a pane on an already-running server; this let the supervisor script resolve a real 'claude' binary and launch a REAL, LIVE Claude Code session inside a test's tmux pane instead of the fake test script. Fixed by propagating PATH/XDG_STATE_HOME into every 'tmux new-session -e' call. Also fixed a test-harness self-recursion bug in the tmux PATH shim (uyev's likely root cause). Independently re-verified by the calling session with real tmux access (not a sandboxed self-report): full reaper suite 52/52 passed including both real-tmux delivery-topology tests, plus a clean full-suite run (2571 passed, only the 2 already-filed pre-existing failures).

title: pyproject.toml dev/test deps depend on private git repo (ai-harness fleet-testkit) -- breaks public contributor install
description: tests/test_public_repo_hygiene.py::test_given_the_shipped_package_and_its_tests_when_scanned_then_no_private_names_remain now FAILS at current main HEAD (confirmed via a real, unrestricted full 'uv run pytest -q' run during AI-CLI-fae.14 F-03 verification -- 2556 passed, 14 skipped, 11 failed). Two findings, one already fixed directly (see below), one substantive: pyproject.toml:119 declares 'fleet-testkit = { git = "https://github.com/sergeiwallace/ai-harness.git", rev = ..., subdirectory = "packages/fleet-testkit" }' under both [project.optional-dependencies] (dev extra) and [dependency-groups]. Confirmed live: github.com/sergeiwallace/ai-harness returns HTTP 404 unauthenticated and 'gh api repos/sergeiwallace/ai-harness --jq .private' returns true -- it is a genuinely private repository. Any outside contributor to this public open-source package who runs 'uv sync --all-extras' or installs the dev dependency group hits a git-clone authentication failure for a repo they cannot access. Introduced by commit d08f422 ('chore(AIH-o4uye): onboard fleet-testkit for process-supervised tests (#104)'), which landed AFTER AI-CLI-fae.13/fae's earlier F-09 public-hygiene verification, so it was never caught by the prior 10/10-passing claim -- a genuine regression in the release-readiness posture, not a false positive. Needs a real decision, not a quick patch: options include (a) making fleet-testkit genuinely optional/skip-gracefully-if-unreachable for public contributors, (b) vendoring a minimal public subset of fleet-testkit into this repo, (c) publishing fleet-testkit itself as a public package/PyPI dependency instead of a private git source, or (d) accepting the dev-only-not-runtime scope as an explicit, documented exception (weakest option -- still breaks 'uv sync --all-extras' for outside contributors and is exactly what test_public_repo_hygiene.py is designed to catch). The OTHER hygiene finding from this same test run (docs/audits/stale-session-reaper-implementation-audit.md:974 naming 'aido' in a Commands Run appendix, introduced by this session's own Round 3 cx audit --write-target worker) was fixed directly and mechanically in the same commit that surfaced this issue -- not part of this issue's remaining scope.
close_reason: Fixed via commit e72d373 (option A): fleet-testkit split into its own optional internal-testkit extra/group, no longer part of the default dev extra. Verified: uv sync --extra dev succeeds without private-repo access; test_public_repo_hygiene.py 10/10 pass. Option C (publish fleet-testkit publicly) tracked separately.

title: test_given_agent_exits_on_first_ctrl_c_when_child_restarts_then_second_ctrl_c_exits_session[bash/zsh] fails: supervisor child did not become ready
description: Confirmed reproducing at clean origin/main HEAD 7e4c1d0 (uv run pytest tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py -v --timeout=45): both [bash] and [zsh] parametrizations of this double-Ctrl-C escape regression fail with 'supervisor child did not become ready', not a timeout/hang like the separately-tracked AI-CLI-wyit. Discovered while independently supplying real runtime pytest evidence for docs/audits/stale-session-reaper-implementation-audit.md Round 3 (a Codex cx audit --write-target round found this Mac's own sandbox couldn't run pytest/tmux, but my own direct shell can). Likely the concrete manifestation of that same Round 3's N-1 finding: current code makes a second direct supervisor SIGINT invoke the same child-terminating path as SIGTERM (src/ai_cli/session_script.py:269-299), violating the design's record-only/no-relay contract for direct supervisor SIGINT (docs/designs/stale-session-reaper.md:89). If the test's harness delivers a second SIGINT before the child is fully ready, the supervisor may now be terminating the child instead of restarting it -- worth checking as the first root-cause hypothesis. Full run: 46 passed, 2 skipped, 3 failed (this + the already-tracked AI-CLI-wyit hang).
notes: Being investigated together with the likely-root-cause N-1 finding under AI-CLI-qt1e -- do not fix independently.
close_reason: Fixed as part of AI-CLI-qt1e Round 2 (5e0bb80): the real root cause was tmux server env inheritance -- a stale tmux server ignored the test's env override, so the supervisor's child resolved a real 'claude' binary and never became ready. title: ai c -R remote tmux session: terminal enters raw escape-sequence leak state (extended-keys Ctrl+C + SGR mouse events typed as literal garbage, unrecoverable)
description: Reported live 2026-09-02 on framework machine tmux session c-r-sw-4 (launched via ai c 4 -R). User pressed left-arrow which navigated into Claude Code's agents/tasks panel, then re-entered the main session -- after that, the pane was unusable: arrow-key movement and Ctrl+C presses were being echoed as literal raw escape-sequence text into the input line instead of being interpreted, and Ctrl+C no longer triggered SIGINT/the documented double-Ctrl+C exit mechanism at all. Captured pane content (tmux capture-pane) showed the literal bytes: repeated ^[[27;5;99~ (the CSI-u / modifyOtherKeys extended-keyboard encoding for Ctrl+C -- key code 99='c', modifier 5=Ctrl) instead of a raw 0x03 SIGINT byte, and a long run of ^[[<35;X;YM sequences (SGR mouse-motion reports, CSI < Cb;Cx;CyM format) generated by ordinary arrow-key/cursor movement. This means the terminal was left in an extended-keyboard-protocol + SGR-mouse-tracking input mode that the shell/CC TUI was not consuming -- consistent with a terminal DECSET-mode leak/desync, most plausibly triggered by the agents-panel view transition not cleanly restoring normal terminal input modes on return. Distinct from AI-CLI-wuu2 (double-Ctrl+C escape mechanism, which fires correctly on a raw SIGINT byte reaching the shell trap -- in THIS bug, Ctrl+C never becomes a raw SIGINT byte in the first place). Likely root cause is in the Claude Code CLI's own TUI terminal-mode handling (kitty keyboard protocol / mouse reporting negotiation), not ai-cli-utils' session_script.py -- but ai-cli-utils' session wrapper may have a defensive-fix opportunity (e.g. resetting terminal modes via stty/tput on agent restart or hot-reload) worth investigating regardless of upstream root cause. Session was killed (tmux kill-session) to unblock the user; an orphaned heartbeat-ticker companion process was also found and reaped separately (kill-session does not reap it since it deliberately runs in its own detached session per session_script.py's design).
close_reason: Diagnosed via Codex research (cx research --write-target, effort high, live web search). Root cause is upstream in Claude Code's own TUI: byte-level decode confirms the captured Ctrl+C was xterm modifyOtherKeys encoding (CSI 27;5;99~, not a raw 0x03 byte) and the mouse stream was SGR any-motion reporting -- both leaking as literal prompt text after the left-arrow agents-panel transition. Matches (independently verified by me, both real, both content-matching) upstream anthropics/claude-code#75899 (exact left-arrow-into-agents-panel-then-degraded-return transition, maintainer-reproduced) and #58653 (SGR mouse leak into prompt in the agent view), plus 3 more cited related reports and the public changelog. Code audit of session_script.py confirmed ai-cli-utils sets tmux mouse-on and documents extended-keys (valid, supported features, not the defect) but never calls stty/termios or negotiates these terminal modes itself -- no reproducible local defect to patch, and Iron Gate 5 (never guess a patch against an unreproduced defect) correctly blocks forcing one. No code change made -- documented as diagnosed-upstream with immediate recovery commands, preventive mitigations (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1, tmux copy-mode workaround, version-check), and a diagnostics checklist for any recurrence. Full writeup: docs/bugs/terminal-escape-sequence-leak.md.

title: ai c -R remote sessions: double-Ctrl+C escape mechanism doesn't reliably exit (infinite restart loop or dead pane)
description: Remote tmux CC sessions launched via 'ai c {N} -R' sometimes cannot be exited via the documented double-Ctrl+C escape mechanism (src/ai_cli/session_script.py). Two symptoms observed: (1) infinite restart loop that never exits and never reaches dead-pane state -- reproduced live on framework machine session c-r-eve-1: exit-intent file session-int-exit-c-r-eve-1 already existed from an earlier double-Ctrl+C, but the supervisor kept respawning a fresh child-body process that died during a preflight/direnv step before ever reaching run_agent()'s exit-file check; (2) other sessions exit to a dead pane that can't return to shell -- live artifact found on framework tmux session c-r-aih-test-auto-compact-2 (pane_dead=1), preserved as repro evidence. Distinct from AI-CLI-p7ny, which covers ai-c-r LAUNCH failures, not post-launch exit/escape failures.
notes:
2026-09-02: Independently re-verified the Codex delegation's fix before shipping. Confirmed the diff is genuinely at the correct site (child-body's per-launch while-loop, src/ai_cli/session_script.py:653-658 -- checks $_child_int_exit_file before any preflight/direnv/hot-reload work). Re-ran the new regression test myself: GREEN with the fix, RED (both bash+zsh) with the fix reverted via git stash -- confirmed non-tautological. Ran the wider nearby-test ring (ctrl+c/exit/clean keyword match, 22 tests): 3 failures, all confirmed PRE-EXISTING (not caused by this fix, verified via stash-and-rerun) -- 1 already tracked (AI-CLI-wyit), 2 newly discovered and filed separately as AI-CLI-u0uv. ruff check + format clean on both changed files. Shipped ai-cli-utils@810992d (main), pushed. NOT closing this issue: symptom 1 (infinite restart loop) is fixed and verified; symptom 2 (dead pane) remains unresolved -- Codex could not reach the preserved remote artifact or create an isolated tmux socket in its sandbox, and this session did not attempt further live remote investigation this pass. Next: investigate the dead-pane symptom (c-r-aih-test-auto-compact-2 on framework was left alive specifically for this) as a follow-up.

2026-09-02: Dead-pane follow-up used live remote access. The named session was already absent. Its capture predates clean-supervisor teardown fix 72721a7, which calls tmux kill-session before supervisor exit; remain-on-exit otherwise retains a dead pane. The generated-wrapper preflight Ctrl+C regression passed remotely under bash and zsh. Focused local regressions: 4 passed. The real-tmux clean-exit test still hangs because its test-only tmux PATH wrapper recursively execs itself; this is separately tracked and was not changed. The disposable remote test process group and temporary state were removed.
close_reason: Both reported product symptoms are fixed: persisted exit requests stop preflight work, and clean supervisor exit tears down the tmux session. The dead-pane artifact predates the latter fix; current remote shell-signal coverage passes.

title: test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed hangs indefinitely (pre-existing, reproduces on main)
description: tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py::test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed hangs indefinitely (confirmed via pytest-timeout at 30s, 'Failed: Timeout (>30.0s) from pytest-timeout' inside subprocess.run's selector.select in tests/conftest.py:216 guarded_run). Reproduced on origin/main HEAD d156cbb in a clean throwaway worktree with a fresh venv -- NOT a regression from AI-CLI-fae.13's security fixes. This hang blocks any full, unbounded 'pytest' or 'pytest -n auto' run from ever completing (explains repeated apparent CI/local hangs this cycle -- xdist eventually stalls waiting on the one worker stuck in this test). The test spawns a real tmux session running a generated supervisor.sh (get_engine_script output) and waits for the session to disappear after a clean child exit (exit 77); something in that real subprocess/tmux interaction never satisfies _wait_for_missing_session's poll condition. Root cause not yet investigated -- needs real debugging of the tmux/supervisor exit-detection path, not just a test-side fix. Workaround for now: run the suite with --timeout=<N> (pytest-timeout is already an installed dependency) or -k 'not test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed' to get a usable signal from the rest of the suite.
notes: Being investigated together with the reaper signal-topology work under AI-CLI-qt1e (same file/feature area) -- may or may not share root cause with N-1/uyev, confirming either way as part of that delegation.
close_reason: Fixed as part of AI-CLI-qt1e Round 2 (5e0bb80): the tmux PATH shim executed 'tmux' by unqualified name, re-resolving to itself and recursing forever instead of the real system tmux, causing the reported 30s+ hang. Fixed by resolving the real tmux binary before prepending the shim's own directory to PATH. Independently re-verified with real tmux access: test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed passes cleanly (no hang) in both the full reaper suite (52/52) and full repo suite (2571 passed) runs.
