**Missing on Framework (5 repos, need cloning):** acn-automation, ai-harness-lite, artelier,
aurion, personal-site.

**BLOCKER hit and NOT yet resolved:** `git clone git@github.com:sergeiwallace/<repo>.git`
from Framework failed for all 5 with `Host key verification failed. fatal: Could not read
from remote repository.` — Framework's `~/.ssh/known_hosts` does not have GitHub's host key
trusted yet (or SSH agent/key forwarding isn't set up for this git@github.com identity on that
machine). Needs `ssh-keyscan github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts` (after verifying the fingerprint
against GitHub's published host keys, not blindly) or equivalent SSH config fix on Framework
BEFORE any of the clones can proceed.

## Scope

1. Fix the SSH host-key-verification blocker on Framework for git@github.com.
2. Clone the 5 missing repos into Framework's ~/projects/ (re-check inventory first in case it

3. For job-pilot and sergei specifically (already present as base repos, just missing the

   Framework matching the branch/state the Mac-side worktrees are on, so those two sessions have

   time (explicitly approved by the user, deferred from AI-CLI-l8ha to avoid burning tokens on a
   ~200MB+ transcript load before repos were even in place to make the test meaningful).
5. Report back to the user when ready, per their explicit "lmk when its ready" instruction.
close_reason:
All scope items completed and verified (2026-08-24):

1. SSH host-key blocker: root-caused differently than filed. Framework's
   known_hosts genuinely had zero github.com entries (confirmed), so the
   original clone attempt via git@github.com over SSH did fail on host-key
   verification exactly as reported. Fixed properly: copied the exact
   github.com key lines from this Mac's own already-trusted known_hosts
   (established via real prior use, not blind TOFU) and independently
   cross-verified them byte-for-byte against GitHub's own published keys at
   https://api.github.com/meta (TLS-verified source) before trusting -- all
   three key types matched exactly. Verified after: ssh -T git@github.com
   from Framework now gets past host-key verification (reaches
   Permission-denied-publickey, the expected response with no loaded SSH
   key, not a host-key failure).

   However: the 5 missing repos were actually cloned over HTTPS, matching
   the convention every other repo on Framework already uses (`gh auth
   status` showed Framework already has `gh` authenticated with
   git-operations-protocol=https, working). So the SSH fix, while correct
   and now in place, was not on the critical path for cloning -- worth
   knowing if a future clone attempt on this machine defaults to git@
   URLs instead of https.

2. Cloned all 5 missing repos onto Framework via HTTPS: acn-automation,
   ai-harness-lite, artelier, aurion, personal-site. Framework's
   ~/projects/ now has all 14 repos, matching the Mac inventory exactly
   (re-verified counts on both sides immediately before cloning, in case
   it had changed since filing -- it had not).

3. Created .worktrees/job-1 (job-pilot, branch wt-job-1) and .worktrees/sw-4
   (sergei, branch wt-sw-4) on Framework via git fetch + git worktree add,
   tracking the same branches the Mac-side worktrees are on.

4. Live-tested actual CC session resume for all 4 sessions via
   `claude --resume <uuid> -p "..."` (headless print mode, not just
   structural presence-checking):
   - aih-1, aih-2, sw-4: loaded cleanly and responded as instructed.
   - job-1: loaded its full 118MB transcript and, rather than following the
     trivial test prompt, genuinely continued its real prior in-flight task
     -- correctly self-detected it was now running on the Linux Framework
     machine instead of the original macOS session, reconciled real GitHub
     state (found JOB-20 Phase 0 had shipped via PR #3 while this context
     was paused), made ONE safe local-only merge (bb49e6d, origin/main into
     wt-job-1, clean, no conflicts, verified still unpushed and worktree
     status clean), and correctly stopped short of two things needing the
     user's sudo (installing a C compiler for a numpy build) rather than

Conclusion: CC session migration from Mac to Framework works end-to-end for
all 4 tested sessions. Report given to the user per their "lmk when its

notes:
ROOT-CAUSED + SYSTEMIC FIX SHIPPED (commit 8fe0796, deployed to Mac uv tool +
aido venv + Hetzner uv tool + aido venv via ai update, 2026-08-24).

Root cause (reproduced live via a direct mosh connection test to Framework):
SSH/TCP to framework-26-sw.taile8670b.ts.net:22 is fully reachable, but mosh's
UDP data channel is not -- mosh's own diagnostic ("did not make a successful
connection ... UDP port NNNNN not firewalled") confirmed this, but that
message never reached the user because mosh's alt-screen-buffer restore wipes
it from the terminal right before printing "[mosh is exiting.]", leaving only
that final line visible -- explaining the "no error message" symptom exactly.

Software bug found along the way: _ensure_tailscale_up() in transport.py only
proves the SSH/TCP control path is reachable, not that mosh's separate UDP
data path works. On a host where UDP specifically is blocked, that check
always reports "reachable" and the old code retried mosh unboundedly, each
attempt failing instantly with the diagnosis wiped as above -- effectively a
silent infinite-retry loop with no way for a user to tell what was wrong.

Fix: capped the Tailscale-recovery retry at one attempt; a second consecutive
fast mosh failure now falls back to SSH transport with an actionable message
naming the UDP port range and the firewalld remediation. This is general --
applies to Hetzner, Framework, and any future remote machine, not hardcoded
to this connection. Regression test added (test_transport.py) proving exactly
3 attempts, not infinite, and the diagnostic message content.

REMAINING (not fixed by this change, needs the user's sudo on Framework):
the actual UDP block on Framework itself. Standard Fedora/firewalld plus
Tailscale gotcha -- the tailscale0 interface's ephemeral UDP range
(60000-61000) is very likely not allowed through firewalld's active zone.
Remediation to run on Framework (no passwordless sudo available there):
  sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-interface=tailscale0
  sudo firewall-cmd --reload
(or, narrower: --add-port=60000-61000/udp instead of trusting the whole
interface). Once applied, ai c 1 -R -m fw should connect via mosh directly;
until then, the shipped fix means it will now fall back to SSH automatically
and connect successfully rather than exiting with no session and no
explanation -- so the originally reported symptom (silent failure) is
resolved either way, pending live verification.
close_reason:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE + REAL FIX SHIPPED AND LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-08-24, commit
893fd10, deployed to Mac uv tool + aido venv + Hetzner uv tool + aido venv).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the earlier notes on this issue: the first diagnosis
(mosh's UDP data channel blocked by Framework's firewall, commit 8fe0796) was
WRONG -- a false signal from a broken local test harness. Every one of my
earlier live mosh reproductions ran through a pty with 0x0 window size
(script -q /dev/null with no controlling terminal), which crashes mosh's own
client internally (a std::vector::at() out-of-range exception while parsing
terminal dimensions) BEFORE it gets a real chance to attempt the UDP
handshake -- and that crash happens to print a misleading "did not make a
successful connection" message on its way out. Re-tested with a correctly
sized pty (80x24, via Python's pty module with an explicit TIOCSWINSZ ioctl)
and mosh connects to Framework cleanly on the first try. UDP was never
actually blocked. The two firewall changes made on Framework this session
(opening 60000-61000/udp in the default zone, then correctly assigning
tailscale0 to the trusted zone) are harmless and arguably still good
practice, but neither was the actual fix -- confirmed by re-testing mosh
after each and seeing the identical (fake) failure both times, using the
same flawed test harness. Apologies for the wasted round trip on the user's
end running those firewall commands.

REAL ROOT CAUSE (found by testing the ACTUAL remote_cmd ai-cli constructs,
not just a bare echo, through the corrected pty): ai-cli hardcoded
"zsh -l -c <remote_cmd>" as the interpreter run ON THE REMOTE HOST, in three
places in src/ai_cli/main.py -- the mosh_args remote command, the ssh_args
remote command, and the named-session allocation preflight
(_request_remote_session_allocation). Framework (Fedora) does not have zsh
installed at all -- confirmed directly via SSH (`which zsh` -> not found,
`rpm -q zsh` -> "package zsh is not installed", default login shell is
/usr/bin/bash). mosh-server's own execvp of the literal string "zsh" fails
instantly ("mosh-server: execvp: zsh: No such file or directory"), and
mosh's terminal-restore erases that exact diagnostic before printing
"[mosh is exiting.]" -- which is exactly, precisely what the user saw, with
no visible explanation.

FIX (systemic, per the user's explicit requirement -- works for any remote
machine, not a one-off Framework patch): added _resolve_remote_shell(), which
probes the remote host for its own available login shell (checks zsh first,
then bash, matching the existing SESSION_SHELL_PREFERENCE precedent already
used for local session launches in session_script.py) before constructing
any of the three remote commands, instead of assuming zsh exists everywhere.
The probe command itself is run via SSH's own default-shell dispatch, so it
makes no zsh assumption either. Falls back to "bash" on any probe failure
(unreachable host, timeout) so a genuine connectivity problem still surfaces
through the normal mosh/ssh retry path rather than failing inside the probe
itself. Also added -o ConnectTimeout=10 to the shared preflight SSH args so
neither the probe nor the existing named-session allocation call can hang
indefinitely on an unreachable host.

LIVE VERIFIED end-to-end against the real Framework machine after deploy:
ran an actual `ai c 99 -R -m fw` launch (throwaway test session name,
cleaned up afterward -- tmux session killed, worktree removed). Full success:
mosh connected, isolated worktree created, tmux session started, Claude Code
booted and rendered its full TUI. This is the first fully successful
`-m fw` launch this session -- the original reported symptom is genuinely
fixed, not just worked around.

Test coverage: 7 new tests in test_remote.py (TestResolveRemoteShell unit
tests covering found-shell/bash-fallback/probe-failure/non-string-stdout
cases, plus end-to-end tests for both the ssh_args and mosh_args
construction paths using a probed non-zsh shell). Full suite: 2559 passing
(up from 2552), same 2 known pre-existing xdist-only flakes as always
(AI-CLI-t4aq, AI-CLI-660i), ruff clean.

title: Worktree .envrc auto-approval not taking effect: launcher still nags for direnv allow
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> also, can you check out why ai-cli-utils and when i launch cc sessions (on both windows and linux) is always houding me about running direnv allow for the worktrees? why isn't that all automated. that should all be automonomously handled by the ai-cli-utils and launch process for `ai c` cc sessions.

## Symptom

Launching a session via the ai launcher repeatedly prompts the user to run direnv allow for the session worktree, on both Windows and Linux. The user expects the launcher to handle worktree .envrc approval autonomously, since it created the worktree itself.

## Why this is a real defect, not missing functionality

Automation for this ALREADY EXISTS and is not working. src/ai_cli/session.py has a helper that approves a worktree .envrc only when it byte-for-byte matches an already-approved repository-root .envrc. So the intended behaviour is exactly what the user expects. The bug is that this path is not taking effect in practice.

Candidate root causes to investigate, in order:

1. The byte-equality precondition fails. Git materialises the worktree's tracked .envrc during checkout, but this repo's .envrc is not static: it writes files into the direnv layout dir and calls PATH_add. If anything rewrites or normalises the file (line endings on Windows especially - CRLF versus LF via core.autocrlf or .gitattributes) the byte comparison fails and approval is silently skipped. On Windows this is the single most likely cause.
2. The root .envrc is itself not approved, so there is no approved source to copy trust from. The helper deliberately refuses in that case.
3. The probe used to decide "is the root trusted" shells out to direnv, and if direnv is missing or errors the helper returns early and silently does nothing.
4. Ordering: approval may run after the point at which the warning is emitted, so the warning fires even when approval later succeeds.
5. The approval is applied to a different path than the one direnv later evaluates (worktree root versus the directory the agent actually starts in), so direnv still considers the evaluated .envrc unapproved.

Note this is distinct from the already-fixed warning bug: that one suppressed a misleading hint when direnv is not installed at all. Here direnv IS installed and the .envrc genuinely is unapproved.

## Requirements for the fix

- The launcher must approve a worktree .envrc autonomously whenever it can establish trust, with no user action, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Keep the security property: never auto-approve content that differs from an already-trusted .envrc. Approving arbitrary unreviewed shell would be worse than the nagging.
- If the byte comparison is the blocker, compare in a line-ending-insensitive way (or normalise) rather than dropping the equality check entirely - the check is the security boundary.
- Never fatal: a failure to approve degrades to a session without the project environment, never a failed launch.
- Regression test proving approval happens for a byte-identical worktree .envrc, and does NOT happen when the content differs.

## Related

- AI-CLI-112 (AI-CLI-8kd) P1 - launcher does not activate direnv before starting the agent; same launch path and same subsystem, likely wants fixing together
- AI-CLI-ai-c-direnv-jsqn - the closed warning-suppression bug, adjacent but different
- AI-CLI-ai-cli-utils-abvz - OS-agnostic umbrella

title: Stray characters typed into the CC prompt box at session launch (terminal query replies leaking to stdin)
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> we sitll need to figure out these issues with all these characters being entered into the claude code cli prompt box all the time, especially when i launch cc sessions. it happens on both linux and windows now but particularly is a problem on my acn-windows machine for some reason. the machine we're on right now. it seems to die down after awhile but its constantly random character bullshit entering the cc session prompt box at launch and causes so many issues and is horrible UI/UX for cc sessions. idk if its related to ai-cli-utils and how we launch cc sessions or if its something we need to fix in ai-harness and have as a part of the ai-harness install script or something. whatever we need. but we nee to fix it and make sure the fix is robust and OS-agnostic as possible / recommended.

## Symptom

On launching a Claude Code session via the ai launcher, stray characters appear typed into the CC prompt input box without the user typing them. Reported on BOTH Linux and Windows, notably worse on the Windows host (Git Bash / mintty). It "dies down after a while", i.e. it is concentrated at launch and then stops.

## Leading hypothesis to test first: terminal query replies landing in stdin

The launcher emits terminal escape sequences at launch time to set the iTerm2 profile, colour and title. Any escape sequence that is a QUERY rather than a pure SET causes the terminal to write its ANSWER to the terminal's input stream. Whatever process is reading stdin at that moment (Claude Code) reads that answer as typed keystrokes. Classic offenders:

- Device Status Report / cursor position request (ESC [ 6 n), whose reply is ESC [ row ; col R
- OSC colour/profile queries (OSC 4, OSC 10-19, OSC 1337 variants) which reply with the current value
- Any OSC sent to a terminal that does not implement it, where the terminator is mis-parsed and the remainder leaks as literal text

"Dies down after a while" fits this exactly: the launch-time burst of sequences produces a burst of replies, then nothing more is emitted so nothing more leaks.

Specific code to examine, in priority order:

1. src/ai_cli/iterm2.py - the profile/colour/title emission. Note one function already guards with a darwin plus tty check, but the launch-time emitter may not be equally guarded, which would mean iTerm2-specific sequences are being written to mintty and gnome-terminal.
2. The call site in src/ai_cli/main.py that emits the profile setup before tmux takes over the pane.
3. src/ai_cli/session_script.py - the generated launch script, for any sequence written to the terminal before or while the agent starts.
4. Any status-line or hook output that writes to the terminal rather than to a file.

## Other candidates if the above is not the whole story

- Bracketed-paste mode left enabled or disabled asymmetrically around the launch.
- tmux passthrough (DCS tmux; ...) being emitted when not inside tmux, or vice versa.
- A background writer (update checker, notifier, quota scrape) writing to the shared tty instead of a pipe.
- On Windows specifically: mintty versus conhost differences in OSC terminator handling (BEL versus ST).

## Requirements for the fix

- Robust and OS-agnostic. Detect terminal capability rather than assuming; never emit an iTerm2-only sequence to a terminal that is not iTerm2.
- Emit no query-type sequence at launch at all if the reply cannot be consumed safely; prefer pure SET sequences.
- Must not regress the iTerm2 profile/colour/title feature on macOS where it does work.
- Prove it with a test that asserts what is written to a non-iTerm2 terminal is empty, or contains no query sequences.

## Related

- AI-CLI-ai-cli-utils-abvz - the OS-agnostic umbrella task
- AI-CLI-112 (AI-CLI-8kd) - launcher direnv activation, same launch path

title: ai: command not found — the auto-update's uv tool install deletes the entry point, so a fresh shell cannot resolve ai at all during a ~47s window
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> why am i getting this error when i try to launch this cc session from ai-harness repo?
> ```
> agemaker-user@default:~/user-default-efs/projects/bms-semantic-knowledge-graph$ cd ../ai-harness/
> sagemaker-user@default:~/user-default-efs/projects/ai-harness$ ai c 4
> bash: ai: command not found
> sagemaker-user@default:~/user-default-efs/projects/ai-harness$
> ```
>
> add a /beads-task and cc task for this and set to in progress and then investigate root cause and /bug-fix

## Task details

NOT a PATH problem and NOT the stale machine-profile claim that ai is unavailable here. The binary
and the PATH entry are both correct; the entry point was TEMPORARILY ABSENT because ai was
reinstalling itself.

## ROOT CAUSE

main.py:2000-2002 already documents the mechanism, for a different victim:

    uv tool install --force REPLACES the tool environment: it deletes the
    existing one and rebuilds it.

The delete-then-rebuild is not atomic, and ~/.local/bin/ai is a uv-managed symlink into that
environment. So for the whole rebuild there is no resolvable ai on PATH, and a brand-new shell
invoking it fails at the SHELL level, before one line of our Python runs.

## MEASURED WINDOW, 2026-08-21 (filesystem timestamps, nanosecond precision)

    23:17:14.952  ~/.local/state/ai-cli-utils/last_update_commit.txt written (commit ea6ce16)
    23:18:01.121  the tool venv rebuilt (pyvenv.cfg, lib/, activate scripts)
    23:18:01.541  the ai entry point re-created

That is a ~47 SECOND window in which ai does not exist. The user's launch landed inside it.
Corroborating: sibling uv tools (aido, copier, ai-core) still carry July mtimes, so this was not a
$HOME wipe - only ai-cli-utils was rewritten.

## WHY THIS IS A THIRD ACTOR, NOT A DUPLICATE OF AI-CLI-7czi

That issue's family is about a process whose files are replaced underneath it. Three distinct
actors exist and only two are fixed:

  1. the lock WINNER            fixed by AI-CLI-an5r - re-execs after installing
  2. the lock LOSER             fixed by AI-CLI-7czi - waits for the peer, then re-execs
  3. a FRESH INVOCATION from a new shell during the teardown window   NOT FIXED - this issue

Actor 3 is categorically different: actors 1 and 2 are already-running Python that can be taught to
wait. Actor 3 never starts. execvp fails in bash. No Python-level guard, no deferred-import
tolerance, and no lockfile can help, because nothing of ours is reachable to consult them. The fix
must live at the command-resolution layer or in the install's atomicity.

## SECOND DEFECT VISIBLE IN THE SAME TIMELINE

The stamp is written at 23:17:14 but the install does not finish until 23:18:01 - the stamp leads
the completion by 47s. main.py:956 claims the opposite in a comment: that the stamp "is written only
once the install has actually succeeded, below". Either the comment is wrong or a second write site
(the ai update path around main.py:2065) writes it early. A stamp that leads completion makes a
concurrent peer's freshness check pass while the tree is still half-written, which is exactly the
condition AI-CLI-7czi's bounded wait tries to detect. Needs resolving as part of this, or split out.

## CANDIDATE FIXES

(a) A NON-UV-MANAGED SHIM at ~/.local/bin/ai that resolves the real entry point and, when it is
    absent, waits briefly and retries. Works precisely because it is not the thing being replaced.
    Cost: the shim must never itself be clobbered by uv tool install, so install.sh has to own it,
    and there is now a second thing that can drift.
(b) ATOMIC SWAP - install into a versioned directory and repoint a symlink with rename(2). Correct
    and window-free, but uv tool install does not offer this, so it means not using uv tool install
    for self-update.
(c) Do not self-update at launch at all; move it to an explicit ai update. Removes the class
    outright, at the cost of the auto-freshness the launcher exists to provide.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), because it is the only one that also protects against every FUTURE cause of a
missing entry point, and because the window is inherent to uv tool install rather than to our call.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 WHEN the ai entry point is absent because a concurrent self-update is mid-rebuild, THEN
     invoking ai SHALL still launch, rather than failing with command not found.
AC-2 THE FIX SHALL be verified by a test that actually removes the entry point for the duration of
     an invocation, not by asserting on a mocked absence - the defect lives at process-exec level.
AC-3 WHEN the entry point is absent for a reason that is NOT a transient rebuild (uninstalled, a
     genuinely broken install), THEN the failure SHALL be reported clearly and SHALL NOT hang or
     retry forever (failure-path AC).
AC-4 Resolve the stamp-leads-completion discrepancy above, or split it out with evidence, and state
     which of the two write sites is responsible.
AC-5 THE MEASURED WINDOW SHALL be re-measured after the fix and recorded, so the improvement is a
     number rather than a claim.
notes:
ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-08-21. Two corrections to the filing above, then the mechanism.

## CORRECTION 1 - the "~47 second window" is NOT the outage duration

The filing read the interval from the update stamp (23:17:14.95) to the restored entry point
(23:18:01.54) as one actor's outage. It is not: it spans TWO actors. A safe self-update wrote the
stamp at 23:17:14, and the fleet installer's destructive reinstall ran 47s later. The outage is
however long that reinstall takes, which is much shorter. The 47s figure should not be quoted.

## CORRECTION 2 - ai's OWN updater was never the destructive one

The filing assumed the destructive uv tool install --force branch had run because
_running_uv_tool_venv() returned None. It does not return None here - verified by running the real
predicate from the installed interpreter, which returns the tool venv (sys.prefix is the venv,
sys.base_prefix is /opt/conda, and uv-receipt.toml is present). Self-update takes the SAFE
uv pip install --python path. The destructive command came from ai-harness install.sh:1988
(_ensure_editable_uv_tool), a different repository.

## THE ACTUAL MECHANISM - a two-owner loop, not a race

  1. self-update runs uv pip install <project> into the live venv, WITHOUT -e. A plain install over
     an editable one replaces it: the editable marker goes, a copied tree appears.
  2. install.sh looks for that marker to decide whether the tool is still coupled to its source.
     Not finding it, it repairs with uv tool install --force --editable.
  3. that repair DELETES AND REBUILDS the whole tool environment, and the ai entry point is inside
     it. For the rebuild there is no resolvable ai on PATH.
  4. the repair restores the marker; the next self-update removes it again. Forever.

So this is not a rare race. It is a scheduled outage, once per installer run, for as long as the two
owners disagree. That is why it looked random: it depends on which owner ran more recently.

Corroborating observation: the live environment was seen in BOTH states within one day - a copied
snapshot earlier (recorded in AI-CLI-7czi's own notes as "only an editable .pth", i.e. the other
phase), and editable immediately after the installer run. The loop is directly observed, not inferred.

## EVIDENCE - reproduced against real uv, in isolation

Scratch venv, throwaway package: editable install leaves _editable_impl_probepkg.pth and no package
directory; a plain install over it removes the marker and materialises probepkg/. Zero risk to the
live install. Two integration tests now pin this against real uv, so if uv ever stops doing it the
fix is flagged as unnecessary rather than silently rotting.

## THE FIX - shipped, ai-cli-utils

Self-update installs editably when the environment holds or records an editable install, so the
marker survives, install.sh sees nothing to repair, and the destructive branch is never reached.
_install_is_editable consults the site-packages marker (ground truth about the current state) and
uv-receipt.toml (original intent, and NOT rewritten by uv pip install, so it still reads editable
after a plain install clobbered the marker). Either being true means install editably, which makes
the fix self-healing from the already-copied state rather than only preventing the next transition.

A ONE-SIDED FIX IS SUFFICIENT, which is the good news: nothing in ai-harness needs to change, because
install.sh only reinstalls when the marker is missing. Keeping the marker present removes its trigger.
That matters because ai-harness cannot currently accept a commit at all (AIH-77bdg).

AC-1 met - the entry point is no longer removed, so there is nothing to survive.
AC-2 met - the real-uv tests exercise actual install behaviour, not a mocked absence.
AC-3 unchanged and still correct: a genuinely broken install is not silently retried.
AC-4 answered by CORRECTION 1 - the stamp does not lead completion; two actors were conflated.
AC-5 superseded - there is no window left to re-measure, because the destructive step is not reached.
Every mechanism sabotage-verified; suite green apart from two PRE-EXISTING failures fixed in their
own atomic commits (a stale session-adopt guard test, and the ruff pin drift from the renovate bump).

title: ai session-adopt cannot adopt a transcript ai session-audit reports as adoptable (slug mismatch)
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> can you create a /beads-task and cc task and set to in progerss to migrate my acn-1 cc session to be adopted by ai-cli-utils so i can launch `ai c 1` from acn-automation repo root and it launches and resumes the existing conversation. same for acn-2, acn-3, and acn-4. we have an ai-cli-utils command that does this but i tried it and couldn't get it to work so if you have any issues getting it to work on windows or in general, then create a bug /beads-task and cc task and link it to the other beads task and then /delegate to opus to /bug-fix it.

## Task details

Blocks/relates to AI-CLI-1ku (AI-CLI-adopt-acn-automation-cc-sessions-hvqd) — this is the
defect that made that task fail by hand.

### Summary

`ai session-audit` locates a transcript by scanning **every** CC project directory and reports
it as `Adoptable`. `ai session-adopt` then re-derives the transcript's location from the
transcript's **recorded cwd** instead of from the directory the file actually sits in, so
whenever those two disagree — the very condition the audit itself prints as `slug-mismatch` —
adoption fails with "no transcript titled X ... nothing to adopt". The audit promises an
adoption the adopter cannot perform.

### Root cause (located, not guessed)

`src/ai_cli/session_audit.py::adopt_ready` (line ~373) passes `source_root=Path(record.cwd)`.
`SessionRecord` already carries `project_dir` — the real physical location — and the class
docstring explicitly warns that recorded cwd is unreliable for residency decisions
(`slug_matches` is kept "as information only"). `adopt_session` then computes
`source_dir = cc_project_dir(source_root, home)` and `find_transcript(source_dir, title)`
returns `None`.

`triage` clears such a record as ready without checking that `record.project_dir` equals
`cc_project_dir(record.cwd)`, which is why the failure surfaces only at adoption time.

### Minimal reproduction (verified 2026-08-20, Windows/acn-windows, ai 0.7.0)

Fixture: a git repo `myproject`; one transcript titled `myproject-1` written into the project
dir slugified from `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/old-thing`, while its only recorded `cwd` is the
repo root.

```text
audit: title='myproject-1'
       physical_dir=C--...-myproject--claude-worktrees-old-thing
       recorded_cwd=C:\...\myproject   slug_matches=False   in_slot=False
triage ready: ['myproject-1'] | skipped: []
ADOPT -> AdoptionError : no transcript titled 'myproject-1' in
         C:\...\claude_home\projects\C--...-myproject - nothing to adopt
         (check the title with `ai cc-migrate --dry-run`, or pass -s/--source)
```

Real-world instance: the `acn-2` session (24.9 MB) physically lived in
`C--Users-<user>-Projects-acn-automation--claude-worktrees-short-courses` with recorded cwd =
repo root. `ai session-audit` listed it as `Adoptable`, but adopting it required hand-passing
`-s <repo>/.claude/worktrees/short-courses` — a directory that **no longer exists on disk**,
so the value is unguessable from the filesystem and only obtainable by reverse-engineering the
project-dir slug.

### Expected behaviour

1. Anything `ai session-audit` reports as `Adoptable` must actually adopt, with no
   hand-supplied `-s`.
2. `adopt_ready` should pass the transcript's known physical location, not its recorded cwd.
3. `ai session-adopt` should accept the transcript directly (`-t` / `--transcript`, both forms
   per the repo's CLI convention) so a user who has the path from the audit can use it.
4. If a case genuinely cannot be adopted, `triage` must classify it as skipped with the reason,
   not as adoptable.

### Also observed in the same workflow (file separately if they are distinct fixes)

- **Malformed generated title.** The 203 MB acn session was titled `-acn-1-1` — a leading dash
  and a doubled index — so `ai c 1` (which looks up the exact title `acn-1`) could never resume
  it. Adoption needed `-c retitle -T acn-1`. Whatever produced that ai_name should not be able
  to emit a leading-dash or double-indexed title; `build_session_name` should reject/normalise
  it. A leading-dash title is also unusable on the CLI without `--` plus options-before-name
  ordering.
- **False-positive post-adopt warning.** The retitle path warns "title '-acn-1-1' no longer
  resolves in .worktrees/-acn-1-1 - the transcript that kept the original title may live
  elsewhere; verify it by hand" even when there was no collision and no other transcript ever
  claimed the old title. In the no-collision retitle case the old title is *expected* not to
  resolve, so the check should be conditional on a collision having been resolved.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A regression test freezes the reproduction above: an audit-reported-adoptable,
   slug-mismatched transcript adopts successfully with no `-s`.
2. `ai session-adopt` gains `-t` / `--transcript` (both forms).
3. `triage` never reports a record as adoptable when adoption would raise "nothing to adopt".
4. Full gate passes: `ruff check src/ tests/ && ruff format --check src/ tests/ && pytest`.

title: Adopt acn-automation CC sessions into ai c slots
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> can you create a /beads-task and cc task and set to in progerss to migrate my acn-1 cc session to be adopted by ai-cli-utils so i can launch `ai c 1` from acn-automation repo root and it launches and resumes the existing conversation. same for acn-2, acn-3, and acn-4. we have an ai-cli-utils command that does this but i tried it and couldn't get it to work so if you have any issues getting it to work on windows or in general, then create a bug /beads-task and cc task and link it to the other beads task and then /delegate to opus to /bug-fix it.

## Task details

Adopt the existing Claude Code sessions rooted at the `acn-automation` repo root into `ai c`
session slots, so that `ai c 1` and `ai c 2` from the repo root resume the existing
conversations instead of starting new ones.

Survey findings (`ai session-audit` from the repo root, 2026-08-20):

- Only TWO acn sessions exist, not four.
  - 203.14 MB / 52,467 lines, titled `-acn-1-1` (a malformed title), in project dir

title: ai c tmux session naming: index doesn't start at 1, doesn't match CC session custom title
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> first /load-task-panel and then add a /beads-task and cc task and set it to in progress and then /delegate to /codex to /bug-fix the ai-cli-utils cc session tmux process naming convention to start from index = 1. and then index should always match the cc session custom title. right now, i have aih-fw-1 cc session with tmux process name c-aih-fw-0 and cc session ai-cli-fw-1 with tmux process name is just c-ai-cli-0. so not only does the latter have 0 index when custom title has index = 1 but also its missing `fw` for some reason. I launched both from their respective repo roots with command `ai c fw`. so we need to identify root cause and /bug-fix with /delegate /codex so that tmux process naming convention indexes are fixed and aligned with cc session custom title and also fix whatever is happening with ai-cli cc session that's causing it to miss a a part of the name i specified. it should be c-ai-cli-fw-1. and we need to make sure it fixes it for all cc sessions regardless of repo or what repo root the cc session (or gemini etc) is launched from.

## Task details

Two distinct defects observed in live session naming, both in the tmux-process-name vs.
CC-session-custom-title alignment path:

1. **Index base mismatch.** `ai c fw` from the ai-harness repo root produced CC session
   custom title `aih-fw-1` but tmux process name `c-aih-fw-0` — the tmux index is 0-based
   while the custom title's index is 1-based. They must always match: same index, starting
   from 1.
2. **Name-segment drop.** `ai c fw` from the ai-cli-utils repo root produced CC session
   custom title `ai-cli-fw-1` but tmux process name `c-ai-cli-0` — missing the `fw` segment
   entirely (as well as showing the same 0-vs-1 index mismatch from defect 1). Expected tmux
   process name: `c-ai-cli-fw-1`.

Root-cause both defects in the session/tmux naming path (likely `src/ai_cli/session.py` and/or
wherever the tmux session name string is constructed separately from the CC custom-title
string), fix so tmux process names and CC/Gemini session custom titles always derive from the
same index (1-based) and the same full name components, and verify the fix holds regardless of
which repo the session is launched from and regardless of agent (`ai c` / `ai g`).
close_reason:
Fixed. Root cause: iterm2.py::_configure_tmux_for_iterm2() unconditionally disables tmux automatic-rename for every session, but only iTerm2-detected terminals got a compensating custom title/rename. Non-iTerm2 terminals (Warp, confirmed via user's live report) render tmux's own native status line, which was left showing tmux's frozen default window name ("tmux") and its own 0-based window index -- unrelated to ai-cli-utils' session naming, which was already correct.

Fix (delegated to Codex implement-network/medium, root cause already established; independently re-verified): added _rename_tmux_window() calling `tmux rename-window -t <session_id> <ai_name>` after session creation and after re-attach, for every terminal. Regression tests assert the exact tmux subprocess call on both launch paths (tests/test_iterm2.py, tests/test_cli.py).

Verification: focused tests 266 (265 pre-existing-unrelated pass + 1 pre-existing-unrelated fail, confirmed identical on unfixed code via git stash); full suite 2350 passed / 16 failed (same 16-failure baseline class -- config/prefix-registry/session-audit flaky-under-xdist tests -- confirmed via git stash on unfixed code, none touch iterm2/tmux window naming); ruff clean on all changed files; full-repo ruff (11 errors) and format (12 files) counts match the pre-existing baseline measured earlier this session, unrelated to this change.

Shipped: commit 427efb0 on origin/main, content-verified. Bug doc updated in place: docs/bugs/tmux-session-name-divergence.md.

title: ai c session naming appends redundant -N suffix when user index is already numeric
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> can you create a /beads-task and cc task and set it to in progress to /bug-fix the ai-cli-utils cc session custom title / tmux process / worktree naming system so that when i provide an index myself, it doesn't auto-append one. for example, i ran `ai c fw-1` from the ai-harness repo root and instead of it create a cc session / tmux process names aih-fw-1 / c-aih-fw-1 it created aih-fw-1-1. it should recognize if the last hyphen separated characters are already a numeric index and if so, it should not add another -N at the end. so /bug-fix this. /delegate to /codex to /bug-fix it

## Task details

'ai c' session/tmux/worktree naming logic auto-appends a numeric -N index suffix even when the
user-supplied title/index already ends in a numeric segment.

Repro: running 'ai c fw-1' from the ai-harness repo root should produce CC session name 'aih-fw-1'
and tmux process name 'c-aih-fw-1', but instead produces 'aih-fw-1-1' (double-indexed).

Expected fix: the naming logic should check whether the last hyphen-separated segment of the
user-provided title/index is already numeric, and if so, skip appending another -N suffix.

Scope: ai-cli-utils repo, the session naming code path used by 'ai c' / 'ai g' for CC/Gemini
session titles, tmux process names, and worktree directory names.
close_reason: Fixed: build_session_name() now treats a name whose last hyphen-separated segment is numeric as an explicit slot (reusing an existing matching session/worktree or allocating that exact name), instead of always appending find_next_index(). Fixed + regression-tested by Codex (implement, high effort), verified independently, merged via https://github.com/sergeiwallace/ai-cli-utils/pull/40 (8355bb8). Bug doc: docs/bugs/ai-cli-ai-c-session-naming-appends-jsqz.md

title: ai c loser of the auto-update lock keeps running while a peer reinstalls it, so a deferred import dies with ModuleNotFoundError
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> yeah, it just worked for some reason. why was that? why did it fail at first? we should still treat that as a bug or understand why it resolved. and how to avoid it in future. it may still be a bug when we first launch it or something, idk. idk why `ai c` worked for aih-1 and kg-2 and ai-cli-1 cc sessions but not aih-2 and kg-1 cc sessions. we need to isolate the issue and /bug-fix this discrepency or flakiness or inconsistent behavior. we need to understand the root cause of this

## Task details

NOT FLAKINESS. Fully deterministic, and it needs TWO conditions to coincide. Observed 2026-08-17:
`ai c 2` (from the ai-harness root) and `ai c 1` (from the bms-semantic-knowledge-graph root) both
died with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ai_cli.session_adopt'`, while `ai c` for aih-1,
kg-2 and ai-cli-1 succeeded in the same burst.

CONDITION 1 -- A CONCURRENT `ai c` REPLACES THIS PROCESS'S OWN INSTALLED FILES.
`_auto_update_if_stale` (src/ai_cli/main.py) serializes with an O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile. The WINNER
runs `ai update --force` -> `uv tool install`, which tears down and rewrites the installed tree. The
LOSER hits `except OSError: return False  # Another process already claimed the update` (main.py:607
at 434ddc9). `False` means "no restart needed", so `cmd_c` SKIPS its `os.execvp` re-exec (main.py:2479)
and keeps running -- while the winner is deleting the very directory it imports from.

Measured evidence that the install shape changed mid-run: the reported traceback frames are all
`.../site-packages/ai_cli/main.py` (a COPIED install), but that directory does not exist now -- only
`_editable_impl_ai_cli_utils.pth` pointing at the main tree. `.pth`, dist-info and
`~/.local/state/ai-cli-utils/last_update_commit.txt` are all stamped 16:47, and the stamp holds
434ddc97 -- the commit whose message is "union-resolve the conflicted store merge that blocked
`ai c` auto-update". The long-blocked update finally ran, and succeeding is what broke the peers.
Timing corroborates: the five sessions were launched within 34 seconds (ps etime 02:16..02:50).

CONDITION 2 -- THE SESSION MUST TAKE THE RESUME BRANCH. The failing import is function-local
(main.py:358, inside `_cc_record_liveness`), reached only via `_cc_session_is_live`, which
`_bare_engine_command` calls ONLY when `_find_cc_session_by_title` returns a match (main.py:467-469):

    matched = _find_cc_session_by_title(target_root, ai_name)
    if matched is not None:
        is_live, pid = _cc_session_is_live(matched)   # <- only here does the import run

So aih-2 and kg-1 had a prior transcript titled for that session in the target worktree, took the
branch, and executed the deferred import AFTER the winner's reinstall. aih-1, kg-2 and ai-cli-1 had
no matching prior transcript, so `matched is None`, the import never ran, and they survived the same
reinstall untouched. Neither condition alone explains the split; a pure time-window theory is refuted
by the fact that same-burst siblings succeeded.

WHY IT "JUST WORKED" LATER, AND WHY IT IS STILL ARMED. Nothing healed. `last_update_commit.txt` now
records 434ddc97, so `_auto_update_if_stale` early-returns at main.py:597 and performs no reinstall,
so nothing is deleted mid-flight. THE NEXT ai-cli-utils COMMIT RE-ARMS IT for any concurrently
launched session that has a prior transcript.

RELATIONSHIP TO AI-CLI-an5r (closed, PR #31 / c5b33d04) -- THIS IS THE GAP THAT FIX LEFT, not a
duplicate. That fix made `_auto_update_if_stale` return bool and added the caller's `os.execvp`, so
the process that PERFORMS the update re-execs instead of running stale code. Its diff converted the
loser's bare `return` to `return False` on the same line -- correct for "no update needed", wrong for
"a peer is replacing my files right now". Same function, adjacent line, opposite actor: it closed the
stale-code hole for the WINNER and left the LOSER executing against a directory being deleted.

FIX SHIPPED FOR THE SYMPTOM (this session): the deferred import at main.py:358 is now guarded and
returns "unproven" on ImportError, matching `_cc_record_liveness`'s own documented fail-OPEN contract
("a pid that cannot be verified counts as unproven and does not block a launch"). A torn install now
costs one liveness check instead of the whole command. Frozen RED first, with a positive control so
the guard test cannot pass vacuously.

WHAT THIS ISSUE STILL OWNS -- THE ROOT CAUSE. The loser must not continue in-process while a peer
reinstalls it. Options: (a) bounded wait for the lockfile to clear, re-check the stamp, and re-exec
when it advanced -- terminating, because the re-exec'd process sees the fresh stamp and early-returns
at :597; (b) re-exec unconditionally on lock contention, which needs a loop guard; (c) take a shared
read lock for the whole launch so no peer can reinstall mid-launch. Note the re-exec itself is
briefly unsafe while `uv tool install` rewrites the `ai` entry point, which argues for (a)'s bounded
wait over (b).

BLAST RADIUS BEYOND THIS ONE IMPORT: 37 function-local `from .<module> import ...` statements exist
in main.py. Guarding one is not a fix for the class; only stopping the mid-run reinstall is.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1  WHEN a concurrent `ai c` holds the auto-update lock, THE LOSING PROCESS SHALL NOT continue
      executing deferred imports against its own being-replaced installation.
AC-2  WHERE the loser detects that the stamp advanced while it waited, IT SHALL re-exec so it runs
      the code actually on disk.
AC-3  THE FIX SHALL terminate -- no unbounded re-exec loop -- proven by a test, not by inspection.
AC-4  WHEN no update is in progress, `_auto_update_if_stale` SHALL keep returning False and add no
      measurable latency to a normal launch (failure-path AC: the fix must not tax the common case).
AC-5  A regression test SHALL reproduce the two-condition failure (peer reinstall + resume branch)
      and FAIL when the fix is reverted.
close_reason:
FIXED AND VERIFIED AC-BY-AC. Commits 1e069ec (fix) and 7986ffc (AC-5 repro + CHANGELOG) on
wt-ai-cli-1. Full suite 2350 passed / 8 skipped; ruff check + format clean; public-repo hygiene guard
passes.

AC-1 the loser no longer continues in-process -- main.py:679 replaces `return False` with
     `_await_peer_update(...)`.
AC-2 re-execs when the peer advanced the stamp -- main.py:639-640 returns True, and cmd_c's existing
     os.execvp consumes it.
AC-3 terminates -- bounded deadline at main.py:630, and the re-exec'd process early-returns on the
     fresh stamp before reaching the contention branch, so no exec loop is possible. Proven by
     test_given_peer_holds_lock_indefinitely..., not by inspection.
AC-4 the common case is untouched -- main.py:660 still early-returns when the stamp is current, and
     test_given_stamp_already_current... asserts NO wait occurs by making time.sleep raise.
AC-5 the two-condition failure is reproduced end to end through the real crash path
     (test_given_resume_branch_and_missing_session_adopt_when_bare_command_built_then_still_launches):
     a matching prior transcript drives _bare_engine_command into the resume branch while
     session_adopt is unimportable.

EVERY TEST SABOTAGE-VERIFIED. Reverting the guard fails the two import tests; replacing
_await_peer_update with `return False` fails both contention tests. Positive controls pass throughout,
so none of them can pass vacuously.

TWO GAPS I HAD LEFT AND SERGEI CAUGHT BY ASKING WHETHER THIS WAS FINISHED:
- AC-5 was only half-met. The original two tests pinned each condition SEPARATELY; the acceptance
  criterion asks for the combination, which is the thing that actually broke `ai c`. Composition was
  assumed rather than tested.
- No CHANGELOG entry, despite this repo keeping a Keep-a-Changelog file and the fleet rule being that
  docs ship in the same change as the fix. Added, written for a general audience with no internal ids
  and no mechanism jargon (public package), and specifically explaining that concurrent launches are
  the trigger and why siblings survived -- otherwise a reader experiences it as randomness.

A REPORTING ERROR IN THIS ISSUE'S OWN LIFE, recorded because it nearly became evidence: while
investigating I claimed a fleet-wide grep "returns nothing". It returned ten files. I had backgrounded
the search, read its output file while it was still running, and reported the empty read as a negative
result. That claim was about the ADJACENT secrets issue (AIH-wkjpp) rather than this fix, and is
corrected there, but the failure mode is general: an incomplete run is not a negative finding.

WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT COVER, deliberately: main.py holds 37 function-local `from .<module> import`
statements, and only one is guarded. Guarding one is not a fix for the class -- stopping the mid-run
reinstall (AC-1/AC-2) is what actually protects the other 36. If a future torn-install crash appears
at a different deferred import, that is not a regression of this fix; it is the same root cause
reaching a site the guard does not cover.

This is a live, human-observable UAT step.

title: ai c N sessions not auto-reconnecting Remote Control; /rc command itself currently non-functional
description:
Sergei reports (2026-08-15, sw-6): new CC sessions still are not Remote-Control-connected from his phone, and separately /rc (/remote-control) is currently not working at all when tapped manually mid-session.

Related, already-closed issue: AI-CLI-165 (external_ref AI-CLI-165, closed 2026-08-02) root-caused the auto-reconnect gap as a stale .claude/.ai-cli-growthbook-toggle marker gate on session_script.py's pre-launch DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK override write, fixed by removing the marker predicate (commit 3254431, following an earlier unexplained revert bc056a8 of commit 1167672 that had first made the write unconditional).

Verified this session (2026-08-15): the fix is still intact in src/ai_cli/session_script.py (~line 448-464) -- the DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK pre-launch write is unconditional for engine==c, no marker check, matching the AI-CLI-165 fix. So this is NOT an obvious code reversion of that specific fix. Two live symptoms to chase instead:

1. Auto-reconnect still not happening on fresh 'ai c N' launches per Sergei's live report (separate from this session's own settings.local.json being absent, which is explained by sw-6 being a long-running --continue process across multiple /compact cycles -- the pre-launch write only fires at fresh process launch, so that absence alone is not evidence of a bug for THIS session; the bug is about genuinely fresh launches).
2. /rc / /remote-control itself failing when manually invoked (reported live, 2026-08-15) -- this is a different layer than the pre-launch toggle; could be a Claude Code CLI-side behavior change unrelated to our launcher.

Needs investigation to determine: (a) whether the pre-launch write is actually landing before 'claude' starts on a genuinely fresh ai c N launch (add logging/reproduce live), (b) whether the SessionStart-hook automatic-restore mechanism (rc-pair skill Step 4, aih-352 D-4/D-5) is registering correctly, (c) whether a recent Claude Code CLI release changed Remote Control / GrowthBook / /rc command behavior in a way that breaks this mechanism (separately being researched via a companion research task), or (d) something else. Root-cause via /bug-fix discipline (reproduce, root-cause, regression test if applicable, fix, verify, document) -- do not guess a patch without reproducing first.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and documented for BOTH symptoms (auto-reconnect on fresh launch, and /rc failing manually). If an ai-cli-utils code fix applies, it is made, independently re-verified via live UAT (not just a sandboxed self-report), and a regression test added where testable. If the root cause is a Claude Code CLI product-side change outside this repo's control, that is documented explicitly (what changed, what release) and the bug is closed with a clear statement of what (if anything) our launcher needs to change to compensate, or that no compensating action is possible/needed.
notes:
2026-08-15/16, sw-6 second delegation pass: Codex implement traced the stable-session-template
deployment path and RC pairing/bridge registry state (no fixable ai-cli-utils code defect found;
manual /rc failure remains explained by the inherited DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK gate, unchanged from the
first pass). Shipped via ai-cli-utils PR #29.

2026-08-16, sw-6, post-reboot live UAT (mba-m3-24-sw): reframed the asymmetry as cross-repo, not
cross-session -- aih-1 (ai-harness) auto-reconnected RC at startup with zero taps; sw-1/sw-2/
sw-4/sw-6 (all sergei) all needed a manual /rc tap. Live diagnostics ruled out the simplest
explanations (bridge registry, env vars, settings.local.json, growthbook-toggle marker -- none
differed meaningfully) before delegating a third Codex pass with two candidate leads
(CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS 0-vs-1 by repo, and a template build-version skew).

THIRD DELEGATION PASS -- ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, SHIPPED AND MERGED: ai-cli-utils PR #31
(squash commit c5b33d04, merged 2026-08-16). Actual cause: an auto-update launch race in
_auto_update_if_stale() (src/ai_cli/main.py) -- it wrote the source-commit stamp BEFORE
confirming the child update subprocess succeeded, so a long-lived ai parent process kept
generating session templates from its already-imported (stale) module even though the stamp
claimed current. A freshly-invoked ai process (no stale import) got the correct template --
exactly matching the observed asymmetry (aih-1's deployed template was a same-day rebuild;
sw-*'s was not). CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS was investigated and found unsupported
(no discovered linkage to Remote Control eligibility in the installed client).

Fix: stamp is now written only after a successful update; the session-launch command re-execs
(via os.execvp) through the updated entry point before generating any template. Verified
independently (not just Codex's self-report): full suite re-run clean both before and after
resolving a merge conflict against a concurrent sw-4 PR (#30, same doc file) -- 2335 passed, 2
skipped both times; ruff/markdownlint/aido validate-doc all clean. CI on the PR showed the same
pre-existing, unrelated failures (test_quota.py Popen assertion; Windows-matrix git/tmux/ssh
tests) already failing on main at the same base SHA -- merged via admin bypass after confirming
that, not blind.

STILL OPEN pending live UAT (cannot be self-verified): once this fix is installed and a fresh
session launched for a previously-affected repo, confirm (a) its generated template contains the
DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK override and (b) Remote Control actually auto-reconnects at startup with zero
manual taps. If it still fails while a comparison session succeeds, that indicates a second,
different cause -- report upstream with exact Claude Code version + diagnostics, since the
launcher-side stale-generator path identified here would no longer explain it.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed: auto-update launch race in _auto_update_if_stale (src/ai_cli/main.py), shipped via PR #31 (squash c5b33d04) with regression-test coverage, independently re-verified (full suite 2335 passed both before and after a merge-conflict resolution). Manual /rc failure (the original inherited-DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK explanation) also resolved this session. Live end-to-end UAT of zero-touch auto-reconnect on an affected Mac session is tracked separately as its own closable outcome: AI-CLI-70on.

title: ai c 6 resumed the wrong CC transcript (sw-6-2 instead of sw-6) sharing the same worktree cwd
description:
Reproduced live 2026-08-15: Sergei ran 'ai c 6' expecting to resume the 'sw-6' CC session (transcript e708efd4-bdb7-4a55-a1c8-997e9747adc8, correctly customTitle=='sw-6' throughout, 17MB/200 history entries, its prior process was an idle bg-spare killed earlier this session as a one-off workaround -- see AI-CLI-idle-claude-bg-wwaj). Instead it resumed a DIFFERENT session, transcript e2184270-60ed-44f2-b198-3b16abfa6dc3, customTitle=='sw-6-2' (a distinct named ai-cli slot the user created previously), 79MB/539 history entries, sharing the exact same cwd (~/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-6) because ai-cli-utils' worktree-per-slot model does not enforce one CC project directory per ai-cli session name -- both 'sw-6' and 'sw-6-2' share Claude Code's own project-directory key (~/.claude/projects/-Users-...-worktrees-sw-6/), which holds both transcripts side by side.

Orchestrating-session investigation so far (read src/ai_cli/session_script.py and src/ai_cli/main.py in full before assuming this is complete):
1. session_script.py has 4 distinct launch branches for engine=='c': (a) prompt_file exists -> bare 'claude --continue "" --name ...' with ZERO title resolution or touch; (b) no prompt_file -> calls 'ai internal resolve-continue-target "/Users/sergeiwallace/projects/sergei/.worktrees/sw-4" ""' (main.py's _find_cc_session_by_title, exact customTitle match, NOT substring -- verified both sessions' titles are correctly distinct, so naive title-collision is NOT the cause) and on a match, touches that file before '--continue' (relying on Claude Code's own --continue semantics of 'resume the most-recently-modified transcript in this project directory' -- the touch is a race-based workaround, not a direct --resume-by-id); (c) resolve_status==2 (a LIVE process already owns the matched transcript, per _cc_session_is_live's psutil-style PID+start-time verification) -> falls back to a FRESH '--continue'-less launch; (d) resolver found nothing AND resolve_status!=2 but the project directory has ANY jsonl file -> BARE 'claude --continue --name ...' with NO title matching and NO touch at all -- this is the branch most likely exercised if resolve-continue-target legitimately returned empty for some reason not yet identified.
2. Claude Code's own 'bg-spare' pre-warmed-background-process feature (a claude-binary-internal mechanism entirely -- zero references to 'bg-spare' anywhere in ai-cli-utils' own source) is a SEPARATE, faster attach path this repo's code has no visibility into or control over. If Claude Code's own bg-spare claim mechanism keys by cwd rather than by ai_name/session identity, and BOTH e708efd4 and e2184270 had (or recently had) their own bg-spare processes registered for this same cwd, the actual resumed process may never have gone through session_script.py's --continue resolution logic AT ALL -- this needs to be determined from artifact evidence (compare timestamps in ~/.claude/sessions/*.json against the tmux pane's actual launch invocation logged wherever ai-cli-utils logs its own launches, e.g. handoff-events.jsonl or equivalent) before proposing a fix.
3. Ruled out as the cause: the git-pull-autostash warning Sergei also saw during this launch ('Warning: git pull --rebase failed in worktree sw-6 (autostash pop conflict?). Index restored to HEAD.') is the PRE-EXISTING, deliberate AIH-443 stranded-autostash defensive mechanism (pull_rebase_autostash(), main.py ~line 2124) correctly recovering from a transient rebase-pull failure with zero data loss -- unrelated subsystem (git sync at launch time, not CC transcript selection), no code path connects the two. Confirm this independently but do not spend investigation budget re-deriving it from scratch.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with artifact evidence (not just plausible-sounding code reading) for why 'ai c 6' resumed e2184270/sw-6-2 instead of e708efd4/sw-6 on this specific occasion -- state definitively which of the branches/mechanisms above (or a different one not yet identified) was actually exercised. Fix ensures a named ai-cli session slot (e.g. 'sw-6') can never resume a transcript titled for a DIFFERENT slot (e.g. 'sw-6-2') sharing the same cwd, regardless of which internal path (bare-continue fallback branch, bg-spare attach, or the resolver's touch-race) is taken -- the exact-title-match guarantee that already exists in one branch (resolve-continue-target) must hold on every launch path, not just the happy path. title: Exiting a CC session can leave it STOPPED not dead, so the launcher reads the name as in use and starts a new session instead of resuming
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> can you real quick kill hte cc session that was created for `ai c 3` from ai-harness repo that has something like rabbit suffix appended to it. also, we need to fix this issue for ai-cli-utils where if i exit a cc session, sometimes it doesn't actually kill the session and when i relaunch it, it sometimes treats it as a still running agent cc session. so you need to also kill the aih-3 cc session process as well so its no longer running so i can launch `ai c 3` to resume / continue it. but also add a /beads-task to ai-cli-utils and ship it and a cc task for how to properly exit cc sessions so the processes aren't continuing after i exit cc session which prevents me from resuming / continuing them so it creates a new cc session instead. /delegate that to opus to /bug-fix. and then kill those processes yourself. and delete the cc session jsonl transcript and whtaever other artifact files for the aih-3-rabbit cc session custom title one as well. then /save-state

## Task details

Exiting a Claude Code session does not reliably end its process. The process can survive in a state
that is genuinely alive to the kernel, so pid-liveness reports the session name as still in use, and
the next `ai c <n>` declines to resume it and launches a new session instead.

### Measured evidence, host sem-kg-sagemaker, 2026-08-14

Terminating the aih-3 session by signal, observed directly:

    pid 25794 = claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --name aih-3 --continue
    kill -TERM 25794    -> rc 0
    4 seconds later     -> /proc/25794 still present, state field = T
    kill -KILL 25794    -> process finally gone

State `T` is STOPPED, not `Z` (zombie) and not gone. **This is the mechanism.** A stopped process:

- is fully alive as far as `/proc/<pid>` and any pid-liveness predicate is concerned;
- is indistinguishable, by pid liveness alone, from a session the operator is actively using;
- never reaps, so it persists until something sends SIGKILL or SIGCONT.

That is why AI-CLI-cc-session-live-mvht does not cover this. That fix made `_pid_is_live`
(src/ai_cli/session_adopt.py:177) actually check pid liveness plus `procStart`, which correctly
handles an ABANDONED RECORD FOR A DEAD PID. Here the pid is genuinely alive, so the predicate is
right and the conclusion is still wrong.

Corroborating observations from the same host:

- A session record outlived its process: `~/.claude/sessions/25794.json` still existed after the
  process was gone, still naming `aih-3`. Removed by hand after asserting the pid was dead.
- The install is EDITABLE (`_editable_impl_ai_cli_utils.pth` -> this checkout's `src`), so the
  shipped source is what runs; this is not a stale-install problem.
- `tmux` is unusable on this host (`libutempter.so.0` missing), so on this machine there is no tmux
  pane whose death would take the child with it. Any exit path that assumes a tmux-managed lifetime
  does not apply here.
- The operator also reported a session launched as `ai c 3` acquiring a word-like suffix (they
  recalled "rabbit"). No such artifact exists now -- swept for it across
  `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.claude/tasks`, `~/.claude/sessions`, every `*.jsonl` transcript, the `ai`
  state dir and tmux, all zero, with a positive control on `aih-4` returning non-zero in three of
  those places. Everything visible restarted at 18:0x, which would have reaped it. So the suffixed
  session is consistent with this defect's downstream symptom but could not be inspected directly.

### What "properly exit" has to mean

The operator's ask is for a correct exit procedure, not only a repair. Both halves are in scope:

1. Exiting must actually end the process, or the launcher must detect and finish a session that
   stopped instead of exiting.
2. Liveness must distinguish "alive and in use" from "alive but abandoned". Pid existence alone
   cannot: it is true for `T` (stopped) and for a process whose terminal is gone.

### Acceptance criteria

AC-1 WHEN a session process is in state `T` (stopped) or any other non-runnable-but-present state,
THEN the launcher shall NOT treat that session name as in use by a live session.
AC-2 WHEN `ai c <n>` is invoked for a name whose recorded process is present but abandoned, THEN it
shall resume/continue that session rather than creating a new differently-named one, or shall
explain what it found and what it will do.
AC-3 WHEN a session is exited through the documented path, THEN its process shall be gone within a
bounded time, verified by the absence of `/proc/<pid>`, not by the exit command's return code.
AC-4 WHEN termination is required, THEN the escalation shall be SIGTERM, bounded wait, SIGKILL, and
it shall reap the process GROUP so a wrapper's children are not orphaned.
AC-5 A test shall fail if the liveness predicate reports a stopped process as a live session; it
must exercise a real stopped process (SIGSTOP a real child), not a mocked `/proc`.
AC-6 The documented exit procedure shall be written down in the repo, and shall state the
verification step from AC-3 rather than assuming the exit worked.
AC-7 WHEN a session record names a pid that is gone, THEN the record shall be pruned rather than left
to be interpreted later.

title: _cc_session_is_live matches a session record without checking the pid, so one stale record blocks that session name forever
notes:
Hit live on sem-kg 2026-08-12: `ai c kg-1` refused with

    Cannot continue session 'kg-1': its Claude Code session is still running (pid 3076127).

`/proc/3076127` did not exist, and no `claude ... --name kg-1` process was running anywhere on the box.
The refusal was pure fiction, and it is not transient: nothing ages the record out, so the session name
stays unusable until a human finds and deletes the file.

## Root cause

`_cc_session_is_live()` (`src/ai_cli/main.py:273`) walks `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` and returns
`(True, record["pid"])` on the first record whose `sessionId` equals the transcript stem. **It never
checks whether that pid is alive.** Claude Code writes one record per process and does not always
remove it — a killed or crashed process leaves its record behind permanently. The docstring already
frames the registry as "best-effort" and says a missing or malformed directory must not block a launch;
a record for a dead process is the same class of unreliability and should not block one either.

Measured on this box at the time: 9 records, **4 of them for pids that no longer exist** (kg-1, aih-1,
aih-3, aih-4). Three were harmless only because a live record for the same name existed alongside them
— each becomes a permanent block the moment its session exits, so this is latent for every session
name, not specific to kg-1.

## Fix

Treat a record as live only when its pid is running, and guard against PID REUSE while doing it:
compare the record's `procStart` against field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`. A recycled pid otherwise reads
as live and reintroduces the same false refusal on a different process. That comparison is already the
established fleet idiom for this check.

Decide deliberately what an unreadable `/proc/<pid>` means here. The worktree-liveness probe fails
CLOSED (unreadable means live) because it guards a deletion. This guard only decides whether to reuse a
transcript, and its own docstring says degraded registry state must preserve launch behavior, so it
should fail OPEN — `/proc` unreadable means "not proven live", allow the continue. Whichever way, state
it in the code, because the two probes reading the same `/proc` with opposite defaults is exactly the
kind of thing that gets "harmonised" wrongly later.

## Done when

A stale record for a dead pid no longer blocks `ai c <name> --continue`, a live one still does, and a
recycled pid is not mistaken for live. Regression test asserts all three, with the dead-pid case going
red against the current implementation.

## Also worth doing

Prune records whose pid is gone when the guard walks the directory. Without it the registry only grows,
and the next reader inherits the same landmine.

FIXED and on origin/main (`398278d`, merging `777d7ca` + `5f4d41a`). Verified by me, not taken on the
delegate's report.

## What shipped

`_cc_session_is_live` now classifies each record through `_cc_record_liveness`, which returns one of
three states rather than a boolean:

- `live` — pid runs AND `procStart` matches field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`, or the pid runs and the
  record carries no `procStart` (nothing refutes it, so the historical refusal is preserved).
- `gone` — pid is not running. The record is pruned as the directory is walked, which is what makes
  this self-healing instead of a manual sweep.
- `unproven` — cannot verify. Fails OPEN: the launch proceeds. Matches the registry's own documented
  best-effort contract; a dead-or-unverifiable process is the same class of unreliability as a missing
  or malformed directory.

`_proc_start_ticks` counts fields from after the **last** `)`, because field 2 is a parenthesized
executable name that may itself contain spaces and parens — a naive `split()` shifts every field and
silently compares the wrong number.

The fail-open choice is commented in code alongside the deliberate contrast with the fleet's *worktree*
liveness probe, which fails CLOSED because it guards a deletion. Two probes reading the same `/proc`
with opposite defaults is exactly what gets wrongly "harmonized" later.

## Verification — mine, independent of the delegate's

- **Mutation-verified by me after the merge:** neutering `_cc_record_liveness` to `return "live"` (i.e.
  restoring the original bug) turns **8 tests red**, including
  `test_given_registry_record_for_dead_pid_when_checked_then_not_live` and the prune, recycled-pid, and
  malformed-stat cases. Restoring gives 40 passed, and `main.py` came back byte-identical (verified by
  `cmp` and an empty `git diff`).
- Hard gate on the MERGED result in the main tree: `ruff check` clean, `ruff format --check` 94 files
  formatted, `uv run pytest` **2322 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Scope checked against the correct base (`merge-base..branch`, not `origin/main..branch`): 4 files,
  +303/-13.
- Present on origin by content: the two new functions appear, and the old unconditional
  `return True, record.get("pid")` is **absent** — a negative control, not just a positive one.
- Both delegated commits carry the full ordered trailer block with an absolute `Delegation-worktree`.

## Good judgment the delegate exercised beyond the brief

- It caught its own **vacuous test**: the first prune-failure probe passed under mutation because the
  escaping `OSError` was swallowed by the walk's outer `except OSError`, producing the same
  `(False, None)` the test asserted. It rewrote the test so the unlinkable dead record sorts before a
  live matching record, making the aborted walk observable. That is what `5f4d41a` is for.
- It found that a **pre-existing test relied on the bug** — asserting a refusal for a fake `pid 12345` —
  and rewrote it to register the test process's own pid and real `procStart`.
- It declined to prune on a `procStart` mismatch: a recycled pid means "not live" but deleting the
  record would mislead `session_adopt.live_sessions()`, `ai session adopt`, and `ai session audit`.
  Fixing the false refusal does not require the delete.
- The brief pointed it at `tests/test_session.py`; it measured that file to have zero references to the
  function and used `tests/test_bare_worktree.py`, which owns the registry fixtures. My brief was wrong
  and it checked rather than complying.

## Residual, filed separately

The prune's dead-pid determination goes through `session_adopt._pid_is_live`, which answers via
`Path.exists()`. That conflates "the pid is gone" with "I could not look" — an unreadable
`/proc/<pid>` (a `hidepid` mount, a different uid) reads as dead and the record is unlinked. Low
probability on the fleet's single-user boxes, but it is a delete authorized by a probe that cannot come
out the other way. Filed as its own issue.
close_reason: Closed

title: ai c 1 — stale orphan worktree directory blocks launch on Windows
ai c bare-mode Windows — TUI corruption and keyboard handling broken (random chars, Shift+Enter, Ctrl+C)
Remote named-session launch preview identity does not match the server-allocated tmux session name
description:
Surfaced by AI-CLI-208's Round 2 audit (N-1,
docs/audits/ai-cli-208-session-naming-casing-audit.md) while verifying DV-1.
CONFIRMED pre-existing, unrelated to casing: verified against
src/ai_cli/main.py at commit 2519721^ (before any AI-CLI-206/208 casing
work) -- the pre-transport remote-preview line already never allocated an
index for a named remote session; it used the raw requested name verbatim
with no index suffix.

BUG: for a NAMED remote launch (e.g. "ai c --remote Planning"), the local
client emits an iTerm2 profile/title, leases a color slot, and constructs a
cleanup command using a locally-guessed session identity (e.g.
"c-r-app-planning") BEFORE the remote host actually runs
build_session_name()/find_next_index() and allocates the real, index-suffixed
session name (e.g. "c-r-app-planning-1"). The local preview and the actual
remote-created tmux session name diverge whenever an index gets appended --
which is every named launch, since named launches always go through
find_next_index(). Verified directly:
  preview: c-r-app-planning
  server:  c-r-app-planning-1
(AI-CLI-208's fix made both sides consistently lowercase, but did not, and
per its own casing-only scope should not have needed to, fix this
pre-existing index mismatch.)

IMPACT: the local machine's color-slot lease, iTerm2 profile/title, and the
"ai internal cleanup-session-files" cleanup command all target a session
name that is not the one actually created on the remote host. Cleanup in
particular may silently no-op against a name nothing ever uses.

ROOT CAUSE: the local machine cannot know the remote host's tmux occupancy
at preview-emission time (it runs before the SSH/mosh transport even
connects), so it cannot compute the same index the remote's
find_next_index() will independently allocate. A correct fix needs either
a remote preflight/handshake that returns the canonical allocated
session_id/ai_name before local profile/color/cleanup setup runs, or some
other mechanism to make named-session allocation deterministic across the
transport boundary -- this is a small protocol change, not a one-line fix.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- For a NAMED remote launch, the local client's iTerm2 profile/title
  emission, color-slot lease, and cleanup command all use the SAME session
  identity the remote host actually allocates via
  build_session_name()/find_next_index() -- not a locally-guessed,
  index-less preview.
- Numeric/bare remote launches (which don't require find_next_index() to
  break a tie -- the index is either explicit or trivially derivable) are
  unaffected if they already work correctly; verify they do as part of this
  fix.
- Regression test: named remote launch: local preview identity must equal
  the identity the remote-side build_session_name() call actually returns
  for the same inputs.
close_reason: Fixed at commit 999a0dd: named remote launches now preflight the remote host via 'ai internal allocate-session-name' (calls the real build_session_name()) before local iTerm2 profile/title/color-lease/cleanup setup, so the local preview and remote-allocated identity are always the same string. Regression test exercises the real local-preview-vs-remote-allocation boundary, confirmed RED-before/GREEN-after. Also fixed a regression the preflight introduced in the pre-existing AI-CLI-208/F-1 shell-injection test (unmocked new subprocess call attempted a real SSH connection). Full suite independently verified green (2539 passed) excluding two unrelated pre-existing failures filed as AI-CLI-t4aq and AI-CLI-660i. Delegated to Codex (cx implement, effort high); shell-injection test regression root-caused and fixed directly by the orchestrating session.

title: ai c <N> ignores an existing case/remote-differing worktree and session, creating a duplicate instead of resuming
description:
REPRODUCTION (Linux/Hetzner, case-sensitive filesystem -- confirmed live):
  1. A project's fleet-registry prefix is registered uppercase (e.g. "APP").
  2. An existing worktree + live tmux session were created earlier, before the
     prefix was uppercase, under the lowercase spelling: worktree
     .worktrees/app-7, tmux session named with a lowercase/no-remote-marker
     naming scheme (observed live case: the existing session is literally
     "c-r-app-7" -- lowercase prefix AND carrying the "-r-" remote-launch
     marker, meaning it was originally created via a remote (-R) launch when
     the prefix still resolved lowercase).
  3. Run "ai c 7" locally on that same machine (no -R flag). build_session_name()
     (session.py:498) computes ai_name purely from the CURRENT project_prefix
     verbatim plus the bare index -> "APP-7" uppercase, and computes the tmux
     session name the same way, with is_remote=False (no "-r-" segment) since
     this specific invocation is local -- neither matches the existing
     "c-r-app-7" session's actual name.
  4. find_next_index() (session.py:264) checks tmux occupancy via a
     "tmux has-session -t <computed-name>" call -- a case-sensitive,
     exact-string match against the computed "c-APP-7", which does not match
     the existing "c-r-app-7" session at all (differs in casing AND the
     remote-marker segment). It reports index 7 / slot "APP-7" as free.
  5. create_worktree("APP-7") (session.py:793, post AI-CLI-203/204/205 fixes)
     correctly does NOT collide with or delete the existing app-7 worktree
     (that class of bug is already fixed) -- but it DOES create a brand new,
     separate "APP-7" worktree and a brand new tmux session, entirely
     unrelated to the user's actual existing work.

IMPACT: the user runs "ai c 7" expecting to resume their existing session/
worktree, and instead gets a second, unrelated, freshly-created worktree +
session under a different name. This is confusing and, if the user starts
working in the new "APP-7" and forgets about "app-7", risks orphaning work in
whichever slot they don't return to. Not the same class of bug as AI-CLI-203
(which was about safety once a collision is detected) -- this is about
occupancy detection and slot resolution never recognizing the two as "the
same slot" in the first place.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, needs verification during root-cause-and-fix): neither
find_next_index()'s tmux occupancy check nor build_session_name()'s naming
construction normalize for casing or for the is_remote ("-r-") segment when
deciding whether a given bare index is already in use. The fleet-registry
prefix casing can legitimately differ from how pre-existing sessions were
named (as observed live), and a session can legitimately have been created
either locally or remotely at different points in its life -- occupancy
detection needs to account for both when deciding "is slot N already taken",
even though the CURRENT invocation's own computed name may still need to
follow the current prefix casing and remote-flag for creating something new.

Distinct from, and not fixed by, AI-CLI-203/204/205 (create_worktree's
collision-safety and accurate create/reuse announcement) -- this is one layer
