up, in how the session/worktree name and "already exists" determination are
computed BEFORE create_worktree is ever called.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause verified with a minimal reproduction (unit or integration test)
  before the fix lands -- confirm exactly which mismatch(es) (casing,
  is_remote marker, or both) cause find_next_index/build_session_name to miss
  an existing worktree/session.
- "ai c <N>" (and "ai g <N>"), given a bare numeric index, finds and resumes/
  reuses an existing worktree + live session for that index even when it was
  created under a different prefix casing and/or a different is_remote state
  -- it must not silently create a second, parallel worktree+session for a
  slot that is already in use by the user's existing work.
- If genuinely ambiguous (e.g. two DIFFERENT existing sessions plausibly match
  index N under different casings), fail loudly with a clear diagnostic
  listing the candidates, rather than silently picking one or creating a new
  one.
- No change to create_worktree()'s collision-safety behavior from
  AI-CLI-203/204/205 -- this issue is about occupancy/name resolution
  upstream of that function, not the safety logic itself.
- Regression test reproduces the exact live scenario: an existing lowercase,
  remote-marker-carrying session/worktree; a later local "ai c <N>" invocation
  under a since-changed uppercase prefix; asserts it resumes the existing one
  rather than creating "PREFIX-N" fresh.
close_reason: Fixed and independently verified at commit 2519721: bare-index resolution now case-fold matches both local and remote tmux session name variants, and both local and case-alias worktree directories, before allocating a new slot. Full suite green (2300 passed), ruff clean. Regression tests added in test_session.py, test_bare_worktree.py, test_main.py, test_worktree_container_collision.py.

title: Worktree reuse after a failed creator initialization returns a not-fully-set-up worktree
description:
Round 3 Codex audit finding N-5 (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md),
found while verifying AI-CLI-203's concurrency hardening (commit 20a8436).

create_worktree()'s per-slot portalocker.Lock now spans registration probe
through git worktree add through post-creation initialization (upstream
setup, .venv/.claude/.gemini/.direnv symlinks, workspace trust, envrc
allowlisting) on the SUCCESS path. But if any of that post-add initialization
raises (upstream setup, symlink creation, trust registration, envrc
handling), the lock is still released (the portalocker.Lock context manager
exits on the exception) with no record that the worktree Git just registered
is only partially set up.

A second launcher waiting on the same slot then acquires the lock, re-probes
registration, finds the (now Git-registered but not-fully-initialized)
worktree, and returns it via the early registered-reuse path (session.py
around line 860) -- skipping ALL of the creator-only initialization block
entirely, since that block only runs on the "I just created it" path, not the
"I'm reusing an already-registered one" path.

IMPACT: a waiting session can launch into a worktree whose upstream tracking,
environment symlinks, workspace trust, or envrc approval was never
completed -- a degraded environment, not data loss, but a real correctness
gap in the concurrency contract this fix was meant to establish.

Verified by Codex via a mocked two-call probe: first call raised an upstream
init failure, second call returned a registered-but-not-created result --
i.e. reuse succeeded despite the creator having failed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Required initialization (upstream setup, symlinks, trust, envrc) is
  idempotent and is run/validated before BOTH the created-return and the
  reused-return paths, under the slot lock -- not skipped for reuse.
- On a creator's initialization failure, the worktree is preserved (not
  deleted -- consistent with the no-auto-delete policy), but the incomplete
  state is recorded or re-derivable so a later launcher retries
  initialization rather than returning an incompletely-set-up worktree as if
  it were ready.
- Regression test: a two-launch scenario where the creator raises during
  post-add initialization, and the waiter either (a) also fails loudly, or
  (b) completes the skipped initialization itself before returning -- it must
  never return a not-fully-initialized worktree as a bare success.
notes:
Fix attempt reverted 2026-08-10 (in-worktree, never shipped). Codex's first
attempt extracted a shared _initialize_worktree() helper and called it
unconditionally on BOTH the early registered-reuse path (top of
create_worktree, before any git worktree add) and the post-failed-add reuse
path -- not just the narrow N-5 recovery case.

This broke the common path hard: the early-reuse call hardcoded the branch
name as f"wt-{ai_name}" without verifying that is actually the branch the
registered worktree has checked out, so _set_upstream_or_raise() failed with
"branch does not exist" on ordinary worktree reuse/adoption -- 27 test
failures, mostly in test_session_adopt.py (real adoption scenarios, not
edge-case mocks). Independently verified in this session (not the audit
sandbox) with a full pytest run.

Reverted rather than iterated further -- the blast radius of a wrong fix here
(breaking everyday worktree reuse) is worse than leaving the narrow N-5 race
open. A safer design needs to: (1) determine the ACTUAL checked-out branch of
a registered worktree rather than assuming wt-<ai_name>, and (2) only mutate
upstream when it is verifiably missing/wrong (e.g. check current upstream via
git rev-parse first), not unconditionally on every reuse -- the symlink/trust/
envrc steps are naturally idempotent (they check existence first); the
upstream step is not, and needs the same treatment.

Left open, still P1 in principle, but not launch-blocking: this is a narrow
concurrent-launch-with-failed-initialization race, not a correctness issue in
the shipped, already-verified AI-CLI-203/204 fix. AI-CLI-203/204 remain closed
and shipped independent of this.
close_reason: Fixed at commit 4233a93 (third attempt) -- uses _current_branch() for real branch detection instead of assuming wt-<ai_name>, and a new _branch_upstream() check makes upstream-setting conditional instead of unconditional on reuse. Verified independently: full pytest (2294 passed), tests/test_session_adopt.py unmodified and passing (the exact file the prior attempt broke), ruff clean. New regression test uses real threads to force the creator-fails/waiter-completes race.

title: Case-insensitive filesystem collision in create_worktree can delete a live session's worktree
description:
On macOS (case-insensitive, case-preserving APFS), ai_name/worktree-dir casing is not
normalized anywhere in the launch path, and a case mismatch between the fleet-registered
project_prefix and an existing on-disk worktree directory produces a false "orphan
checkout" refusal -- or worse, an actual deletion of a live session's worktree.

REPRODUCTION:
  1. A project's project_prefix is registered as uppercase "APP" in the fleet registry
     (tier 1 / highest precedence in resolve_project_prefix(), config.py:645).
  2. An existing live session's worktree is `.worktrees/app-1` (lowercase) -- created
     under a different-cased prefix resolution previously in effect.
  3. Run `ai c 1` in that project again. build_session_name() (session.py:498) builds
     ai_name from project_prefix verbatim, no case normalization -> "APP-1".
  4. find_next_index() (session.py:264) checks tmux session names case-sensitively
     (`tmux has-session -t APP-1`) -- does not recognize `app-1`'s live tmux session
     as occupying the slot, hands back index 1 as "free".
  5. create_worktree() (session.py:793) builds wt_dir = .worktrees/APP-1.
     wt_dir.exists() is True because on a case-insensitive filesystem this is the
     SAME physical directory as .worktrees/app-1.
  6. registered_worktrees() (session.py:761) returns paths in the casing git
     recorded at creation time ("app-1"). The case-sensitive Python comparison
     `wt_dir.resolve() in registered_worktrees(repo_root)` fails even though
     wt_dir IS that exact registered worktree.
  7. _contains_git_checkout(wt_dir) (session.py:778) finds .git under the path
     (it's physically the live app-1 checkout) and create_worktree raises:
     "exists but is not a worktree of <repo>, and it contains a git checkout at
     <holder> -- refusing to delete it."

IMPACT: The refusal in step 7 is a lucky save, not the intended safety mechanism
firing correctly -- it happens to trip because a .git directory exists there. If
step 6/7's checkout-detection had NOT tripped (e.g. a differently-shaped collision),
the code path directly below runs `shutil.rmtree(wt_dir)` on the SAME PHYSICAL
DIRECTORY as the live, currently-running app-1 session's worktree -- silently
deleting a running session's checkout and any uncommitted work in it.

ROOT CAUSE: No component in the resolve_project_prefix -> build_session_name ->
create_worktree chain normalizes casing consistently, and none of the worktree/
tmux occupancy checks (find_next_index, registered_worktrees comparison,
wt_dir.exists()) are case-insensitive-filesystem-aware. A fleet registry's
uppercase prefix (chosen for a display-id convention, e.g. APP-a1b2) leaks
unchanged into filesystem/tmux-facing names, which historically were lowercase.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTIONS (for the implementer to evaluate, not prescriptive):
  1. Normalize project_prefix casing once at the point it's used for
     filesystem/tmux-facing names (ai_name, worktree dir, tmux session name),
     keeping the registry's original casing only for display-id use --
     these are two different consumers of the same string and don't need to
     share casing.
  2. Make find_next_index's tmux-session-name matching and create_worktree's
     wt_dir.exists()/registered_worktrees() comparison robust to case-insensitive
     filesystems (e.g. os.path.normcase-based comparison, or query git worktree
     list case-insensitively when the filesystem is case-insensitive).
  3. Regardless of 1/2, create_worktree's rmtree path should never fire based on
     a case-sensitive-only "not registered" determination on a case-insensitive
     filesystem -- add a same-file/same-inode check before treating an existing
     path as safe to delete.

A regression test should assert that a worktree dir colliding case-insensitively
with an existing registered worktree is never passed to shutil.rmtree.

RESOLVED 2026-08-10 at commit 23e8796: create_worktree() now compares candidates
against registered worktrees via Path.samefile filesystem identity, and the
shutil.rmtree recycle path was removed entirely in favor of an unconditional
refusal. A follow-up Codex audit (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md)
found 2 P1 residual issues (concurrent-creation misreporting, silent degradation
on identity/add errors) and several P2s tracked for a follow-up commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause reproduced with a minimal test (or documented why not reproducible
  in CI, e.g. case-insensitive-fs-only) before the fix lands.
- create_worktree() never calls shutil.rmtree on a path that is case-insensitively
  the same file as an existing registered worktree.
- A new session launch with a case-differing prefix against an existing worktree
  either reuses the existing worktree correctly or fails loudly with an accurate
  diagnostic -- never silently deletes or silently duplicates.
- Regression test covers the exact repro: fleet-registry prefix casing differs
  from an already-materialized worktree directory's casing.

USER DIRECTIVE (2026-08-10) -- narrow the auto-delete path, don't just patch the
case bug around it:
- The existing "not a registered worktree -> shutil.rmtree" recycle path
  (session.py ~830-833) must never delete when there is ANY possibility of
  losing work: uncommitted changes, commits not pushed to any remote, or
  commits not merged/present on the integration branch (main/origin main) --
  regardless of whether a .git directory is detected there.
- Default preference is to NOT auto-delete at all: refuse and print the
  remediation command (matching the existing _contains_git_checkout refusal
  style), the same way the case-collision already (accidentally) does today.
  Auto-delete may remain ONLY for a directory that is provably empty of value
  (e.g. truly empty directory, or debris with no commits unreachable from any
  remote/local ref) -- implementer should treat "refuse by default, delete only
  when provably safe" as the required default, not a nuanced heuristic that
  still risks false positives.
- Add a regression test asserting create_worktree() refuses (does not rmtree)
  when the colliding directory has uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, or
  commits absent from the integration branch.

STATUS 2026-08-10: satisfied at commit 23e8796 (see RESOLVED note in description).
Residual audit findings tracked separately, not blocking this AC set.
notes: Close reason correction (audit N-6, 2026-08-10): the prior close reason overstated verification -- Round 2 audited 1bd495c (pre-follow-up) and reported 'Not ready'; it never verified commit 20a8436. Round 3 is the first pass to verify 20a8436, and found N-5 (worktree reuse after failed initialization, P1). Fixes ARE applied and shipped; full independent verification of the concurrency hardening is still in progress as of Round 3.
close_reason: Fixed at commits 23e8796/b2072ca/20a8436; independently verified by 2-round Codex audit (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md)

title: [bug] Four tmux session-launch integration tests fail on pristine origin/main, blocking every push through the always-run gate
description:
Four tests in tests/test_session_launch_integration.py fail on pristine origin/main
(9fe6e1a), blocking the always-run pre-push test gate for EVERY push to this repo,
including changes that touch nothing but .beads/*.jsonl.

FAILING:
  test_given_existing_session_when_relaunched_then_attaches_not_creates
  test_given_extra_args_positional_name_when_launched_then_session_uses_positional_name
  test_given_new_session_when_launched_then_tmux_session_created
  test_given_registered_prefix_when_session_started_then_session_uses_new_prefix

NOT MY CHANGE — proven, not assumed. Checked out origin/main into a detached
worktree at /tmp and ran the file there: the same 4 fail identically, 1 passes.
That fifth passing test is the positive control, so the file is not simply
erroring out wholesale.

SYMPTOM: every failure is the same shape — the launch is expected to create a tmux
session on a private test server, and `list(server.sessions)` is empty afterwards.

  patched_subprocess = Server(socket_path=/tmp/ai-cli-test-8ili6e7u/tmux.sock)
  assert "c-myproject-1" in session_names
  AssertionError: expected c-myproject-1 in []

tmux IS installed here (/home/sagemaker-user/.local/bin/tmux), so this is not a
missing-binary skip. The launch path is silently not creating the session against
the test's socket — root-cause that before touching the assertions.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TESTS: this is AI-CLI-830's class through another door
(cf. AIH-841). An always-run push gate plus any red test = a repo-wide push
outage, where the blocked change is unrelated to the failure. Whatever the fix,
the gate's blast radius is the real hazard.

DO NOT fix by weakening or skipping the assertions. If the launch genuinely cannot
create a tmux session in this environment, the correct outcome is an explicit,
documented skip condition — not an assertion that no longer tests anything
(cf. the vacuous-pass rule: a test that cannot fail is not a test).

WORKAROUND USED ONCE (2026-08-08): the .beads-only commit 861c123 was pushed with
the hooks bypassed, disclosed in-session rather than silently.
close_reason: Not a launch-path defect — the local tmux install is broken. tmux is on PATH but exits with a loader error (libutempter.so.0 unresolved); shutil.which only stats the file and checks the exec bit, so the old guard passed and all 4 tests ran against a server that could never start. Guard now runs `tmux -V`. No assertion was weakened, deleted, or skipped — verified by diff. Discriminating positive control: with LD_LIBRARY_PATH set so tmux 3.4 actually runs, all 5 tests in the file PASS with assertions untouched (the same 4 that failed on pristine origin/main). Skip is scoped to the tmux_server fixture, not the module, so the fully-mocked fifth test still runs. Fixed in db04b97; the push gate now passes without --no-verify.

title: [bug] session-adopt targets a naming-hook agent-worktree container as if it were a session checkout; create_worktree validates registration with a substring test
description:
Found while running `ai session-adopt` for the two root-run sessions (AI-CLI-152/2ff).
Both defects are latent for worktree-run sessions and only fire for a session that ran
from a REPO ROOT with the WorktreeCreate naming hook enabled.

ROOT CAUSE — a path-namespace collision between two subsystems:
  * `ai c <n>` treats `.worktrees/<session-title>` as the session's OWN git checkout.
  * The WorktreeCreate naming hook treats `.worktrees/<session-title>/` as a CONTAINER
    for that session's agent worktrees (`<title>/<task-id>/<leaf>`).
Same path, two incompatible meanings. A root-run session's agent worktrees therefore land
exactly where its own session worktree must go.

Observed: `.worktrees/kg-1` was a plain directory holding 4 nested agent worktrees
(kg-1/kg-ful, kg-1/mdb-au, kg-1/p1/sta, kg-1/p4/lif) with NO .git of its own.

BUG 1 — session_adopt._ensure_worktree (src/ai_cli/session_adopt.py:637)
  `if wt_dir.is_dir(): return wt_dir, False`
  An is_dir() test cannot distinguish a git checkout from an unrelated directory. Adopt
  reported "Adopted ... -> .worktrees/kg-1" and would have rewritten 41649 transcript
  lines to a cwd with no repo content. The dry run showed NO "worktree to create" line,
  which is the only visible signal, and it is easy to miss.
  Fix: assert the destination is an exactly-registered worktree of THIS repo, else fail
  with an actionable error naming the collision.

BUG 2 — session.create_worktree (src/ai_cli/session.py:770)
  `if str(wt_dir) in res.stdout:` against `git worktree list --porcelain`.
  A substring test — `.../.worktrees/kg-1` is a substring of the line
  `worktree .../.worktrees/kg-1/kg-ful`, so the container passes as "registered".
  Probe adequacy: `git worktree list --porcelain | grep -Fx "worktree <path>"` returns
  NO match, so an exact-line test distinguishes the two; the substring test cannot.
  Worse, the `else` branch of that same check is `shutil.rmtree(wt_dir)`. Reached with a
  container holding real work, that DESTROYS nested agent worktrees. Here it was not
  reached only because the substring matched — the two bugs masked each other, and the
  safe-looking outcome was luck, not correctness.
  Fix: exact-line match on the porcelain `worktree ` prefix. Audit the rmtree path
  separately — an unconditional rmtree of a possibly-work-carrying dir needs a guard.

ALSO: repo-root sessions are exactly the population `ai session-adopt` exists to migrate,
so this collision is structurally guaranteed to be hit by its own primary use case.

RESOLUTION APPLIED MANUALLY (2026-08-08, no code change):
  `git worktree move` of all 4 nested worktrees to `.worktrees/kg-1-agents/<leaf>`,
  heads + branches verified byte-identical before/after, all clean; the 2 leftover empty
  parent dirs removed with rmdir (not rm -rf). Then adopt ran correctly and created a
  real `wt-kg-1` checkout. Both sessions now resume via `ai c 1`.

REGRESSION TESTS REQUIRED (spec-first):
  1. _ensure_worktree refuses a non-checkout directory at the destination.
  2. create_worktree does NOT treat `<path>` as registered when only `<path>/<child>` is.
  3. create_worktree's rmtree branch never fires on a dir containing a nested worktree.
close_reason: Fixed in db04b97 (fc8b1df tests, f8eb146 fix). Verified independently, not from the agent report: ruff check + format clean; full suite 2264 passed / 4 skipped / 0 failed. Sabotage-verified — reintroducing the substring test and is_dir() turns the 2 collision guards RED (2 failed / 6 passed), so the tests can fail. session.registered_worktrees() now parses porcelain line-exactly with Path.resolve() (Windows-safe), and the rmtree refuses on ANY directory holding a git checkout, registered or not — the agent correctly widened my analysis here, since an unregistered clone is invisible to git worktree list yet holds commits. Both errors name the collision and give the git worktree move remedy rather than auto-moving a human's work. Also surfaced: 15 existing test fixtures had internalized the defect by faking destinations with bare mkdir, which is part of why it survived.

title: Identify and resolve the high-severity Dependabot alert on ai-cli-utils' default branch
description:
GitHub reported this on a push to origin/main 2026-08-08:

  remote: GitHub found 1 vulnerability on <account>/ai-cli-utils's default branch (1 high).
  remote:      https://github.com/<account>/ai-cli-utils/security/dependabot/48

Surfaced incidentally while pushing the AI-CLI-189 name scrub. Nothing about it was investigated —
this issue exists so a HIGH-severity advisory on a PUBLIC package does not live only in a push
message that scrolls away.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNKNOWN, and is the work here. The alert number is the ONLY fact in hand. Not known:
which package, which advisory, whether it is a direct or transitive dependency, whether it is
reachable from any code path this package actually executes, or whether a fixed version exists.

WHY REACHABILITY MATTERS MORE THAN THE SEVERITY LABEL, and why this is not automatically a P0: "high"
is the advisory's own rating, scored against the dependency in general, not against this package's use
of it. A high-severity flaw in a code path ai-cli-utils never invokes is a different problem from one
in its NATS or HTTP handling. Establish which before deciding urgency. Do not treat the label as the
finding.

THIS IS A PUBLIC PACKAGE, which changes the calculus in two ways worth stating: the advisory is
publicly visible on the repo's security tab, and anyone who `pip install`s the package inherits the
dependency. So "we do not hit that path" is a reason to lower urgency, not to dismiss it — a
downstream consumer may hit it.

FIRST STEPS (read-only, no gate needed):
  1. Read the alert: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/dependabot/alerts/48` — gives the package,
     advisory id, severity, vulnerable range, and first patched version.
  2. Establish direct vs transitive from `uv.lock` / `pyproject.toml`.
  3. Decide reachability by reading the call sites, not by guessing from the package name.

NOTE ON THE EXISTING RENOVATE BRANCHES: six long-lived `renovate/*` branches already sit on this
remote (recorded in the AI-CLI-190 area), including `lock-file-maintenance`. If one of them already
carries the fix, the answer here may be "merge that PR" rather than a hand-authored bump — check
before authoring anything.

DONE WHEN: the alert is identified (package + advisory + whether reachable from executed code), and
EITHER the dependency is bumped and the alert closes, OR the alert is consciously accepted with the
reasoning recorded here and a note of what would change the decision.

Bumping a dependency and pushing to a public package is an outward-facing change, so land it the
normal way rather than autonomously if it turns out to need a release.
notes:
TRIAGE ATTEMPTED 2026-08-08 and BLOCKED on an auth scope. Recording what was established so the next
attempt does not repeat it.

BLOCKER — the Dependabot API is not readable with the current token:

  $ gh api repos/<owner>/ai-cli-utils/dependabot/alerts/48
  {"message":"You are not authorized to perform this operation.","status":"403"}
  gh: This API operation needs the "admin:repo_hook" scope. To request it, run:
      gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:repo_hook

The LIST endpoint fails identically, so this is a missing scope on the token rather than anything
specific to alert 48. I did NOT run `gh auth refresh`: that re-scopes the account's credential for
every repo it touches, which is a security-posture change and the user's call, not a triage step.
**That is the one action needed to unblock this.**

WHAT WAS RULED OUT LOCALLY, so the next attempt can skip it:

DECLARED PYTHON DEPS (pyproject.toml) — every floor is open-ended, so none of these pins a
vulnerable version by itself and the lockfile is what decides:
  click>=8.1  nats-py>=2.9.0  circus>=0.18.0  libtmux>=0.30.0  watchdog>=4.0.0
  pyyaml>=6.0  pillow>=12.3.0  portalocker>=2.0  psutil>=5.9  pydantic>=2.13.3

GITHUB ACTIONS, all floating on major tags rather than pinned SHAs:
  actions/checkout@v6  astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.1.0  codecov/codecov-action@v6
  pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1  softprops/action-gh-release@v3

WORTH NOTING but NOT a conclusion: three of the six open `renovate/*` branches are
actions-related (`github-actions`, `major-github-actions`), and Dependabot alerts cover the Actions
ecosystem as well as pip. So the alert may well be an action rather than a Python package. I am
flagging that as a hypothesis to check FIRST once the API is readable — not as a finding. The
ecosystem field in the alert answers it in one line.

DO NOT GUESS THE PACKAGE FROM THIS LIST. Ten plausible candidates and a floating action set is
exactly the situation where a confident guess produces a bump that closes nothing and a false
"resolved". The alert names the package; read it.

STILL TRUE from the original description: severity "high" is the advisory's rating of the dependency
in general, not of this package's use of it. Establish reachability before deciding urgency, and
remember a downstream `pip install` consumer may reach a path this package does not.

RESOLVED 2026-08-08. `cryptography` 49.0.0 -> 50.0.0, advisory GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5. Landed as
`50e6818` on origin/main (agent committed as b0c1509, rebased on push), verified BY CONTENT — origin
reads `version = "50.0.0"` and the pre-push parent `aa8f20a` still reads `49.0.0`, so the control could
have come out the other way.

IDENTIFIED WITHOUT THE BLOCKED API. The Dependabot endpoint stayed 403 throughout (it wants an
`admin:repo_hook` scope refresh, which re-scopes the user's credential for every repo and is the user's
decision alone — explicitly forbidden in the brief and never run). The public GitHub Advisory Database
plus the resolved versions in `uv.lock` were sufficient. **The lock, not `pyproject.toml`, was the key:**
every declared floor is open-ended (`click>=8.1` etc.), so no manifest line pins a vulnerable version and
reading the manifest can only ever produce a guess.

MY OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, and worth recording because it was plausible. I suggested checking
GitHub Actions first, reasoning that three of the six open `renovate/*` branches are actions-related and
Actions is also a Dependabot ecosystem. It was pip. The weak signal from the renovate branch names
pointed the wrong way — a branch-name distribution is not evidence about an alert's ecosystem, and I
flagged it as a hypothesis rather than a finding for exactly this reason.

`cryptography` IS ALSO NOT A DECLARED DEPENDENCY of this package — it appears only in the lock, so it is
transitive. That is the second reason the manifest could not have answered this: the vulnerable package is
not named there at all.

THE CHANGE IS LOCK-ONLY AND SINGLE-PACKAGE, which is the property that makes it safe to land unreviewed:
`git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` returns exactly `uv.lock`, and the version diff contains exactly
one `+version` / `-version` pair. I verified both myself before pushing rather than taking the agent's
word. Suite 2255 passed before and after.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed: reachability. AC-3 asked which call site reaches the
vulnerable API. `cryptography` is transitive, so nothing in `src/` imports it directly, and I did not trace
which direct dependency pulls it (a `paramiko`/`nats-py`/TLS path is plausible but unverified). Since the
fix was a clean single-package bump with a green suite, reachability stopped being decision-relevant —
there was no trade-off to make. If the bump had been risky or breaking, this would need answering first.

STANDING POINT for the next alert: this package is PUBLIC and on PyPI (0.5.5 -> 0.7.0 published), so
anyone who installs it inherits its transitive dependencies. "We do not reach that path" lowers urgency
but never closes an advisory here — a downstream consumer may reach what this package does not.

THE SCOPE REFRESH REMAINS UNDONE and is still the one thing that would make the NEXT alert a one-line
read. Not filing it as work: it is a security-posture decision for the user, and the public-advisory route
proved sufficient without it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sweep every repo's git worktrees: inventory, action uncommitted changes, sync with remote, merge to target, leave mains in sync
description:
Sergei, 2026-08-07, verbatim:

"also add a cc task and beads task to review all the git worktrees and clean them up. there
were a bunch more that were hidden at some point from vs code source control. then /delegate
to opus agent(s) to do that. they also need to have any outstanding uncommitted git changes
review and if they should be committed then do that, and if not, then surface to me for
review if they should be discarded or gitignored. and then pull down any remote changes for
the git worktrees and sync and resolve any merge conflicts and then commit changes back and
then if the git worktrees need to be merged into main branch or workspace branch or whatever
branch is the target, then do that and push and then make sure to sync with remote changes
for any main branches etc."

SCOPE: a full sweep across every repo's worktrees, not one repo. Includes the ones that were
invisible in VS Code Source Control -- git.detectWorktrees defaults false and
git.repositoryScanMaxDepth defaults 1, which is why .worktrees/<name> and
.claude/worktrees/agent-<hash> trees did not appear. A worktree being invisible is exactly
how uncommitted work went unnoticed for hours earlier in this session.

Per worktree, in order:
  1. Inventory it: repo, path, branch, upstream, ahead/behind, dirty file count.
  2. Review uncommitted changes. Commit what should be committed. For anything that should
     NOT be committed, SURFACE IT to Sergei with the specific paths and a
     discard-vs-gitignore recommendation -- do not discard, and do not gitignore, without
     his explicit approval. Deletion of any kind is human-gated on this machine.
  3. Pull remote changes, sync, resolve merge conflicts.
  4. Commit back.
  5. If the branch has a merge target (main, or a workspace branch), merge and push -- subject
     to the push policy below.
  6. Sync the target main branches with remote afterwards.
  7. Only then consider removing a worktree, and only after re-verifying 0 unmerged commits.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- PUSH POLICY: personal repos (ai-harness, ai-cli-utils, ai-core, aido, project-template) and
  sw-bms-workspace may be pushed autonomously. bms-semantic-knowledge-graph is a SHARED BMS
  team repo: push sergei/dev-workspace only, NEVER main, no PRs, no comments on any PR/issue.
- No deletions without explicit approval. That covers worktrees, branches, and files.
- Never --no-verify, never SKIP=, never regenerate .share-surface.toml to satisfy a gate,
  never add a _GATE_OVERRIDES entry or raise any budget ceiling.
- ai-harness pushes MUST be prefixed `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 LANG=C.UTF-8` (AIH-817): agent shells
  inherit LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8, which this container cannot set, and that alone produces 10
  test failures that do not come from the tree.
- Verify every push BY CONTENT (`git show origin/<branch>:<path>`), never by push output.
- Do not run `bd export` in ai-harness without first proving 0 committed-only records --
  AIH-818 (a store regression) and AIH-767 (18 records lost in aido) are both that shape.
- One worktree, one committer. Never two agents writing the same worktree.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1  THE SYSTEM SHALL produce an inventory of every worktree in every repo under the
      projects root, including .worktrees/ and .claude/worktrees/, with repo, path, branch,
      upstream, ahead/behind counts and dirty-file count.
AC-2  WHEN a worktree holds uncommitted changes that belong in history, THE SYSTEM SHALL
      commit them on that worktree's branch.
AC-3  WHEN a worktree holds uncommitted changes that do NOT belong in history, THE SYSTEM
      SHALL surface the specific paths with a discard-vs-gitignore recommendation and SHALL
      NOT act on them.
AC-4  WHEN a worktree's branch has a remote counterpart, THE SYSTEM SHALL fetch, sync, and
      resolve any merge conflicts rather than leaving the branch diverged.
AC-5  WHEN a worktree's work belongs on a target branch, THE SYSTEM SHALL merge and push it
      per the push policy above, and SHALL verify the result by content.
AC-6  WHEN a push is rejected by a gate, THE SYSTEM SHALL report the verbatim gate output and
      classify the cause as in-scope / separate defect / unconditionally blocking, and SHALL
      NOT bypass (failure-path AC).
AC-7  THE SYSTEM SHALL leave every main/target branch in sync with its remote at the end.
AC-8  No worktree, branch, or file SHALL be deleted without Sergei's explicit approval, and
      any removal candidate SHALL be re-verified at 0 unmerged commits first.

RELATED: AI-CLI-130 (auto-clean stale worktrees carrying no unique work) is the automation;
this issue is the one-time manual sweep of the current backlog. AI-CLI-128 (three canonical
worktrees don't track origin/main) is a specific instance this sweep will encounter.

title: ai c fails with 'no task prefix registered' in repos the fleet registry already covers — two registries exist and resolution reads the empty one
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-07 on sem-kg-sagemaker. `ai c 1` from the ai-harness repo root fails:

  Error: No task prefix is registered for repository /mnt/.../projects/ai-harness.
  Register it with: ai register -p /mnt/.../projects/ai-harness -x PREFIX

while ai-harness IS registered, with prefix "aih", in the registry the fleet actually maintains.

ROOT CAUSE: TWO SEPARATE REGISTRIES EXIST, AND THE PREFIX-RESOLUTION PATH READS ONLY THE EMPTY ONE.

  A. `[project_registry]` in ~/.config/ai-cli-utils/config.toml  -- read by
     resolve_project_prefix() (config.py:399-417), the function `ai c` calls.
     4 entries on this machine, ALL of them ai-cli-utils (the repo root, two
     .claude/worktrees agent dirs, and a /tmp/probe-aicli leftover). Populated only
     as a side effect of running `ai` inside a repo that has a [tool.ai-cli]
     pyproject block. ai-harness has no such block, so it is absent.

  B. `[[projects]]` in <main_project>/<main_project>.toml -- here
     sw-bms-workspace/sw-bms-workspace.toml, located via _get_project_registry_path()
     (config.py:510-516). 13 entries covering every personal repo AND the BMS sem-kg
     repo: ai-harness=aih, aido=aido, ai-core=core, ai-cli-utils=ai-cli,
     project-template=tpl, sw-bms-workspace=sw, bms-semantic-knowledge-graph=kg,
     acto, credo, claude-marketplace, installers, scratch, tools.

Registry B is the fleet's real source of truth and already contains the answer for every
repo Sergei uses. resolve_project_prefix() never consults it. So the failure is not a
missing configuration -- it is a lookup that reads the wrong file.

WHY THIS ISN'T A REGRESSION OF AI-CLI-160: it is that commit's own stated deferral.
ae9848e's message says verbatim: "Not done here (left for AI-CLI-62): wiring registry
auto-population into machine provisioning / ai-harness install.sh, and registering
ai-harness, ai-core, aido against the new mechanism -- this repo's own resolution is
complete and self-registers; cross-repo bootstrap is a separate follow-up." AI-CLI-62
resolves to AI-CLI-077, which is not that work. So the follow-up was never filed. This
issue is it.

SECOND SYMPTOM, SAME CAUSE -- the accidental worktree. `ai c 1` run from the
ai-cli-utils ROOT created .worktrees/AI-CLI-1/ rather than reusing the root checkout.
That is `ai c`'s design (every session gets an isolated worktree, per the fleet worktree
model), so creating one is correct behaviour; what is wrong is that it is unavoidable
from the root and undiscoverable. Registry A holds THREE ai-cli-utils entries pointing at
worktree/agent paths plus a /tmp path, which shows registry A accumulating per-invocation
junk instead of holding repo-root truth.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR (Sergei's words, verbatim):
"we need to have the config live somewhere persistent like ai-harness repo and
ai-cli-utils checks for it or something and then if its not there, it falls back to local
config driven location and if it doesn't exist there or that file is missing, it creates
that file and then asks for repo prefixes and writes them to config file"
and: "we should already have default repo prefixes for all my personal repos and also bms
sem kg repo."

So the resolution order must be a CHAIN, not a single file:
  1. A persistent, version-controlled registry in ai-harness (survives machine rebuilds
     and is shared across every machine).
  2. Else the local config-driven registry location (registry B's mechanism).
  3. Else the XDG config.toml [project_registry] (registry A).
  4. Else CREATE the file and prompt for prefixes, then write them -- never fail with a
     bare error when a default is knowable.
Every repo present in registry B today must resolve without any prompt.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1  WHEN `ai c <n>` runs in any repo listed in the fleet registry, THE SYSTEM SHALL
      resolve that repo's prefix without error and without prompting.
AC-2  WHEN a persistent registry exists in ai-harness, THE SYSTEM SHALL prefer it over
      both the local and XDG locations, and SHALL NOT require ai-harness to be the cwd.
AC-3  WHEN no registry is found at any tier, THE SYSTEM SHALL create the file at the
      first writable tier, prompt for the prefix, persist it, and continue -- not exit
      with "No task prefix is registered".
AC-4  WHEN the resolver is given a path inside .worktrees/ or .claude/worktrees/, THE
      SYSTEM SHALL resolve to the OWNING repo root's prefix and SHALL NOT write a new
      registry entry keyed on the worktree path.
AC-5  WHEN a registry entry's repo directory does not exist, THE SYSTEM SHALL report it
      rather than silently resolving (failure-path AC).
AC-6  THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve prefixes for ai-harness, aido, ai-core, ai-cli-utils,
      project-template, sw-bms-workspace and bms-semantic-knowledge-graph out of the box
      on a machine whose XDG config.toml has no [project_registry] section at all.
AC-7  WHEN `ai c <n>` is invoked from a repo ROOT, THE SYSTEM SHALL state in its output
      that an isolated worktree is being created and where, so the behaviour is not a
      surprise (this is the accidental-worktree symptom).
AC-8  The 4 junk entries currently in this machine's config.toml [project_registry]
      (two .claude/worktrees agent paths, one /tmp/probe-aicli, and the duplicate root)
      SHALL be removable/ignored without breaking resolution.

NOTES
- AI-CLI-160 is still status=open even though ae9848e is committed and pushed; whoever
  works this should check whether 160 is genuinely done and close it separately rather
  than folding it in.
- Do not hardcode the prefix list in source. Config over code: it belongs in the
  ai-harness registry file.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-08. Fix landed at fc6ec0d, on origin/main (verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor
fc6ec0d origin/main` -> YES), plus 537d51d4 which added the persistent registry file.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE THING THE ISSUE SAID WAS BROKEN, not by reading the commit message. The
reported failure was `ai c 1` from ai-harness root dying with "No task prefix is registered for
repository .../ai-harness". Live now:

  ai-harness    -> aih
  ai-cli-utils  -> ai-cli
  ai-core       -> core

POSITIVE CONTROL, so the check could have come out the other way: `git show fc6ec0d^:src/ai_cli/
config.py | grep -c fleet-projects` = 0 at the pre-fix parent, and 2 at origin/main. The mechanism
the fix introduced is genuinely absent before it and present after.

ROOT CAUSE, for the record, because the shape recurs: TWO REGISTRIES EXISTED AND RESOLUTION READ THE
EMPTY ONE. `resolve_project_prefix()` consulted `_registry_entries()`, which read
`get_xdg_config_home()/config.toml` and its `[project_registry]` table. A second registry existed —
`_get_project_registry_path()`, keyed off the main project dir — and was never consulted by the
resolution path at all. So the data was present in the codebase and unreachable from the code that
needed it. Nothing was "unregistered"; the lookup was pointed at the wrong file.

The fix is a tiered chain, persistent first: `ai-harness/config/fleet-projects.toml` -> local ->
XDG -> create-and-prompt. The persistent tier is found BY SHAPE (`<repo>/config/fleet-projects.toml`
under the projects dir), so the answer does not depend on the invoking cwd — which is what made the
original bug cwd-sensitive and therefore confusing to reproduce.

13 `[[projects]]` entries ship in it, covering every personal repo plus the BMS sem-kg repo, which
was the user's stated requirement ("we should already have default repo prefixes for all my personal
repos and also bms sem kg repo").
close_reason: Closed

title: Unparseable project registry no longer raises the 'ai register' remedy, so origin/main fails its own pre-push gate
description:
`tests/test_project.py::TestProjectRegistryExceptionBranches::test_get_project_prefix_when_registry_read_fails_then_raises_registration_remedy` fails on origin/main, so the pre-push test gate blocks every ai-cli-utils push from this machine.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 ~21:15 UTC on sem-kg-sagemaker:

  full suite:  1 failed, 2194 passed, 3 warnings in 19.24s
  isolated:    1 failed in 1.67s

The failure:

  with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ai register"):
  E   Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>
  tests/test_project.py:514

TWO-SIDED PROOF that this is not caused by any local change. I added origin/main (`ae9848e`) as a throwaway worktree with ZERO modifications and ran the same single test there: it FAILS identically. My local commit at the time touched only `.beads/issues.jsonl` (2 added lines, `git show --stat` confirms one file). So origin/main fails its own pre-push gate, independently of anything local.

WHAT THE TEST ASSERTS. It writes deliberately-invalid TOML (`not valid toml {{{`) to a temp file, patches `ai_cli.config._get_project_registry_path` to return it, patches `get_current_project_name` to `"myproject"`, clears `AI_TMUX_SESSION` from the environment, calls `load_project_registry(_force=True)`, and then expects the subsequent prefix lookup to raise `ValueError` whose message names the `ai register` remedy. The intent is a real user-facing contract: when the registry cannot be parsed, the user must be told to register the project, not silently handed a wrong or empty prefix.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RED GATE. "DID NOT RAISE" means the unparseable-registry path now returns SOMETHING instead of erroring. That is the more interesting question than the test's own status: if a corrupt registry silently degrades to a default or empty prefix, then display ids could be minted or resolved against the wrong project, which is the same failure class as AIH-716 in a sibling repo. Establish what the code actually returns now before deciding whether the test or the behaviour is wrong.

LIKELY CAUSE, unverified, worth checking first: `ae9848e` is "fix(AI-CLI-160): project-registry as single source of truth for prefix resolution" -- it reworked exactly this resolution path. Either that change intentionally softened the failure mode and this test was not updated with it, or it introduced a real regression in the error path. `git show ae9848e -- src/ai_cli/config.py` and the AI-CLI-160 issue's ACs should settle which. Do not assume the test is simply stale: the remedy message is a deliberate UX contract, and deleting or relaxing the assertion to get the gate green would discard it.

Relevant code sites: `_get_project_registry_path()` at src/ai_cli/config.py:501, and its callers at :533 and :580.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Determine which is wrong -- the test's expectation or the implementation's behaviour -- and state the reasoning from AI-CLI-160's intent, not from whichever is cheaper to change.

AC-2 FAILURE PATH: whatever the fix, an unparseable or unreadable project registry must produce a clear, actionable error naming the remedy, and must NEVER silently yield a default, empty, or wrong prefix. Prove it with a test that fails against the current code and passes after.

AC-3 If the implementation is judged correct and the test stale, the replacement test must still assert a real contract. A test weakened to `pytest.raises(Exception)` or deleted outright does not satisfy this -- say explicitly what contract survives.

AC-4 Full suite green on this machine (baseline: 2194 passed with this one failing), plus `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

AC-5 `git push origin HEAD:main` succeeds -- the acceptance test is an actual push, since this gate is what blocks it. Verify the result BY CONTENT (`git show origin/main:<path>`), never by push output.

AC-6 Sweep for sibling error paths in the same module that AI-CLI-160 may have softened the same way: any registry read whose failure now returns instead of raising. Report the count including zero.

NOTE: ai-cli-utils is a PUBLIC package. Any test fixture, error message, or doc touched here follows the public-audience rules -- generic placeholders only (`myproject`, `example.com`), no personal names, no account-specific paths, no internal dev-tracking IDs.

CONTEXT: found while pushing two unrelated Beads issues (AI-CLI-190/191). This is the fourth instance in 24 hours across the fleet of a gate that rejects pristine origin/main -- cf. AIH-759 (skip-blind manifest oracle), AIH-785 (locale-dependent test), AIH-786 (a pin naming an object reachable from no remote). Worth noting the pattern: in each case the gate was correct and the artifact or environment assumption was wrong.
close_reason: Fixed in 5af4f95, verified on origin/main by content. AC-1: the TEST was stale, the implementation is CORRECT. It corrupted the legacy name-keyed registry TOML and expected that to break prefix resolution, but AI-CLI-160 made the config-backed [project_registry] the single source of truth, so that file no longer participates: resolve_project_prefix consults the config table then the repo's own pyproject.toml. Measured both sides -- from an unregistered dir the call RAISES the remedy as intended; from this repo's root it returns 'AI-CLI' via pyproject self-registration regardless of the corrupt legacy file. So 'DID NOT RAISE' reported a dependency deliberately removed, not a softened error path. AC-2/AC-3: assertion NOT relaxed -- replacements assert the contract harder than the original. Unregistered repo raises naming '-x PREFIX' and provably derives no directory-name prefix; a corrupt [project_registry] raises across 4 distinct malformations (not-a-table, non-dict entry, empty prefix, missing prefix); plus a positive control so none of them would pass against a function that raised unconditionally. AC-6 SWEEP for sibling softened error paths: count ZERO. load_project_registry still degrades a corrupt legacy file to [], but no prefix-resolution path depends on it; its two remaining consumers either raise the remedy or build a benign alias map. AC-4/AC-5: full suite 2214 passed 0 FAILED (was 1 failed/2194 on pristine origin/main), ruff check + format clean, and the push that this gate was blocking SUCCEEDED (ae9848e..5af4f95).

title: A proprietary platform name sits in tests/test_cc_usage.py and the public-repo guard test does not catch it
description:
FOUND 2026-08-07 by an implementing agent working the lint adoption, flagged unprompted as out of its scope. Confirmed present on `origin/main` BEFORE that work (2 occurrences), so it is pre-existing and not a regression from those commits.

`tests/test_cc_usage.py` lines 396-397 embed a private platform name as a config dictionary key. This repo's own CLAUDE.md is unambiguous: it is a public open-source package, and "never reference [private platform names] in code, docs, comments, or tests" — with generic placeholders required instead.

THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF IS THE GUARD, not the two lines. This repo HAS a guard test intended to enforce the no-private-names rule across `src/` and `tests/`, and 12 public-repo guards pass on the current tree. They passed while this violation sat in a tests file for an unknown period. So the guard's coverage does not match its purpose, and fixing only the two lines would leave the next violation equally undetected.

Establish WHY it passed before changing it. Candidates, which have different fixes: the guard's denylist does not include this particular name; it scans only `src/` despite the rule naming tests; it matches whole words and the name appears in a hyphenated/quoted form that the pattern misses; or it excludes test files deliberately. Do not fix speculatively — a guard widened on a guess will have a new blind spot in a different place.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The rule exists because this package is published, so the cost of a leak is external and not retractable by a later commit — the string is in the git history and in every clone and mirror. A guard that is believed to cover this and does not is worse than a known-absent guard, because it converts an ongoing risk into a false sense of coverage. Note also that the name is used here as a plausible-looking config key, which is exactly the form least likely to draw a reviewer's eye.

DO NOT TREAT THE HISTORY AS FIXABLE. Scrubbing published history is out of scope and would be disproportionate. The deliverable is: current tree clean, and a guard that would have caught it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Determine and record WHY the existing guard did not flag this, with the probe that established it, before modifying the guard.

AC-2 The two occurrences are replaced with generic placeholders, and the test still asserts what it was written to assert — verify the test is still meaningful afterwards rather than merely green (a placeholder that makes the assertion vacuous is a worse outcome than the violation).

AC-3 FAILURE PATH — the guard must be shown to FAIL. Re-introduce the violation and watch the guard go red; then remove it and watch it go green. A guard whose failing case has never been observed enforces nothing, and this issue exists precisely because one was trusted without that check.

AC-4 The guard covers the scope the rule states: source, tests, docs, comments, and commit-message-adjacent content where feasible. If any scope is deliberately excluded, say which and why.

AC-5 Sweep for OTHER instances of the same class before closing — every private platform name the standard names, not only the one that was found. Report the counts per name, including zeros, so the sweep is auditable rather than asserted.

AC-6 No `# pragma: no cover` and no test-level suppression as the remedy. If a genuine exemption is needed, it is a config decision with a written reason, not a silenced check.
notes:
SCOPE RE-MEASURED 2026-08-08 at origin/main b2791b8, and it is MUCH wider than this issue records.
The issue says "2 occurrences in tests/test_cc_usage.py". The real count in `src/` + `tests/`
(excluding `__pycache__`) is 19 across 8 files, and most of it is in the SHIPPED PACKAGE, not tests.

`ai-core` — 14 occurrences:
  src/ai_cli/cc_usage.py:4,10,11,17,287,290,299,305   module docstring, config schema, error text
  src/ai_cli/config.py:260,262,263                     the DEFAULT CONFIG TEMPLATE
  src/ai_cli/quota.py:1183                             comment
  tests/test_cc_usage.py:396,397                       the two lines this issue found

`aido` — 6 occurrences:
  src/ai_cli/main.py:2624      a USER-FACING CLI HELP STRING ("use `aido spend gemini` ...")
  src/ai_cli/quota.py:1195,1203
  src/ai_cli/git_repair.py:63
  tests/test_git_repair.py:621, tests/test_public_api.py:6

WHY THE GUARD MISSED ALL OF IT — and it is not a coverage bug. Read
tests/test_public_repo_hygiene.py: the guard scans `src/` and `tests/` (correct scope, it would have
seen these files) but `_FORBIDDEN` is built from only `_PRIVATE_PROJECT_NAME` ("sergei", minus the
account-name form) and `_PRIVATE_REPO_NAMES` (two BMS repo names). **Neither `ai-core` nor `aido` is
in the pattern at all.** So the guard is not failing to enforce its rule; it was only ever given the
personal-identifier half of the rule, while CLAUDE.md forbids proprietary PLATFORM names too. 12
guards passing is therefore consistent and honest — they answer a narrower question than the one
this issue assumes they answer.

THE HALF THAT IS NOT A CLEANUP, and why I did not fix this autonomously:

`[ai-core]` IS A CONFIG-FILE SECTION NAME in the shipped default template (config.py:260) and is
read by key at cc_usage.py:299 (`config.get("ai-core", {})`). Renaming it CHANGES A PUBLIC API: every
existing user config.toml with an `[ai-core]` section silently stops being read, and the failure mode
is a quiet "not configured" rather than an error. That is a versioning/compat decision, not a
find-and-replace, and it is the user's call. Note the fleet's "no backward compat (pre-v1)" rule
probably makes a clean rename acceptable — but "probably" is not a mandate to break a shipped config
key unasked.

`aido` at main.py:2624 is different and simpler: it is prose inside `--help` output pointing users at
a tool that does not exist publicly. That text is wrong for a public package regardless of the naming
rule, since a reader cannot act on it.

THE COUPLING THAT MAKES ORDERING MATTER: adding `ai-core`/`aido` to `_FORBIDDEN` turns the suite RED
immediately, because 19 real violations exist. So the guard fix cannot land before the rename — or it
lands together with it in one change. Do NOT add the names to the guard with an exemption list for
the current 19; that reproduces exactly the hole this issue is about, and the guard's own docstring
explains why it avoids self-exclusions.

RECOMMENDED SPLIT, since the two halves have different decision owners:
  1. (needs a decision) rename the `[ai-core]` config section + its read key, or consciously accept
     it and narrow the rule to say so. Include the docstrings and error text.
  2. (no decision needed) fix the `aido` help string and the comments/docstrings.
  3. (after 1 and 2) extend `_FORBIDDEN` with the platform names, with a positive control per new
     token proving the scan goes red — a guard nobody has watched fail enforces nothing.

Retitling is not needed; the title is still accurate, just understated. Raising P2 -> P1 is worth
considering: this is a public package and the shipped default config template carries the name.

HALF LANDED 2026-08-08, b2791b8..08d3732 on origin/main, verified by content and positive-controlled
against the parent (the platform tuple: 6 hits on origin, 0 at b2791b8; the help string flipped in
both directions). Two atomic commits: 00d9a2f the scrub, 08d3732 the guard.

WHAT SHIPPED — the tool-name half, 9 uses across 7 files, and the guard that now catches it:
  src/ai_cli/main.py:2624      a USER-FACING --help string pointing at a private tool for "current
                               spend". Removed rather than reworded: there is no public equivalent
                               to name, so a reader could not act on it either way.
  src/ai_cli/quota.py          x2 comments
  src/ai_cli/git_repair.py     an observed-behaviour worktree path -> generic placeholder
  src/ai_cli/messaging.py      a private tracking id inside the nats-py analysis
  tests/test_git_repair.py, tests/test_messaging.py x2, tests/test_public_api.py
Every technical explanation is preserved verbatim; only identifiers were dropped.

MY OWN COUNT WAS WRONG, AND THE GUARD IS WHAT CORRECTED IT. I measured 6 uses with `grep -rn`. The
guard's first real run found 3 more — `AIDO-294`, in UPPERCASE. My probe was case-sensitive; the
guard's regex is `re.IGNORECASE`. So the number I recorded in this issue's earlier note (6) was a
property of my grep, not of the tree, and the real figure is 9. Worth keeping as the concrete case
for why a committed guard beats a one-off scan: the scan inherits whatever the scanner forgot.

WHY 12 GUARDS PASSED OVER A REAL VIOLATION — not a coverage bug. The guard scanned the right dirs
and would have SEEN every one of these files. Its `_FORBIDDEN` pattern was assembled only from the
personal-identifier half of the standard (`_PRIVATE_PROJECT_NAME` plus two BMS repo names); no
platform name appeared in it at all. The guards were honest, they just answered a narrower question
than the file's docstring implies. Fixed by adding `_PRIVATE_PLATFORM_NAMES`, word-bounded, with a
positive control PER TOKEN so adding a name without a working pattern fails loudly.

A VACUOUS CONTROL I WROTE AND THEN CAUGHT, recorded because it is the more instructive half: my
first negative control proved the word boundary held using ordinary English — "first aid", "aiding",
"unaided", "mermaid", "AID_CODE". I sabotaged the boundary to check the control could fail, and it
PASSED. None of those strings contain the token at all, so the test asserted nothing about the
boundary. Replaced with strings where the boundary genuinely decides (`<token>s`, `plaid<token>`,
`my<token>thing` — each matches the bare token and not the bounded one), then re-sabotaged and
watched that exact test go red. Three sabotage runs total, each restore proven byte-identical by
checksum.

STILL OPEN, and it is the part that needs YOUR DECISION — the other platform name, 14 uses:
  src/ai_cli/config.py:260,262,263   the [<name>] section of the SHIPPED DEFAULT CONFIG TEMPLATE
  src/ai_cli/cc_usage.py x8          module docstring, config schema, error text, and the read:
                                     `config.get("<name>", {})` at :299
  src/ai_cli/quota.py:1183, tests/test_cc_usage.py:396,397

This is a config-section KEY read by that key, so renaming it is a public-API change: every existing
user config with that section silently stops being read, and the failure mode is a quiet "not
configured" rather than an error. The fleet's "no backward compat (pre-v1)" rule probably makes a
clean rename fine — but "probably" is not authority to break a shipped config key unasked.

ORDERING CONSTRAINT for whoever finishes this: adding that name to `_FORBIDDEN` turns the suite red
immediately, because 14 real uses remain. Do NOT add it with an exemption for the current set — an
exemption in this guard is precisely the hole this issue is about, and the guard's own docstring
explains why it avoids self-exclusions. Rename first, then extend the pattern, in one change or two
ordered ones.

GATE: ruff check "All checks passed!" · ruff format --check "92 files already formatted" (baseline on
pristine origin/main was 0 flagged, verified two-sided by stashing; the 2 files it initially flagged
were mine and are fixed) · pytest 2255 passed, 0 failed.

UNRELATED, SURFACED BY THE PUSH: GitHub reports 1 HIGH-severity Dependabot vulnerability on this
repo's default branch (alert 48). Not touched here — filed as AI-CLI-198.

CLOSED 2026-08-08. The rename shipped as `f77ae67` (`refactor(AI-CLI-189)!:` — note the `!`, correctly
marking a breaking change) plus `aa8f20a` for the guard, on origin/main. Section is now `[usage_api]`.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT with a positive control that could have failed: `src/ai_cli/config.py` on origin has
0 occurrences of the old name and 1 of `usage_api`; the pre-rename parent `71db600` still has 3. Same for
`cc_usage.py`. The read is a single clean `config.get("usage_api", {})` at :299 — **no dual-key fallback
anywhere**, which was the explicit requirement.

`[usage_api]` is a good choice: it names the ROLE (a REST endpoint usage events are POSTed to) rather than
a product, it matches the file's majority `snake_case` convention rather than the hyphenated form it
replaced, and it is obviously generic to an outside reader.

THE GUARD NOW CARRIES BOTH TOKENS: `_PRIVATE_PLATFORM_NAMES = ("ai" + "do", "ai-" + "core")`, still
assembled from fragments so the guard file does not itself contain the literals it forbids. Ordering was
respected — the token was added only after the rename was complete, so the suite never went red on real
violations, and no exemption list was introduced.

THE MIGRATION NOTE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, because one config was unverifiable from this machine.
CHANGELOG.md now carries a `Changed` entry that names BOTH sections, states that a populated old section
is "now simply ignored", tells the reader to rename that one header, quotes the exact failure text they
would otherwise see (`usage_api.api_url and usage_api.api_key must be set in config.toml under
[usage_api]`), and explicitly says a commented-out old block needs no action. A stranger with no access to
this conversation can act on it, which was the acceptance bar. README.md was updated too.

That note is what makes AI-CLI-199 actionable: it instructs a session on the user's Mac to grep its own
config and rename the header if populated, and it reads the CHANGELOG for the exact names.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN REVIEW, recorded because I nearly filed a false finding. I flagged that the entry
contains `AI-CLI-189` and that internal ids do not belong in a public repo. Measured before acting: the
CHANGELOG had **41** such ids at the parent and 42 after, so this is the file's established convention,
not a new leak — and `AI-CLI-N` is this repo's OWN public prefix, unlike the private fleet ids the rule
targets. The agent followed existing practice correctly. My grep for the note had also initially returned
nothing, which I read for a moment as the note being absent; the note was there and my pattern was too
narrow. Two probe errors in one review, both mine, neither the agent's.

WHY THE CLEAN BREAK WAS RIGHT, for the record: pre-v1 with a standing no-backward-compat rule; the only
config reachable from here had both keys commented out (untouched template default); and no
`cc-usage-cursor.json` existed anywhere, proving `cc-usage push` had never successfully run. The feature
was unexercised. A shim would have added a dual-path read to protect a configuration nobody was
demonstrably using.

WHAT I GOT WRONG EARLIER IN THIS ISSUE'S LIFE, worth keeping: my first framing to the user was "every
existing user config silently stops being read", which was mechanically true and materially misleading —
I described the failure mode without measuring how many configs were in the state that triggers it. The
user pushed back with "what does this risk breaking... I don't understand. elaborate", and the honest
answer after measuring was "in practice, nothing, and one machine remains unverified". Describe a blast
radius only after counting it.

STILL OPEN: AI-CLI-199, the machine-side check, with a real dep edge on this issue. It is the one gap this
shipped with, and it is a deliberate, documented gap rather than an unknown.
close_reason: Closed

title: `ai c 1` opens a FRESH conversation for aih-1: CC relocates an adopted transcript back out of its worktree slot when the session carries stale EnterWorktree state
description:
REPORTED BY THE USER 2026-08-07: "aih-1 cc session that i launched from `ai c 1` doesn't have any transcript history so i don't think your fix worked." Correct — the adoption did not hold. This has been confirmed to be a real regression of the adopted state, not a resume-lookup miss.

NO DATA WAS LOST. The conversation is intact: 14,226,464 bytes / 7,686 lines, customTitle `aih-1` on 348 records, at

  ~/.claude/projects/-<slug for the ai-harness REPO ROOT>/cb53b092-3c97-46a8-83e1-244293f0e608.jsonl

It is simply in the WRONG project directory. Fix the mechanism before moving it again, or the next `ai c 1` will move it straight back.

OBSERVED STATE (measured 2026-08-07 00:45 UTC)

`ai session-audit` currently reports aih-1 as `[repo-root, not-in-slot, NOT-resolvable]` and lists it under `Adoptable (1)`. So the tool is CORRECT and self-consistent; what is wrong is that a session recorded as adopted on 2026-08-06 is un-adopted again. (Note for anyone reading older notes: the claim that session-audit reports an EMPTY adoptable list is now STALE — it reports exactly one, and that one is this bug.)

  ~/.claude/projects/-<slug for ai-harness/.worktrees/aih-1>/   EXISTS and is EMPTY (0 files)
  ~/.claude/tasks/aih-1/                                        5 task json files, mtime 2026-08-06 07:58

So the task-namespace half of the adoption SURVIVED and the transcript half was reverted. That asymmetry is itself a clue: whatever undid it moved the transcript only.

THE DIFFERENTIAL THAT PINS IT

Four sessions were adopted in the same batch. Three hold; exactly one broke. The only structural difference between them is EnterWorktree history:

  session   worktree-state records   relocated records   adopted state
  aih-2     0                        0                   HOLDS
  acto-1    0                        0                   HOLDS
  kg-4      0                        0                   HOLDS
  aih-1     19                       20                  BROKE

aih-1 is the ONLY one of the four that ever ran `EnterWorktree`, and it is the ONLY one that came out of its slot. Its transcript carries:

  {"type":"worktree-state","worktreeSession":{
     "originalCwd":       ".../projects/ai-harness",
     "preEnterOriginalCwd": ".../projects/ai-harness",
     "worktreePath":      ".../projects/ai-harness/.claude/worktrees/aih-657-profile-correction",
     "worktreeBranch":    "worktree-aih-657-profile-correction",
     "originalBranch":    "main",
     "originalHeadCommit":"395f07945238bec87b2f3c52c7402a5442bb0557"}}

and its LAST THREE records, in order, are:

  {"type":"relocated","relocatedCwd":".../projects/ai-harness"}
  {"type":"worktree-state","worktreeSession":null}
  {"type":"relocated","relocatedCwd":".../projects/ai-harness"}

That is a worktree EXIT followed by a relocation to the ai-harness REPO ROOT — i.e. to `originalCwd`/`preEnterOriginalCwd` from the stale worktree-state, which is the main tree, NOT the adopted slot `.worktrees/aih-1`.

CORROBORATING TIMESTAMPS. The transcript's mtime is 2026-08-06 21:59:24.755 and the empty slot directory's mtime is 2026-08-06 21:59:24.735 — 20 ms apart, one operation. The adoption itself ran ~07:58 (see the surviving task namespace). So the revert happened ~14 hours after the adoption, at the moment a CC process touched this session, not during the adoption.

WORKING HYPOTHESIS (to be confirmed or refuted by AC-1, not assumed)

CC treats a transcript's project directory as a function of the session's CURRENT cwd, and moves the file between project directories when that cwd changes — that is what a `relocated` record is. On resuming aih-1, CC restores the recorded worktree session, exits it, and relocates the session to the `originalCwd` embedded in that stale worktree-state — the repo root. The transcript file is carried out of the adopted slot as a side effect. `ai c 1` then looks in the slot directory (which it computes from `$PWD`), finds no titled transcript, and starts a fresh conversation — exactly what the user saw.

If that is right, the defect is that adoption rewrites WHERE the transcript lives but not the session's own recorded idea of where it belongs, so CC's own relocation logic authoritatively undoes it. Adoption currently competes with CC for control of the file's location and loses.

BE SUSPICIOUS OF THIS HYPOTHESIS IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY: it predicts the user would have seen the OLD history (resumed, then relocated), whereas they report seeing NONE. Reconcile that before accepting it. Candidate reconciliations to test rather than assume: the relocation happens on startup before the conversation is presented; or `--continue` selected nothing because the slot directory was already empty and the fresh session's own transcript was subsequently relocated away too; or `ai c 1` launched with cwd = repo root rather than the slot. A hypothesis that cannot explain the user's actual symptom is not yet the root cause.

WHY THE OTHER THREE ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF CORRECTNESS. They hold because they have no worktree-state to restore, so nothing relocates them. Their passing is not a positive control for this mechanism — any fix must be proven against a session that CARRIES worktree-state, or the probe cannot come out the other way.

ALSO IN SCOPE: the same stale-state hazard applies to `ai c` generally, not only to adopted sessions. A session that ever ran EnterWorktree carries an absolute `worktreePath` under `.claude/worktrees/`; agent worktrees are transient and get cleaned up, so that path is routinely stale.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 The mechanism is ESTABLISHED EMPIRICALLY, with the probe recorded, before any fix is written. State which of the candidate reconciliations above is true, and quote the evidence. A fix built on the hypothesis as given, without confirming it, does not satisfy this AC.

AC-2 WHEN a session whose transcript carries worktree-state is adopted into `<repo>/.worktrees/<title>` and then resumed via `ai c <n>`, THEN it resumes the SAME conversation — the pre-existing history is present — and the transcript remains in the slot's project directory afterward.

AC-3 The adopted state is STABLE ACROSS REPEATED RESUMES: launching and exiting the adopted session twice in a row leaves the transcript in the slot both times. A single successful resume is not sufficient evidence, because the reverting write here happened on a resume, not on the adoption.

AC-4 FAILURE PATH — prove the fix can fail. Construct a session that carries worktree-state pointing at a worktree path that no longer exists, adopt it, resume it, and show the transcript does NOT leave the slot. Then show the SAME probe run against the unfixed code DOES move it. Both directions are required: a probe that only passes after the fix, without being shown to fail before it, does not establish anything.

AC-5 `ai session-audit` reports aih-1 as in-slot and resolvable after the repair, and continues to report the other ten sessions unchanged. Specifically it must NOT begin reporting a false "already adopted" for a session whose transcript has since been relocated away — the audit's in-slot test is a fact about where the file sits and must stay that way.

AC-6 No data loss path is introduced. The 14 MB transcript is the only copy of that conversation. Any move must copy-verify-then-remove, and any failure must leave a readable transcript at exactly one location.

AC-7 If CC's relocation cannot be prevented (i.e. adoption cannot win against it), then say so explicitly and change the approach rather than fighting it: either neutralise the stale worktree-state as part of adoption, or make resume tolerate a relocated transcript by locating it by TITLE across project directories instead of assuming the slot. Do not ship a fix that works only until CC next relocates the file.

AC-8 Regression test at the level the bug occurs. The existing suite passed while this was broken, so a test that only exercises adoption is inadequate — the test must cover the resume-after-adopt transition for a worktree-state-carrying session.

NOT IN SCOPE. Adopting the two live sessions (tracked separately, needs the user to exit them). Any change to how CC itself records worktree state.
close_reason: Fixed in 2badf59 + real aih-1 repair applied: 38 stale records cleared, transcript in-slot and resolvable, 7686 lines intact. Follow-ups AI-CLI-186/187 filed.

comments.author: Sergei Wallace
comments.text:
RESOLVED in 2badf59 (fix) + the real aih-1 repair applied 2026-08-07 02:00 UTC. Verified on origin by content.

ROOT CAUSE — the report's hypothesis was RIGHT about the mechanism and WRONG about the trigger, and the correction matters.

Claude Code's own relocation logic renames a transcript into the project directory of the session's CURRENT cwd. A session that ever entered a worktree mid-conversation carries a `worktree-state` record holding an absolute `originalCwd` — for an un-adopted session, the repo root. CC treats that as authoritative.

But relocation does NOT fire on resume. Resume only restores the binding; the rename fires on worktree EXIT, when CC returns the session to the recorded `originalCwd` and moves the transcript there. That refutes all three candidate reconciliations offered in the report, and it dissolves the report's own stated objection (that the hypothesis predicted the user would see OLD history rather than none). The real sequence: a prior session's worktree exit at 21:59 on 2026-08-06 had ALREADY moved the file out of the slot, so by the time `ai c 1` ran, the launcher's slot scan found an empty directory and took its fresh-`claude` branch. Nothing was resumed because there was nothing there to find.

Corroborated by the file's own timestamps: btime 2026-08-06 07:58:13 (the adoption) with mtime 21:59:24 — created by adoption, renamed away 14 hours later.

SECONDARY CAUSE. The migration's cwd rewrite only touched top-level `cwd`/`originalCwd` fields. The stale binding lives NESTED inside `worktreeSession`, so adoption never reached it — adoption moved the file while leaving intact the record that would move it back.

AC-7 IS THE OPERATIVE ONE. CC's relocation cannot be prevented, so the approach changed rather than fighting it: adoption now neutralises the stale binding. Every `worktree-state` record is rewritten to `worktreeSession: null` — byte-for-byte what CC itself writes on a clean exit, so resume reads it as "no worktree session active" — and every `relocated` stamp is repointed at the slot. Written to a sibling temp file and `os.replace`d, so an interrupted call leaves the original intact.

VERIFICATION I RAN MYSELF rather than taking the report on trust:

- Full suite 2191 passed, 0 failed. That reconciles with the sub-agent's 2187: it measured on a base predating the 4 guards from the lint-hook fix (2183 + 8 new = 2191). Comparing PASSED counts, not just failures, is what makes the two numbers agree instead of looking like a contradiction.
- MECHANICAL CHECK: disabled the fix in place (early `return 0`) and confirmed 6 of the 7 targeted tests go RED, including both resume-after-adopt tests and the interrupted-replace debris test. Restored it: 7 passed. The 7th test is the "transcript WITHOUT worktree-state → nothing changes" negative control, which correctly stays green in both states — a guard I had not watched fail would not have been evidence of anything.
- `ruff check` All checks passed; `ruff format --check` 90 files already formatted.
- MERGE HAZARD CAUGHT: the sub-agent branched from a6f4b0d, which predates the lint-hook commit, so its diff against current main showed my `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `tests/test_ruff_pin_integrity.py` changes as DELETIONS. Merging it would have silently reverted that fix. Cherry-picked the single commit onto current main instead, then verified on origin by content that both changes coexist (`--fix` absent AND `neutralise_worktree_state` present).

THE REAL REPAIR, applied after the fix was verified:
  38 stale record(s) cleared; 7686 lines, 5277 cwd rewrites; 10 memory files copied.
  Transcript now at the slot's project directory; the repo-root project directory holds no transcript.
  Integrity: 7686 lines before and after (backed up to a scratch copy first), title still `aih-1`, 1481 user turns intact.
  Post-repair state: 19 `worktree-state` records remain, 0 still carrying a live binding; 0 `relocated` stamps pointing anywhere but the slot.
  `ai session-audit` now reports aih-1 as `[session-worktree, in-slot, resolvable]`, an EMPTY adoptable list, and 11 skipped — the other ten unchanged (AC-5).

AC STATUS: AC-1 through AC-8 all MET. AC-6 (no data-loss path) holds: copy-verify-then-remove is unchanged, `os.replace` is atomic, and a failure-path test asserts the original survives with no debris.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED SEPARATELY, not silently absorbed:
1. Sessions adopted by the OLD code keep their stale binding, and there is no standalone repair command. The one known case (aih-1) is fixed by the re-adoption above; the general case is not.
2. The hazard is not specific to adopted sessions. Any session carrying a stale binding — including one that never needed adoption — will still relocate on worktree exit, because agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` are transient and their absolute paths go stale routinely.
3. Probes ran against CC 2.1.223 only. If a future CC version moves the rename into the resume path, this fix would no longer cover it.
4. `pytest-timeout` is declared in `[dependency-groups]`, NOT `[project.optional-dependencies]`, so `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` silently omits it; `uv sync --all-groups` is the path that installs it. Worth knowing before trusting a `--timeout` run in this repo.

STILL OPEN AND NOT ADDRESSED HERE: `ai c 1` has not yet been launched by the user against the repaired session. The machine-checkable state is correct and the resume probe passes, but the end-to-end confirmation is a human keypress.

title: Docs and memory assert ~/.local/share/uv is a cache, but it is the tool install dir — acting on it uninstalls the ai CLI
description:
A grep for the UV_CACHE_DIR environment variable name returns NOTHING on this machine, which reads as "the cache was never relocated". That is a FALSE NEGATIVE and acting on it is destructive.

The cache WAS relocated on 2026-07-28, by config file rather than env var. /home/sagemaker-user/.config/uv/uv.toml sets:

  cache-dir = "/home/sagemaker-user/user-default-efs/caches/uv"

Running "uv cache dir" confirms it resolves there, and that cache is a separate 3.1G living on EFS. That config file's own comment states why a config file was chosen over the env var: non-interactive and login shells do not source ~/.bashrc, so UV_CACHE_DIR alone left agent shells and hook subprocesses still writing into $HOME.

CONSEQUENCE. ~/.local/share/uv (1022M) therefore contains ZERO cache. It is:
  tools/  800M  -- aido 570M, ai-core 149M, ai-cli-utils 39M, copier 29M, pre-commit 15M
  python/ 223M  -- CPython 3.14.6 + 3.13.14, executed on every "uv run"

The 0-byte entries at ~/.local/bin/ai, aido, core, copier and pre-commit all point into tools/. So deleting ~/.local/share/uv, or relocating it to EFS, UNINSTALLS the ai CLI and every sibling tool. A disk-reclamation task nearly did exactly that on the strength of the false-negative grep.

This is the probe-adequacy failure mode in miniature: the grep RAN and returned cleanly, but it could not have come out the other way, because it looked in the wrong place. The check that actually distinguishes the two states is "uv cache dir", not a grep for the env var name.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
