AC-1 Every doc, memory file, or bead comment asserting that ~/.local/share/uv is a cache, is disposable, or that the uv cache relocation is still pending is corrected. Search at minimum ai-cli-utils docs/ plus MEMORY.md, ai-harness docs/ plus the machine profiles, and any disk or cleanup bead.

AC-2 The canonical way to locate the uv cache is recorded as "uv cache dir" (authoritative: it honors the config file, the env var, and the platform default), with an explicit note that grepping for UV_CACHE_DIR is NOT sufficient, and why.

AC-3 ~/.local/share/uv is added to whatever do-not-delete list the fleet keeps for this machine, with the reason recorded (live tool installs; deleting it uninstalls the ai CLI).

AC-4 If any automated cleanup script or documented cleanup step targets ~/.local/share/uv, it is fixed or removed.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 by the AI-CLI-173 disk analysis, which also found that the disk premise itself had expired: the home volume was resized from 5G to 100G and now reports 6% used with 95G free. Full write-up in sw-bms-workspace at docs/analysis/sagemaker-space-disk-pressure.md, commit b859be8.
close_reason: Fixed in 27a549c (merge of e53e9bf). Adds docs/procedures/uv-disk-usage-troubleshooting.md recording the three-directory structure (cache on EFS via ~/.config/uv/uv.toml, tools, interpreters), `uv cache dir` as the only reliable locator, and why grepping UV_CACHE_DIR is a false negative -- non-interactive and login shells never source ~/.bashrc, which is exactly why the config-file form was chosen on 2026-07-28. AC-1 audit was largely a CLEAN NEGATIVE and that is the useful finding: the two existing mentions (main.py tools-dir fallback comment, uv-hardlink bug doc) were already accurate, and no script, Makefile or documented cleanup step targets ~/.local/share/uv. The gap was missing guidance, not wrong code. Verified myself rather than from the agent report: 2112 passed / 0 failed, 221 hygiene+guard tests pass on the new doc, and the diff adds ZERO machine-specific paths or private tool names (checked, since the finding originated on a private machine and this is a public package). Nothing under ~/.local/share/uv or ~/.config/uv was modified.

title: 14 display IDs are double-allocated across two machines, so the dual-ID precommit gate blocks every .beads commit
description:
Blocks every commit that stages .beads/issues.jsonl in this repo. Surfaced 2026-08-05 while fixing the store/JSONL drift (AI-CLI-u9x / AI-CLI-fcl).

POSITIVE CONTROL, so this is not a new regression: the committed file at HEAD (43a6dab) already violates the invariant once, on AI-CLI-160 (AI-CLI-fae and AI-CLI-w4p both claim it). Resolving the drift raised the export from 158 to 172 records, which exposed 14 more. Counts: HEAD 158 records / 1 collision; post-reconciliation 172 records / 15 collisions.

ROOT CAUSE. bd-new serializes allocation with an flock on .beads/.displayid.lock and computes max(N)+1 from existing external_ref values. Both halves are per-store, so while this machine's Dolt store was diverged from the tracked JSONL, each machine computed max(N)+1 over a DIFFERENT record set and handed out the same N. The lock did its job; the input to max() was wrong. Every collision is one store-only issue against one JSONL-only issue, which is exactly the signature of two independent allocators, not of a lock race.

The collisions, AI-CLI-143 through 156 plus 160:
  143  urv (store-only)  vs 6tq (in HEAD)
  144  udn (store-only)  vs 7id
  145  v0u (store-only)  vs u9x
  146  n20 (store-only)  vs xnn
  147  vs8 (store-only)  vs z90
  148  v1t (store-only)  vs imn
  149  aq0 (store-only)  vs mda
  150  i0k (store-only)  vs lk8
  151  oea (store-only)  vs 50l
  152  2ff (store-only)  vs bc3
  153  fcl (store-only)  vs 70q
  154  8v4 (store-only)  vs oa8
  155  1db (store-only)  vs d2p
  156  b01 (store-only)  vs k1u
  160  fae             vs w4p   (pre-existing at HEAD)

WHY THIS WAS NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS. The gate prints a ready-made repair, bd update <id> --external-ref=AI-N --add-label=id:AI-N. Do not run it as printed: it hand-assigns display IDs, which the fleet rule forbids, and it invents a NEW prefix (AI- instead of AI-CLI-), so it would introduce a second ID namespace in this repo rather than repair the first. Choosing which side of each pair keeps its number is also not mechanical, because several of these IDs are already cited in commit messages and docs, so renumbering the wrong side silently invalidates those references.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 Every external_ref in .beads/issues.jsonl is unique, and ~/.claude/bin/bd-precommit-validate passes on the staged file.
AC-2 For each of the 15 pairs, the side that keeps the number is the one already referenced in a commit message, doc, or plan; the other is renumbered above the current max. Record the decision per pair.
AC-3 Renumbering goes through the sanctioned path and keeps the AI-CLI- prefix; no hand-assigned IDs, no second prefix namespace.
AC-4 The id:PREFIX-N label and external_ref stay in agreement on every renumbered issue (bdx resolves both).
AC-5 A regression check that would have caught this: assert uniqueness of external_ref across the store AND the tracked JSONL, not just within whichever one is being written.
AC-6 The allocator no longer computes max(N)+1 from a single possibly-diverged source. Either reconcile before allocating or derive the ceiling from the union of store and tracked JSONL.

RELATED. Same defect class as ai-harness AIH-tpdl (22 duplicate display IDs in that store) and AIH-owd8 (the display-ID lock racing under concurrent sessions). AC-6 is the shared fix; the fleet-wide sweep belongs with those.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in cda2d76. Adjudicated all 15 pairs from commit evidence rather than preference: 11 IDs stayed with the side already cited in a commit message or doc, and the 4 uncited pairs kept the older record. The other side of each pair was renumbered 162-176 under the .displayid.lock flock, keeping the AI-CLI- prefix. Did NOT use the repair the gate prints, which hand-assigns under a different prefix (AI-N) and would have opened a second ID namespace. Verified on origin/main by content: 173 records, 0 duplicate external_refs, 0 external_ref/label disagreements, no non-id labels destroyed. bd dual-ID precommit gate now PASSES. Root cause (bd-new computes max(N)+1 per store, so a diverged store yields a duplicate N) is the shared fix with AIH-tpdl/AIH-owd8 and stays open there.

title: test_given_stale_quota_cache_when_run_then_ai_statusline_part_called fails deterministically on main
description:
tests/test_quota.py::TestStatuslineScript::test_given_stale_quota_cache_when_run_then_ai_statusline_part_called FAILS on main:
  AssertionError: ai quota statusline-part should be called as a background refresh when cache is stale (>30s)
  assert False  where False = PosixPath('/tmp/.../ai_statusline_called').exists()

Reproduced in isolation (single test, -p no:randomly): 1 failed. So it is deterministic here, not an ordering artifact — though it may still be environment-sensitive (the test relies on a backgrounded refresh completing within a 1.5s sleep, which is timing-dependent by construction).

NOT caused by the uv --link-mode work (AI-CLI-148): the test's only external surfaces are PATH, a fake 'ai' shell shim, TMPDIR and the sentinel file — it never touches uv or the install path. Verified by reading the test body.

Contributes to the pre-push gate being red (4 failures on main: this one, the hygiene leak, and two uv-argv assertions already fixed).

INVESTIGATE: whether the stale-while-revalidate background refresh actually fires on this platform (the statusline script may spawn it in a way that does not survive, or the 1.5s window is too short under load), and whether the test should poll with a timeout instead of a fixed sleep. A fixed sleep in a concurrency assertion is the same wall-clock-dependence class as AI-CLI-158.
close_reason: Fixed in 4268f62: root cause was NOT a sleep race or lock file (both hypotheses refuted by a pristine-TMPDIR probe) — the test inherited an ambient CC_BILLING_MODE=api, which routes the statusline script down the cache-hit branch so the quota code never ran and the sentinel was never touched. Billing mode is now pinned in the test environment. Same ambient-process-state class as the GIT_DIR leak (AIH-353).

title: CC task namespace: writes land in an unrelated session-<hash> dir and completed tasks vanish, so namespace recovery cannot work
description:
MEASURED (2026-08-05, ai-cli-1 session, this machine):
- This session created 2 CC tasks and updated them 6 times. A content grep for their subjects across ALL of ~/.claude/tasks returned NOTHING.
- ~/.claude/tasks/session-f5b6cafa/ (matching this session's transcript UUID f5b6cafa-bc9e-455e-a6f3-89ab8ea02f98) EXISTS but holds 0 files.
- The only namespace written in the last 40 min is ~/.claude/tasks/session-c00b86c4/ — and its 4 tasks are kg-1's (KG-156..KG-159), not this session's.
- 814 namespace dirs exist; 795 (97.7%) hold zero json files.
- CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID is UNSET in this session (it is only exported by 'ai c <n>' launches, ai-cli-utils commit 9ada6d0), so this session is transcript-keyed.

TWO DISTINCT SYMPTOMS, both need root-causing (do not assume one cause):
(a) Completed tasks appear to be pruned from disk. The /task-panel recovery procedure greps for status pending/in_progress, so a cleanly-completed session leaves an EMPTY namespace and recovery finds nothing. If pruning is intended, the recovery procedure's premise is wrong and must be rewritten; if not, it is data loss.
(b) A namespace's name does not reliably correspond to the session that writes it. session-f5b6cafa exists-but-empty while an unrelated session-c00b86c4 receives writes. Determine what actually derives the key (CC internal, not documented in our skill) before proposing any fix.

CONSEQUENCE: the /task-panel skill's orphan-recovery path (~/.claude/skills/task-panel, steps 3a-3f) cannot recover this session's tasks after a crash — verified live today. It also risks adopting ANOTHER session's tasks: the only recoverable candidates on this machine carry kg-* and SageMaker-infra subjects.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this is CC-harness behavior, not necessarily an ai-cli-utils defect. The fix may be (1) always pin CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID rather than only via 'ai c', (2) correct the /task-panel skill's documented premise, (3) an upstream CC report, or some combination. Root-cause FIRST; do not implement before the mechanism is established. Verify claims against CC's actual behavior rather than our skill's description of it — the skill has already been shown wrong here.

Blocks the CC-task-migration step of AI-CLI-149 (session-adopt): moving task files is meaningless until it is known where CC actually reads them from.
close_reason: Root-caused: TWO independent Claude Code harness defects (2.1.222), neither an ai-cli-utils bug. (1) A 5s-debounced sweeper deletes every task file in a namespace once ALL its tasks are 'completed', writing the highest id to .highwatermark first. Proven by that ledger: independently re-verified 10/10 .highwatermark files exist iff the id sequence has a gap, each value == highest missing id; negative control = ZERO of 814 namespaces retain an all-completed set; 15 completed tasks DO survive, all in namespaces that also hold an open task. So completion alone does not delete — the all-completed condition does. (2) The namespace key is the active TEAM name (per-process, regenerated every start incl. --continue), not the transcript UUID — one transcript spread tasks over 4 namespaces. This session's own session-f5b6cafa has hw=4 with zero files, explaining the original report exactly. CONSEQUENCE: /task-panel orphan recovery is structurally broken (its live-exclusion step names 2 non-live namespaces, excludes neither live one, and selects a LIVE session's dir). NO code fix needed here: ai-cli-utils already pins CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, the highest-precedence resolver branch and a complete mitigation; the reporting session simply was not launched via 'ai c'. Doc: docs/bugs/cc-task-namespace-persistence.md (BUG-011). Commit 4268f62. NOT established: whether the wipe is intentional (undocumented is proven, 'bug' is not); the no-teams fallback path; single host/version only.

title: ai session-adopt: adopt a non-ai-c CC session into a worktree — transcript, tasks, memory, and worktree creation in one validated command
description:
Extends the shipped 'ai cc-migrate' (AI-CLI-144, transcript-only) into a full session-adoption command so any CC session started WITHOUT 'ai c' can be resumed by 'ai c <n>' from the right repo, losing nothing.

MEASURED CURRENT STATE (2026-08-05, this machine):
- 187 transcripts total, only 11 titled. Titled sessions and their cwd:
    kg-1     64.67 MB / 20068 lines  -> kg repo ROOT (needs worktree .worktrees/kg-1)   [LIVE, do last]
    aih-1    14.23 MB /  7683 lines  -> ai-harness ROOT (needs worktree)
    aido-1    7.79 MB /  4695 lines  -> already in .worktrees/aido-1 (OK)
    kg-2       7.28 MB / 3017 lines  -> already in .worktrees/kg-2 (OK)
    kg-3       5.90 MB / 2708 lines  -> already in .worktrees/kg-3 (OK)
    ai-cli-1   4.78 MB / 2440 lines  -> ai-cli-utils ROOT (needs worktree)             [LIVE, do last]
    aih-2      2.86 MB / 1297 lines  -> ai-harness ROOT (needs worktree)
    acto-1     1.57 MB /  837 lines  -> acto ROOT (needs worktree)
    kg-3       0.83 MB /  419 lines  -> kg repo ROOT (DUPLICATE title vs the worktree kg-3 — the fail-loudly case)
    aih-3      0.79 MB /  398 lines  -> already in .worktrees/aih-3 (OK)
    proj-1     0.53 MB /  232 lines  -> ~/projects (not a repo; surface for a decision)
- Untitled transcripts >1MB: ZERO. All 176 untitled are <1MB and are pytest sandboxes / /tmp probes — per Sergei, not worth migrating.
- Only kg-1 (pid 2855875) and ai-cli-1 (pid 2923882) are live processes.

SCOPE — one command, must handle:
1. Worktree: create the target worktree if absent (off fresh origin/main, per the repo's own convention); if it already exists, USE it. Never clobber.
2. Duplicate-title collision (the real 'kg-3' case above): a transcript at the repo root sharing a customTitle with one already in the target worktree must FAIL LOUDLY and present options (retitle + adopt to a new index, keep-both, skip), never silently pick one. 'ai c' resolves by first customTitle, so a duplicate makes resume nondeterministic.
3. Transcript: reuse cc_migrate.migrate_session (already verifies line count before deleting the source; preserves mtime).
4. CC tasks: move/merge ~/.claude/tasks/<old-ns>/*.json into the pinned namespace (~/.claude/tasks/<ai_name>/). IDs are namespace-scoped, so a merge must not clobber an existing N.json — renumber and report. NOTE: depends on the namespace-persistence defect filed separately.
5. Memory: ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ — cc_migrate deliberately skips this because other sessions may share the source root. Adoption must handle it explicitly (copy vs move vs merge) with a stated rule, not silence.
6. Anything else keyed by the project slug rather than the session UUID — inventory it first and state what is intentionally left alone (UUID-keyed state is unaffected by design).

REQUIREMENTS: dry-run default or a mandatory --dry-run/-n preview; per-session validation with a probe that can fail (post-adopt, assert 'ai c <n>' actually resolves that transcript); idempotent (re-running adopts nothing); refuses to touch a LIVE session (check /proc for the pid in ~/.claude/sessions/*.json) — kg-1 and ai-cli-1 must be rejected while running; bulk mode over all titled sessions with a per-session skip/continue; both short and long option forms (repo CLI convention).

PRECONDITION: /home/sagemaker-user is at 87% of 5.0G (660M free) and kg-1's transcript alone is 64MB. A copy-then-verify adoption doubles a transcript transiently, so the command must check free space before writing and fail cleanly rather than ENOSPC mid-write (an ENOSPC here corrupts the transcript being migrated).

DOC: a procedure doc covering the whole flow so this is repeatable by hand if the command is unavailable.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-05 (Sergei) — duplicate-title collision handling is RETITLE-TO-FREE-INDEX, and it is ALWAYS a hard human gate.

Required behavior for the collision case (the real kg-3 instance: a 0.83 MB transcript titled 'kg-3' at the kg repo root vs the 5.90 MB one already in .worktrees/kg-3):
1. DETECT the collision before touching anything and STOP. Never auto-resolve, never pick by size/mtime, never silently skip. Exit non-zero with the two candidates printed (title, size, line count, cwd, mtime) so the human can tell them apart.
2. OFFER retitle-to-free-index as the primary remedy: compute the lowest unused index for that repo's prefix (scan existing customTitles + existing worktrees so the chosen index collides with neither), and show the exact proposed new title.
3. REQUIRE explicit human confirmation of the new index before writing. A --yes/-y style blanket confirm must NOT cover this case: the gate is unconditional even in --all/bulk mode, which should pause on the collision, report it, and continue with the remaining sessions rather than aborting the batch.
4. Retitle means rewriting the customTitle records in the transcript (the resume path matches on the FIRST titled record — see cc_migrate.transcript_title) and adopting into the worktree for the NEW index. Verify post-adopt that 'ai c <new-index>' resolves the retitled transcript and 'ai c <old-index>' still resolves the original.

Suggested surface: -c/--on-collision {gate,retitle} defaulting to 'gate', plus -T/--new-title TITLE and -I/--new-index N to supply the human's answer non-interactively on a second invocation. Keep both short and long forms per repo convention. Do NOT add a 'force'/'auto' collision mode — the gate is the requirement, not a default.
close_reason: SHIPPED 2026-08-06 as commit 93685ec: src/ai_cli/session_adopt.py (784 lines), tests/test_session_adopt.py (999 lines), docs/tools/cc-session-adoption.md. 2112 passed / 0 failed, 100% coverage on session_adopt.py, no pragma. Proven in real use: all four non-live adoptions (aih-1, aih-2, acto-1, kg-3-root to kg-4) completed via this command, and its unconditional title-collision gate correctly refused the kg-3 duplicate and proposed a free index. The one remaining open item — the live-session refusal being proven with os.getpid() rather than a real CC process — is split out as AI-CLI-181 so it keeps its own identity rather than holding this closed-outcome issue open.

title: Re-verify AI-CLI-99's core.bare=true corruption fix is still holding fleet-wide
description: AI-CLI-99 (fixed 2026-07-13, per ai-harness memory note ai-harness-main-tree-never-bare.md) root-caused a real corruption class: GIT_* env (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/etc) leaking from a CC worktree session into git subprocesses in session_script.py/copier_update.py, which then wrote core.bare=true (+ a stale core.worktree pointing at a .worktrees/* sibling) onto a repo's SHARED .git/config -- corrupting every session on the main path with 'fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree'. Fixed via a GIT_* env-scrub + a deterministic repair guard at 'ai c' launch. Originally tracked only as CC task #63 (subject named a bd issue, AIH-353, that does not exist in this or the ai-harness store -- confirmed via bd search, genuine drift, not a lookup error). No bd issue previously existed for this re-verification ask. Needs: (1) confirm the env-scrub + repair-guard code is still present and unregressed in session_script.py/copier_update.py, (2) empirically check a sample of live repos/worktrees on this machine for an incorrectly-set core.bare=true, (3) if the corruption has recurred anywhere, root-cause why the fix didn't hold and file/fix accordingly.
close_reason: Re-verified via Codex implement (gpt-5.6-terra, medium effort): HOLDING. _git_env() still strips all 9 git-targeting env vars (git_repair.py:81-106), every git subprocess in the module passes env=_git_env(), repair_bare_worktree_config() backstop intact (git_repair.py:120-156). Read-only fleet check across 21 repos found zero instances of core.bare=true or a nonempty core.worktree. This repo itself: core.bare=false, no core.worktree, clean tree. Focused regression suite (test_git_repair.py) passed 8/8. One caveat: live origin/main verification was blocked by a transient DNS failure in the sandbox, so this is confirmed against cached/local state, not a fresh network fetch -- re-check if network issues are suspected separately. Replaces the dangling CC task #63 reference to a nonexistent AIH-353.

title: ai c derives wrong prefix for worktrees, session titles and beads ids -- registry never populated
description:
`ai c` derives the wrong prefix for worktrees, session titles, and beads ids because the project registry is never populated on a new machine.

SYMPTOM: a worktree named `wt-ai-1` in ai-cli-utils. The correct prefix is the project's registered alias (AI-CLI, matching its beads prefix), not `ai`. Sergei reported it 2026-08-03 on bms-windows-sem-kg.

ROOT CAUSE, verified rather than assumed:
- ai-cli's config on this machine resolves to C:/Users/wallas12/AppData/Roaming/ai-cli-utils/config.toml (get_xdg_config_home(), NOT ~/.config/ai-cli -- worth knowing, since looking in the POSIX location shows nothing and reads as "no config at all").
- That file exists but is the UNTOUCHED DEFAULT TEMPLATE: `main_project` is still commented out under [project], and there is no project registry section with per-project prefixes.
- config.py load_config() writes DEFAULT_CONFIG on first use and never registers anything, so a fresh machine gets a config that parses fine and carries no project mappings. Nothing prompts, nothing fails.

WHY `wt-ai-1` SPECIFICALLY: `ai-cli-utils`[:3] == `ai`. That is the cwd-derived fallback AI-CLI-88 was closed for removing (`cwd.name[:3]`, the 'myproject'-style ghost session). Either the fallback survives on a path AI-CLI-88 did not cover, or a second copy of that logic exists for WORKTREE naming while AI-CLI-88 only fixed SESSION resolution. Determine which before fixing -- if it is the latter, the same latent bug affects every repo and AI-CLI-88 should not have been closed as fully fixed.

SCOPE OF THE FIX:
1. Establish correct prefixes for every repo root Sergei launches sessions from, at minimum: ai-harness (AIH), ai-cli-utils (AI-CLI), ai-core (CORE), aido (AIDO), bms-semantic-knowledge-graph (KG), sw-bms-workspace (KG -- note it HOSTS the KG store for the semantic-kg work, so decide deliberately whether these two share a prefix or need distinct ones; today both use KG).
2. Make the prefix ONE source of truth used by all three consumers -- git worktree names, CC session custom titles, and beads display-id prefixes. They currently disagree, which is why a `wt-ai-1` worktree can coexist with an AI-CLI beads store.
3. AUTO-CONFIGURE ON A NEW MACHINE. This is the durable half: a fresh machine must arrive with the registry populated, not with a default template. AI-CLI-62 (open, P1, "Proactive project registry registration") already proposes `ai register --project --prefix --type`, registry opt-in, and a self-describing `[tool.ai-cli]` block in pyproject.toml -- that is the right mechanism; this issue is the concrete driver for it. Wire it into machine provisioning (ai-harness install.sh / scripts/bootstrap) so it is not a manual step.
4. FAIL LOUDLY rather than guessing. Any unresolvable prefix should error with the remedy, never silently truncate a directory name -- the AI-CLI-88 principle, applied to worktree and title derivation too.

Related: AI-CLI-62 (the mechanism), AI-CLI-88 (closed, same class of bug, may be incompletely fixed), AI-CLI-103 (expand config.toml coverage). Cross-repo: ai-harness AIH-604 / AIH-606 cover provisioning and the folded-in bootstrap that should carry this registration.

Also pending: delete the stray `wt-ai-1` worktree once it is confirmed merged and pushed (hard human gate per ai-harness AIH-603 R8).
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-08 as fixed by the AI-CLI-195 work (fc6ec0d + 537d51d4), which addressed the SAME
root cause this issue diagnosed: the project registry was never populated, so resolution had no data.
This issue reported the bms-windows face of it (a worktree named `wt-ai-1`, from `ai-cli-utils`[:3]);
AI-CLI-195 reported the sem-kg face (a hard "No task prefix is registered" error). One cause, two
symptoms, one fix.

VERIFIED AGAINST THIS ISSUE'S OWN TWO CLAIMS rather than by assuming the sibling fix covered it:

1. THE cwd-DERIVED FALLBACK IS GONE FROM RESOLUTION. `grep -rn '\[:3\]' src/ai_cli/` returns only
   two unrelated hits — a conflict-summary join in sync.py:1454 and a body preview in
   handoff.py:156. Neither is a prefix derivation. This issue's open question was whether the
   fallback AI-CLI-88 was closed for removing had survived on some path; it has not.

2. NO TIER DERIVES A PREFIX FROM THE DIRECTORY NAME, and `resolve_project_prefix`'s docstring now
   says so explicitly, citing both AI-CLI-88 and this issue by id: "no tier derives a prefix from
   the directory name, because a truncated guess mints task ids against the wrong project". The
   tier chain is persistent fleet registry -> `[project] main_project` registry -> XDG
   `[project_registry]` -> the repo's own `[tool.ai-cli]` metadata -> an interactive prompt that
   persists what it is told. An unresolvable prefix stays a LOUD failure naming the remedy, which is
   the correct behaviour: this issue's real complaint was that a silent wrong answer is worse than
   an error, and it now errors.

WHAT MADE THIS FAMILY CONFUSING, worth keeping: the config file resolved through
`get_xdg_config_home()`, which on Windows is `C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/ai-cli-utils/
config.toml` — NOT `~/.config/ai-cli`. Looking in the POSIX location showed nothing and read as "no
config at all", when in fact a config existed and was simply the untouched default template. A
lookup pointed at the wrong location produces evidence indistinguishable from absence.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: the bms-windows machine itself. The fix's persistent tier is found by SHAPE
(`<repo>/config/fleet-projects.toml` under the projects dir) and ships 13 entries in
version control, so it should resolve identically there without per-machine setup — but that is
reasoning, not a measurement, and this box is sem-kg-sagemaker. If `wt-ai-1`-style naming recurs on
bms-windows after an `ai update`, reopen rather than filing fresh.
close_reason: Closed

title: test_weekly_pace_shown_as_magnitude_color_encodes_direction is non-hermetic — calls real datetime.now() before its own time-mock, fails intermittently, blocks all pushes
description:
Found 2026-08-02 ~19:00 EDT while pushing an unrelated history-linearization fix to main.

tests/test_quota.py's _capture() helper (used by this test) calls
qdb._get_current_week_start() to establish week_start_str BEFORE entering the
with patch("datetime.datetime") block that mocks "now" for the rest of the test.
_get_current_week_start() falls back to datetime.now(timezone.utc) when no now
argument is passed (quota_db.py:191-198), so the anchor week boundary the test
computes its "fixed" 161-hours-elapsed offset from is itself derived from REAL
wall-clock time, not a fixed point.

test_weekly_pace_shown_as_magnitude_color_encodes_direction expects "17% usage,
161h elapsed (~96% of week) -> -79% delta" but got -76% at measurement time --
consistent with the real "current week" boundary shifting the effective elapsed
fraction depending on when the test actually runs, despite the test author's intent
that hours_elapsed=161 be a fully fixed synthetic scenario.

Impact: this makes the test flaky against real time rather than fully hermetic, and
since it runs in the repo's local pre-push test-gate hook, a failure here blocks
ALL pushes to ai-cli-utils main -- not just ones touching quota code -- until either
real time drifts back into the window the hardcoded expected values assume, or the
test is fixed.

Fix direction (not yet investigated in depth): either pass a fixed now into
_get_current_week_start() inside _capture() so the whole scenario is deterministic,
or change the test's assertions to compute their expected percentages from the same
_get_current_week_start()-derived boundary the code under test uses, rather than a
hardcoded "79%"/"~96%" comment-derived constant.
close_reason: Fixed: _capture() now passes a fixed reference instant into _get_current_week_start() instead of falling back to real datetime.now(). Commit cc77f79 (ai-cli-utils main). Full suite verified green (2009 passed) before push.

title: [bug] NATS handoff payload writes unvalidated filename/content into the queue dir (path traversal + untrusted payload)
description: In _on_handoff_signal_watch and _write_pending_if_claimed_drain (src/ai_cli/main.py), 'filename' and 'content' from the NATS payload are written to pending_dir/filename without validation: a crafted filename escapes the queue dir (path traversal), and content is written verbatim (untrusted payload later injected into a session prompt). Fix independently of the v2 design: derive the filename locally from id+slug pattern, schema-validate payload fields, reject non-conforming messages, log rejects. Failure-path tests required.
notes: Plan confirmed: this vulnerability closes as a byproduct of full handoff retirement (AI-CLI-archive-retire-exjn), not a standalone fix. Close only once the vulnerable NATS write paths are confirmed removed/unreachable -- do not close on plan alone.

title: Handoff v2 Phase 2: hook-based delivery (Stop/UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart); retire restart-based delivery and pre-claim
description: Implement Phase 2 of docs/designs/cross-session-handoff.md: per-session Stop + UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart hook pickup (bounded, idempotent, 2s budget, exit-0 on failure), claim moved to pickup time; retire signal-watch pre-claim and exit-signal restart delivery (parity inventory in doc). Race-safe hook registration against shared settings. Full EARS ACs in the design doc Phase 2.

title: Handoff v2 Phase 1: queue integrity + observability (leases, reconciler, dead-letter, lifecycle events, ID serialization, machine targeting)
description: Implement Phase 1 of docs/designs/cross-session-handoff.md: lifecycle event logging on every claim/complete path, lease fields (lease_expires_at, attempt, schema_version) + reconciler returning expired claims to pending, dead-letter/ dir after max_attempts, serialized ID assignment (O_EXCL lock), for_machine filtering in claim_handoff/check_handoff/_find_best_handoff, migration handling for existing lease-less claimed files. Full EARS ACs in the design doc Phase 1.

title: ai c N session launcher does not auto-connect Remote Control — the GrowthBook pre-toggle isn't producing a working zero-touch reconnect in practice
description:
Sergei reports (2026-08-01) that new CC sessions launched via 'ai c N' do NOT start out Remote-Control-connected — he still has to manually run the /rc-pair skill every time. This is the opposite of the intended behavior: ai-harness's AIH-352 design (docs/designs/aih-352-remote-control-growthbook-session-toggle.md, D-1 option (d)) specifies that the launcher writes 'env.DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK: ""' into .claude/settings.local.json BEFORE 'claude' starts, so that 'remoteControlAtStartup: true' can do its normal zero-touch auto-reconnect for a worktree that was already Remote-Control-paired before.

Known relevant prior state in this repo (verify current, don't trust blindly — this is from ai-harness's own bd store / CC task panel, may be stale):
- src/ai_cli/session_script.py and tests/test_growthbook_launch_toggle.py both reference DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK/remoteControlAtStartup/the ai-cli-growthbook-toggle marker already — so SOME implementation exists.
- ai-harness's own docket references a CC task 'AIH-352: flip to default-on for all repos/worktrees/CC sessions (no opt-in marker)' and a separate 'AIH-352: live UAT of Phase 5 automatic restore, then re-land ai-cli-utils@1167672' — implying a specific commit (short hash 1167672) was built, possibly reverted pending live UAT, and may or may not have been re-landed since. Check git log for that hash and its current status in this repo's history.
- ai-harness's docs/bugs/aih-441-rc-pair-false-restored-on-signal.md documents at least one previously-found-and-fixed bug in this same mechanism ('AIH-441, level-vs-edge in wait_for_autorestore_gate') — read it for context on what's already been debugged and fixed once.
- ai-harness's rc-pair skill (~/.claude/skills/rc-pair/SKILL.md) is the manual fallback/visibility layer for this same mechanism and documents the intended two-path design (manual /rc tap vs. a restart that should auto-reconnect via the launcher's pre-toggle) — useful for understanding what 'working' looks like from the CC session side.

This needs investigation to determine whether: (a) the launcher-side toggle write never actually lands before 'claude' starts (a sequencing bug), (b) it lands but the '.ai-cli-growthbook-toggle' opt-in marker Sergei's worktrees need isn't actually present/being checked correctly, (c) the commit implementing 'default-on for all repos/worktrees/CC sessions' was never actually merged/released despite the CC task marking it as done work, or (d) something else entirely. Root-cause via /bug-fix discipline (reproduce, root-cause, regression test, fix, verify, document per docs/procedures/root-cause-and-fix.md in ai-harness) rather than guessing a patch.
close_reason: Root-caused: the launcher's pre-launch DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK write was gated on .claude/.ai-cli-growthbook-toggle, a marker file confirmed absent fleet-wide (find across ~/projects found zero instances). That gate was restored by a same-day, unexplained revert (bc056a8) of an earlier unconditional-write commit (1167672); the automatic-restore mechanism the revert was protecting against is separately fixed now. Fixed by removing the marker predicate (session_script.py); frozen regression test flips the old test that had encoded the bug as expected behavior (RED confirmed via git-stash verification, GREEN after). Full suite: 2009 passed, independently re-run (not trusted from the delegated agent's own sandbox-limited report). Bug doc: docs/bugs/remote-control-launch-override-marker.md (BUG-009). Commit 3254431, pushed.

description:

   src/ai_cli/sync.py:211 — docstring example: "sergei--worktrees-sw-5" -> "sw-5", "sergei" -> None
   tests/test_session.py:1291,1297,1298 — AI_TMUX_SESSION "c-sergei-1"; get_current_project_name -> "sergei"; registry [{"name": "sergei"}]
   tests/test_config_watch_hash.py:11,60 — project_name="sergei", plus a comment citing private cross-repo commit SHAs
   tests/test_growthbook_launch_toggle.py:77 — project_name="sergei"
   tests/test_runaway_loop_guards.py:45,142 — project_name="sergei"
   Plus ~20 docs/ files (207 total occurrences of the string repo-wide).

   "bms-semantic-knowledge-graph" (7 occurrences) and "sw-bms-workspace" (8), including
   absolute EFS paths. Authored 2026-07-28 in this session; the rule was known and missed.

IMPORTANT SCOPE BOUNDARY — do not over-fix:
README.md occurrences of "sergei" are the LEGITIMATE GitHub org/URL
(github.com/sergeiwallace/ai-cli-utils, CI/codecov badge URLs). Those are correct and MUST
be left alone. The violation is "sergei" used as a stand-in PROJECT NAME, not the account
name in a real repository URL. Any bulk find-and-replace will break the badges and the

myapp, session-1, test-session, example.com, user.

legitimate URL usage from project-name usage. Control-test whatever pattern is used
(confirm it flags a known-bad line AND does not flag the README badge URLs) before
reporting the repo clean.

Full suite must stay green: baseline 1965 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed. Several tests pass

title: Auto-update stamp is written before the update runs, latching a failed host behind forever

comments.author: T
comments.text:
Found while root-causing AI-CLI-132 (stranded autostash); deliberately NOT fixed there because it needs its own design.

`_auto_update_if_stale` (src/ai_cli/main.py) writes its stamp file keyed on the CURRENT HEAD *before* running `ai update --force`. If the update cannot advance HEAD, the early-return then matches that same hash forever and auto-update never retries.

Measured live on the remote build host: stamp file and HEAD were both 4711d4e, and the host had not auto-updated for five days.

AI-CLI-132 removes the way HEAD gets frozen in the first place, so this is no longer reachable by that route — but the latch itself is still there for any other cause of a failed update.

NOT a one-line move of the write. Writing the stamp only on success means every subsequent `ai` invocation retries a failing update, which is presumably why it was written this way. Needs a real retry policy (backoff, attempt counter, or stamp-on-attempt plus a separate success marker).

title: Guard the harm, not the cause: block commits that delete files still live on origin/main
description:
AIH-443's genesis is still unknown after three investigations. This issue stops arguing with that and closes the damage path instead.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:
- Shape A: git-tracked symlinks a sub-agent checkout never materialized.
- Shape B: 'git pull --rebase --autostash' exiting 0 after its stash pop conflicted.
- Shape C: pre-commit's staged_files_only.py writes unstaged changes to a patch, runs 'git checkout -- .' (which RESTORES the file), runs hooks, then re-applies the patch in its finally block (which RE-DELETES it). Located at pre_commit/staged_files_only.py L53-86.
- Genesis -- what deletes the file in the first place -- is NOT identified. An agent narrowed it to a one-second window (a pull --rebase --autostash at 20:22:16, the deletion patch at 20:22:17) but correctly refused to name a file:line it could not prove.

CRITICAL FRAMING, do not get this wrong: pre-commit is NOT the bug and must NOT be patched. Restoring unstaged changes after running hooks is its correct designed behavior, and a deleted file is a legitimate unstaged change -- someone who ran 'rm' intending to commit that deletion needs it preserved. It is also third-party. 'Fixing' it would break real workflows.

THE INSIGHT: you cannot reliably distinguish an intentional 'rm' from a phantom deletion -- that is structural, since 'rm' + 'git add -A' and 'git rm' produce identical index states. But you do not need to. The missing file is harmless and recoverable from HEAD. The HARM is committing that deletion to main. Guard the outcome, not the cause, and the fix holds regardless of how many genesis shapes exist.

Existing detection is a warning at launcher time (detect_phantom_deleted_files, branch worktree-aih443-shapec, commit 50886a5, unpushed). That is an alarm, not a guard -- a warning printed at launch does not stop a 'git commit -a' twenty minutes later.

Note this rule has been hand-written into roughly ten sub-agent briefs today ('do not commit any file deletion you did not intend'). A rule that must be retyped into every delegation is a rule that belongs in code.

WORTH RESEARCHING FIRST, and route it Codex -> Gemini -> CC per fleet policy: is there a known interaction between 'git pull --rebase --autostash' and pre-commit's post-merge hook that drops a tracked file? The one-second window above is a specific, checkable question with a possible published answer, and two root-cause guesses were already wrong today.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: A pre-commit-stage guard rejects any commit containing a deletion of a tracked file that is still present on origin/main, unless the deletion is explicitly acknowledged.
AC-2: The acknowledgement path is usable and documented -- intentional deletions must remain easy, or the guard gets bypassed and becomes worse than nothing.
AC-3: The guard is PROVEN able to fail: stage a real phantom deletion, watch it reject; stage an acknowledged deletion, watch it pass. Both directions demonstrated.
AC-4: pre-commit itself is NOT patched, wrapped, or worked around.
AC-5: Distributable beyond one repo -- the same class of loss applies fleet-wide.
AC-6: The research question above is answered or explicitly recorded as unanswerable, before genesis is declared un-findable.

title: Runaway loop re-ran _refresh_live_session_scripts ~9M times in 2 minutes, emitting 1.1 GB of output
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by forensics on a 1.1 GB junk file, before deleting it.

THE ARTIFACT: `sergei/.worktrees/sw-1/typescript` — 1,164,748,852 bytes, produced by the Unix
`script(1)` command (which writes to a file of exactly that name). Its own header and footer bound
the window precisely:

    Script started on Fri Jul 24 21:25:16 2026
    Script done   on Fri Jul 24 21:27:16 2026

**Two minutes. 1.1 GB.**

WHAT IS IN IT: sampling at the 500 MB and 700 MB offsets shows one line repeating, per live
session, interleaved with full-screen repaint escapes (`ESC[H` cursor-home, `ESC[K` erase-line):

    refreshed session template: c-aih-1
    refreshed session template: c-aih-2
    refreshed session template: c-kc-1
    refreshed session template: c-sw-1
    refreshed session template: c-sw-3
    refreshed session template: c-sw-6

That string exists in exactly one place: `src/ai_cli/main.py:373`, inside
`_refresh_live_session_scripts()`.

RATE: 8,160 occurrences per sampled MB x ~1,110 MB = roughly **9 million** emissions in 120
seconds, about **75,000 per second**.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: `_refresh_live_session_scripts()` iterates live tmux sessions ONCE per
call and prints one line per managed session. It contains no loop of its own. So the function is
not the bug — **something called it, or its caller, several million times.** Its docstring says it
is "called after `ai update` installs a new template", which makes the auto-update / auto-restart
path the first place to look. Do not assume that is the answer; establish it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE DISK: 75k iterations/second means each one also ran
`tmux list-sessions` (a subprocess) and `_write_stable_session_script()` (a file write with a
chmod). For two minutes. That is a subprocess-and-write storm against the tmux server and the
state dir, not merely noisy logging. Nobody noticed at the time; it surfaced three days later only
because a stray `script` recording made it physically large.

The 1.1 GB file has been deleted (untracked debris, no unique content) after this evidence was
extracted. The forensic detail above is the record — it cannot be re-derived.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 The loop that invoked this ~9M times is identified by file:line, with the trigger condition
     that made it spin. If it cannot be identified, say so explicitly and state what was ruled
     out — a guessed cause recorded as fact is worse than an open issue.
AC-2 The loop is bounded, or made incapable of re-entering at this rate.
AC-3 Proven by reproducing the trigger and showing the invocation count bounded — before the fix
     it must be shown unbounded. A run that simply completes proves nothing.
AC-4 `_refresh_live_session_scripts()` gains a guard so a pathological caller cannot turn it into
     a subprocess storm (rate limit, idempotence check, or a no-op when nothing changed).
AC-5 No `--no-verify` / `SKIP=` in the fix or its verification.

comments.author: T
comments.text:
AC-1 ANSWER, recorded by the lead because the agent had no bd access from its worktree.

The '~9M invocations / 75k per second subprocess storm' premise in the original brief was WRONG, and I propagated it. It is arithmetically impossible and I verified that independently: this machine forks+execs 'tmux list-sessions' at 32/sec (agent measured 38). One refresh call = one tmux fork+exec + 6 printed lines, so 9M lines = 1.5M calls in 120s = 12500 calls/sec required. That is ~390x above what the hardware does. A probe that returns 32 when the theory needs 12500 is a decisive negative control.

What the 1.1 GB file actually was: 1.11 GB / 9M occurrences = 122 bytes each, against ~44 bytes for the bare line + CRLF. The remaining ~78 bytes/line are ESC[H / ESC[K full-screen repaint escapes. So it is a terminal repainting a screen whose scrollback held ONE 'ai update' output -- not 1.5M fresh invocations. If that reading holds, the repaint source is CC's own TUI renderer, outside this repo, and is NOT fixed here. AC-1 is therefore answered as: no caller loop exists; the emitter's only caller is _do_update_or_deploy() at main.py:985, which self-disarms via the last_update_commit.txt stamp written before spawning.

A DIFFERENT, real runaway loop was found and fixed in the same auto-restart path -- session_script.py:287 ran 'read -t 1 -r < /dev/null', which returns instantly on EOF rather than waiting out its timeout, so the watcher's 'while true' busy-spun for the life of every session. I verified this directly: 5 iterations of the buggy form took 0.084s where correct behaviour is 5.0s. Every counter-derived duration (30-tick heartbeat, 10-tick startup grace, 10-tick config check) was wrong by the same factor. Fixed to 'sleep 1'.

Shipped as 6cbaaef on origin/main. 1856 passed / 7 skipped, up from 1850 baseline. All three guards proven able to fail by mutation.

Lesson for the record: I asserted a mechanism in a delegation brief without checking whether the hardware could produce it. Same failure as the worktree-upstream-drift root cause earlier the same day. Check whether the mechanism is POSSIBLE before it becomes the brief an agent works from.

title: ccF Fable statusline meter is structurally dead — Anthropic removed the per-model quota surface it scraped
description:
Sergei, 2026-07-26: "ccF (fable) usage quota % is still at 2% even though i'm pretty sure we've
run a fable agent... it's usage quota % increases notably whenever we run it, from what ive
observed."

CONFIRMED A BUG, and confirmed independently by the driver rather than on the audit agent's word.

ROOT CAUSE: `ai_cli/quota.py::_scrape_usage_hidden_pane()` gets the Fable number by spawning a
hidden tmux session, launching an interactive `claude`, typing `/usage`, and regex-scraping a
"Current week (Fable)" progress-bar line. **That line no longer exists.** Reproduced by hand
twice against the currently-installed CC v2.1.220 (day view and week view): the dialog now shows a
"What's contributing to your limits usage?" section — session-characteristics text plus
Skills/Subagents-by-name attribution tables — which is not a quota bar and is not keyed by model
at all. The repo's own research doc (`docs/research/claude-quota-statusline-rate-limits-2026.md`,
written 2026-07-13 against CC 2.1.207) confirms the line existed then and was the SOLE per-model
source, so this is an upstream removal somewhere between 2026-07-25 evening and 2026-07-26.

DRIVER-VERIFIED from `~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota.db` directly:
- `weekly_sonnet_pct` last had a non-null value at **2026-07-25T23:07:23Z** (value 2.0), and had
  been 2.0 for **239 consecutive snapshots** before that.
- Every snapshot since is **NULL** for Fable while `usage_percent` (all-models) climbed 55% -> 57%
  in the same window. The two feeds are provably decoupled.
- `~/.local/state/ai-cli/fable-scrape-backoff.json` shows `misses: 4`, backoff already maxed at the
  120-min ceiling. The code's own instrumentation knew it was failing.

So the Fable coordinator plus five sub-agents run on 2026-07-26 COULD NOT have moved this meter
regardless of actual usage. This is not the transient server-side rate-limit the code's comments
assume.

THE OTHER TWO METERS ARE FINE (verified with positive controls, not absence-of-error):
- ccWk (Claude weekly): reads `rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage` from CC's own statusLine
  stdin JSON. Observed climbing in ~10-minute steps; a fresh live `/usage` capture matched.
- cxWk (Codex weekly): live JSON-RPC to `codex app-server --stdio` `account/rateLimits/read`,
  300s cache. A fresh independent call returned byte-identical to the cache.

NEAR-MISS ON SILENT FAILURE — worth its own attention. The display is not strictly lying: the
stale-past-2h marker does render (`ccF 2% ->73% (clock glyph)`, confirmed via `od -c`). But it is
one dim low-contrast character next to a normally-coloured "2%" and a green "->73%" pace delta —
and that delta is now meaningless, since it is `frozen_pct - elapsed_time_pct`, growing every day
purely because time passes while the numerator is frozen. At a glance it reads as a healthy meter.

THE DECISION THIS ISSUE NEEDS (not a patch — there is no replacement data source):
(a) Past some staleness threshold, replace the number with an explicit unavailable state
    (`ccF n/a (stale 5d)`) and suppress the pace arrow. Threshold suggested at 24-48h.
(b) Find a new proxy — e.g. the new Skills/Subagents attribution tables. Lossy, and not
    Fable-specific.
(c) Drop per-model tracking entirely until Anthropic exposes one again.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1 A stale meter renders as unmistakably unavailable, not as a plausible coloured percentage.
AC-2 The pace-delta is suppressed whenever its numerator is stale — a delta computed from a frozen
     value is worse than no delta.
AC-3 Whatever source is chosen, its disappearance fails LOUDLY rather than pinning the last value.
     The current design's failure mode is the bug, not the missing line.
AC-4 Proven by simulating source loss and showing the display state change — a check that cannot
     distinguish "fresh 2%" from "frozen 2%" proves nothing.

title: DONE 2026-07-20: watcher now hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global + project) and `.mcp.json` alongside `CLAUDE.md`
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-115]` **DONE 2026-07-20: watcher now hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global + project) and `.mcp.json` alongside `CLAUDE.md`** (`session_script.py`'s `_config_watch_files`), with regression coverage in `tests/test_config_watch_hash.py` (6 tests: real-bash hash-change behavioral checks for each watched file + a stability sanity check, not just string presence). Full test suite (1843 tests) green. **Auto-restart config-change watcher never hashes `.claude/settings.json` — only `CLAUDE.md` — so `env` overrides (e.g. `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`) silently never propagate to already-running sessions** — Filed 2026-07-20 (Sergei + Claude, root-caused live). `session_script.py`'s idle-triggered auto-restart (`config_reload_idle_secs`, default 90s) exists specifically so a config edit propagates to a long-running CC session without a manual kill — but its change-detection hash (`session_script.py` ~line 240) only covers `$HOME/projects/CLAUDE.md` + `$(pwd)/CLAUDE.md`. It never hashes `.claude/settings.json` (global `~/.claude/settings.json` or any project-level `<repo>/.claude/settings.json`), even though that file's `env` block is exactly the kind of process-launch-only config (like `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`) that needs a real process restart to take effect — `/compact` does not re-read it. **Concrete incident:** sergei commit `87eacfe6` (2026-07-18 21:57) removed `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=70` from `sergei/.claude/settings.json` to restore the native ~96.7% auto-compact threshold. sw-1 (pid 88380) had launched the prior evening (Jul 17 21:29) and ran continuously through the fix — the watcher never detected the settings.json change (it doesn't watch that file), so no idle-restart ever fired, and the override stayed baked into that process's env for 2+ days across ~6 compactions. On 2026-07-20 it fired auto-compact again at the stale 70%-of-window boundary, reproducing the exact "ctx-pct read ~66%" symptom the original fix commit's own message described — because ctx-pct reports the real full-window %, which doesn't land exactly on the override's own percentage base. **Fix:** extend the watcher's hash to also cover `.claude/settings.json` (global + project-level, same two-path pattern already used for CLAUDE.md) so `env`-block edits trigger the same idle-restart CLAUDE.md edits already get. Scope-design first (is `env` the only settings.json key that needs this, or should the whole file be hashed?) before implementing. Related: sergei commits `7315f0e2` (added the override), `87eacfe6` (removed it, documents the same 66%-vs-70% confusion), `ai-harness` `f38c1c4` (ctx-pct override-aware reporting — already correct, not the bug).

title: `ai c`/`ai g` launcher doesn't activate direnv before starting the agent — fleet-wide stale/missing-secrets exposure
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-112]` **`ai c`/`ai g` launcher doesn't activate direnv before starting the agent — fleet-wide stale/missing-secrets exposure** — Filed 2026-07-19 (Claude, sw-1), from `docs/research/cc-bash-tool-direnv-env-loading.md` (Codex research, `cx research --effort high`). Root cause: the launcher `chdir`s to the resolved project/worktree in Python or a generated non-login zsh script, then invokes `claude`/`gemini` directly — no `direnv exec`/export evaluation at any point. Combined with Claude Code's Bash tool never activating direnv itself (separate, already-documented finding — `sergei/docs/procedures/secrets-management.md` § Agentic CLI and non-interactive shell loading), this means an agent session's actual secrets/env state depends entirely on whatever the parent shell had at `ai c`/`ai g` launch time — stale if a session is long-running past a Doppler rotation, wrong-but-valid if launched with a lingering override, or silently missing if launched from a shell that never `cd`'d into a populated project. Demonstrated concretely via AIDO-252 (a stale `AIDO_DB_DSN` override silently won for an entire session). **Scope:** run the generated session process under `direnv exec <target_root> <agent-or-session-command>` once the launcher has resolved the final project/worktree root — apply to every launch/restart variant (normal, `--once`, bare, explicit `-p`, worktree and no-worktree, new tmux session, restart/hot-reload, resume/continue, remote SSH/mosh, both Claude and Gemini) — wrapping only the first invocation is insufficient if a later restart path re-invokes the binary outside the activated subtree. Acceptance criteria + required regression-test list are fully spelled out in the research doc's Recommendation §1 and "Required regression tests" — use those directly, don't re-derive. **Related:** the research doc above (full analysis + 3-layer recommendation, this is layer 1 of 3), `sergei/docs/procedures/secrets-management.md` (layer 3, already documented), AIDO-252 (the triggering incident).
notes: Linked to cross-repo hardening research: ai-harness AIH-764 (Research: systemic hardening against secret exposure into CC/agent session transcripts) -- related systemic gap (stale/missing secrets exposure via launcher not activating direnv), not the same failure shape as the other 5 tracked incidents but part of the same 'secrets handling keeps failing in new ways' pattern.

title: DONE 2026-07-23 — both bugs fixed for real, full suite green (1853 passed, 0 failed), no `SKIP_TESTS=1`.
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-121]` **DONE 2026-07-23 — both bugs fixed for real, full suite green (1853 passed, 0 failed), no `SKIP_TESTS=1`.** Two test-suite bugs surfaced by AI-CLI-120's fresh-worktree run. **Bug 1 (8 failures, `detect_repo_root()` "resolved to `.../.worktrees/...`" RuntimeError):** root cause was a **test bug, not a production bug** — `main.py`'s AI-CLI-99 repair backstop calls `_session.detect_repo_root()` for real, unmocked, before any of these 8 tests' own worktree-specific mocking begins; their blanket `subprocess.run` patches' generic "success, empty stdout" default fallback incidentally answers that unrelated call too. `detect_repo_root()` then treats `Path.cwd()` (with empty joined path) as the git-common-dir, and since the *real* pytest process cwd is inside a worktree, its parent naturally contains `.worktrees`, tripping the function's own worktree-nesting safety guard. Fixed by explicitly patching `ai_cli.session.detect_repo_root` to return `None` in all 8 affected tests (`tests/test_cli.py`, `TestCliWorktreeGitPull`'s shared `_run_c_with_fake_subprocess` helper plus 3 standalone tests in `TestCliSessionSetupBranches`/`TestCliSessionExecvp`) — `main.py` already handles a `None` return gracefully (skips the repair step), which is exactly the correct behavior for tests that aren't testing that code path at all. **Bug 2 (18 failures, Python-version drift):** fixed by adding `.python-version` (pinned to `3.13`) — no such pin existed anywhere in the repo, so a fresh worktree's `uv sync --frozen --extra dev` (no explicit `-p`) silently resolved to whatever uv's newest locally-installed interpreter was (3.14.3) instead of the fleet's actual working baseline (3.13.12); confirmed by deleting `.venv` and re-syncing with no override — now correctly resolves to 3.13 automatically. Verified: full suite (`uv run pytest -q`) — 1853 passed, 0 failed, 3 warnings (pre-existing, unrelated asyncio warnings) in ~11s. **Bug 3, found while re-verifying the push (17 failures + 9 errors, `git commit`/`git init` subprocess failures in temp fixture repos):** the suite ran clean under a manual `XDG_STATE_HOME=$(mktemp -d)` override but failed identically via the real pre-push test-gate hook, reproducing in two independently-fresh worktrees — proving it wasn't index corruption or worktree staleness. Root cause: no test-level isolation for `XDG_STATE_HOME` existed (only quota/Fable state had a dedicated fixture, `_isolate_quota_state`, AI-CLI-97) — tests creating ephemeral git repos raced against the real, shared `~/.local/state/ai-cli-utils/` whenever invoked without the manual override. Fixed with a new autouse fixture, `_isolate_xdg_state_home` (`tests/conftest.py`), isolating it for every test the same way quota state already was. Verified deterministic across 4 consecutive full-suite runs with no manual env override. **Bug 4, found re-verifying yet again (down to 4 `test_sync.py` failures, real git commit-message content bleeding into ephemeral `git commit` calls inside test fixtures, reproducing only via the real pre-commit-wrapped pre-push hook, never standalone):** root cause is `AI-CLI-70` itself, more precisely diagnosed this round — see `docs/bugs/worktree-index-corruption.md` Round 3. git injects `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` into every hook process; pre-commit strips these before its own internal git plumbing but not before running a hook's `entry` command (confirmed in pre-commit 4.6.0's `languages/unsupported_script.py`), so `test-gate.sh` and everything it spawns inherited the real worktree's git-targeting env raw. Fixed by stripping those vars at the top of `test-gate.sh` itself (canonical: `project-template@b0ef80a`, applied here at `39dfe6f`) — the earliest possible point of defense, ahead of pytest even starting. Verified: the push that had been failing on this exact leak succeeded cleanly on the next attempt with no other change. **Regression test added** (`tests/hooks/test-testgate-git-env-strip.sh`, matching the existing `tests/hooks/test-corrupt-index-guard.sh` convention): shims `git` on `PATH` to capture what env the first git subprocess `test-gate.sh` spawns actually sees, with leaked `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` simulated in the environment beforehand. RED-verified against a reverted copy of the fix (fails for the right reason — leaked vars visible) before being trusted GREEN against the real fixed script.

title: Bug: git worktree index corruption after rebase conflict resolution
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-70]` **Bug: git worktree index corruption after rebase conflict resolution** — Recurring issue: after resolving a rebase conflict, the worktree index shows 100+ `D` (staged deletions) + matching `??` (untracked) entries for files that exist on disk. Root cause Round 1: pre-commit stash captures corruption, pop restores it. Root cause Round 2: `git pull --rebase --autostash` at session startup perpetuates corruption across sessions. **Root cause Round 3 (2026-07-23):** recurred again in two fresh worktrees with no autostash involved — traced to git itself injecting `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` into every hook process (pre-commit's own `no_git_env()` works around this for its internal plumbing but not for the hook's `entry` command), so `test-gate.sh` and everything it spawns — including this repo's own test suite, which shells real `git` in ephemeral fixture repos — inherited the real worktree's git-targeting env raw. Fix Round 1: pre-push guard hook (`.githooks/corrupt-index-guard.sh`, 16 tests). Fix Round 2: self-healing in `main.py` before autostash runs (5 new tests). Fix Round 3: strip git-targeting env vars at the top of `test-gate.sh`, before pytest starts (canonical: `project-template@b0ef80a`, applied here `39dfe6f`). Bug doc: `docs/bugs/worktree-index-corruption.md`.

title: Bug: duplicate `/exit` injection in auto-restart watcher
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-79]` **Bug: duplicate `/exit` injection in auto-restart watcher** — The watcher loop injects `/exit` + Enter into the CC pane multiple times. Two root causes: (1) pane-content guard (`'^[[:space:]]*❯[[:space:]]*$'`) doesn't explicitly reject prompts that already contain `/exit` text; (2) `config_hash_file` is written once at session start and never updated after a config change is processed — so after `/exit` fires and CC restarts, the config change detector immediately re-fires because the stored hash is still the old one, creating a new `config_changed_file` → new `signal_file` → another injection. Fix: (a) add `/exit` content check before injection; (b) re-write `config_hash_file` with the current hash immediately after a config-triggered signal_file is created so the baseline advances. File: `src/ai_cli/session_script.py` ~lines 151–211. Related: `[AI-CLI-35]` (prompt injection safety), `[AI-CLI-74]` (auto-restart feature).

title: Statusline /usage scrape robustness — replace the flaky interactive-TUI hidden-pane scrape with `claude -p /usage`
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-95]` **Statusline /usage scrape robustness — replace the flaky interactive-TUI hidden-pane scrape with `claude -p /usage`** — Filed + done 2026-07-13 (Sergei; root-cause investigation). **Problem:** the per-model weekly line (`Current week (Fable)`) was captured only ~1/3 of scrapes. **Root cause:** the scrape drove the *interactive* `/usage` TUI in a hidden tmux CC session — inherently nondeterministic: (1) readiness race (`/usage` sent on heuristic prompt-detection before CC is fully interactive → dropped keystrokes / partial render); (2) async per-model data loads *after* all-models/session, so `capture-pane` samples a mid-render frame; (3) terminal-size/animation/progressive-paint dependence. No grace-tuning fixes a fundamentally wrong mechanism. **Fix (robust, not a workaround):** CC 2.1.x runs slash commands non-interactively via `claude -p /usage` — deterministic (verified 3/3 incl. Fable, vs ~1/3), ~1-2s, and **$0** (`--output-format json` → `total_cost_usd:0`, zero tokens, `num_turns:0`; /usage is metadata, not a model turn). New `_get_usage_via_print_mode()` is now the primary path in `_get_claude_usage_snapshot()`; the legacy hidden-pane scrape is kept as a **fallback** only (belt-and-suspenders for CC versions where community docs still claim `-p` slash commands are interactive-only). Live end-to-end: `_get_claude_usage_snapshot` now returns Fable 3/3. Full ai-cli-utils ruff+pytest gate green (195 quota tests). Related: AIH-120, AI-CLI-83, AI-CLI-94.

If one scrape fails to parse the Sonnet breakdown, the latest row has `None`, overriding valid data from earlier rows. Fix: fall back to the most recent non-`None` `weekly_sonnet_pct` value across the last N snapshots instead of hard-coding row index 0. **✅ ALREADY DONE (verified 2026-07-12, ai-cli-statusline):** shipped in commit `de92cdb` (2026-04-29) — `quota_statusline_part()` already does `next((r["weekly_sonnet_pct"] for r in rows if ... is not None), None)` over `ORDER BY snapshotted_at DESC LIMIT 3`. title: Auto-register CC workspace trust at session/worktree launch (fix "workspace has not been trusted" permission drop)
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-90]` **Auto-register CC workspace trust at session/worktree launch (fix "workspace has not been trusted" permission drop)** — DONE 2026-07-05 (aih-1). Root cause: Claude Code 2.1.x (GH [#72896](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/72896), a side-effect of the CVE-2026-33068 trust hardening) gates the trust *dialog* on an ancestor walk but gates `permissions.allow` *loading* on an exact `gitRoot(cwd)` match. With `~/projects` trusted as an ancestor, the dialog is suppressed so each workspace's exact key never auto-registers; a non-interactive `claude` there drops its `.claude/settings.json` permissions and prints `Ignoring N permissions.allow entries ... this workspace has not been trusted`. Reproduced verbatim. Fix: new `ai_cli.trust` — `ensure_workspace_trusted()` idempotently sets `projects[gitRoot].hasTrustDialogAccepted=true` in `~/.claude.json` (atomic, best-effort, no-op if the file is absent/unparseable), wired into `create_worktree()` + the launch path (covers worktree, `--no-worktree`, bare). New `ai trust-backfill [--root ~/projects]` remediates existing repos. Keeps the `~/projects` ancestor trust (needed for headless launches). +10 tests. Not fixed upstream (2.1.201 latest). Analysis: `ai-harness/docs/research/claude-code-workspace-trust-permission-drop.md`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Root-cause + robustly fix the recurring `core.bare=true` git-config corruption from worktree operations
description: `[P1]` `[AI-CLI-99]` **Root-cause + robustly fix the recurring `core.bare=true` git-config corruption from worktree operations** — DONE 2026-07-13. **Confirmed two vectors, fixed both:** (1) **leaked `GIT_*` env** — `session.py`'s `create_worktree`/`cleanup_worktree` and `copier_update.py`'s isolated-worktree flow ran `git worktree add/remove` via `subprocess.run` with no `env=`, inheriting the caller's `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/etc. verbatim; when the caller is a nested CC session already inside a worktree, those vars can leak into a worktree op targeting the shared main-tree gitdir and write `core.bare`/`core.worktree` onto it; (2) **a wrong "restore `core.bare=true`" recovery workflow** that had propagated via session memory/resume messages only (no committed doc said this) — main tree is a normal working tree, never intentionally bare. **Fix shipped:** new `src/ai_cli/git_repair.py` — `_git_env()` strips `GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES/GIT_PREFIX/GIT_CONFIG/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` before every git subprocess call in `session.py`/`copier_update.py`/`main.py`'s launch path that touches repo/worktree structure (keeps innocuous `GIT_SSH*`/`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`/`GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`); `repair_bare_worktree_config(repo_root)` is a deterministic backstop — asserts + repairs `core.bare`/`core.worktree` on a normal working tree regardless of source (covers paths we don't control, e.g. CC's own `isolation: worktree` tool), wired at `ai c N` session launch (`main.py`, before/after the launch's git ops) and before/after every worktree add/remove in `copier_update.py` + `session.py`. **Tests:** 8 new (`tests/test_git_repair.py` — env-scrub incl. innocuous-var retention, repair for bare-only/stale-worktree-only/both/healthy-noop, plus a real-git-repo end-to-end repro of the exact corruption). Full suite 1811 passed, ruff clean. **No live repro of the leak itself** (constructing the exact GIT_* combination that reproduces the write proved not deterministic in isolation — see ai-harness `docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md` § root-cause note); the env-scrub + backstop guard are correct regardless of the precise trigger. Research: [📄 ai-harness/docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md](../../../ai-harness/docs/research/nested-agent-worktree-orchestration.md) § "Root cause + fix — `core.bare=true` recurrence". Also resolves the guard referenced prospectively as AIH-215 in ai-harness plan docs (no separate AIH-215 roadmap entry existed — this AI-CLI-99 fix is that guard). Related: AIH-167, AI-CLI-89, AI-CLI-91, #182. **Deploy:** reinstall in 3 places (local Mac `uv tool install`, Hetzner `uv tool install`, aido venv `uv pip install`) — handled by the launching session, not this task.
close_reason: Closed

title: test_given_lockfile_exists_when_auto_update_then_returns_early hangs/times out (execnet gateway stuck)
description: Confirmed pre-existing on unmodified HEAD (verified via git stash during AI-CLI-fae.14 v0.8.0 re-verification): tests/test_cli_dispatch.py::TestAutoUpdateLockfile::test_given_lockfile_exists_when_auto_update_then_returns_early hangs and times out (>90s under the default -n auto xdist run, >30s isolated) both with and without the fae.14 diff applied. Isolated run shows the xdist execnet gateway worker stuck reading from its pipe (gateway_base.py _thread_receiver -> from_io -> read), suggesting the test spawns something that blocks and never returns control to the worker, similar in shape to the already-tracked stale-session-reaper hang (AI-CLI-test-given-clean-child-exit-wyit) but a different test/module. Also observed: running the full suite with -n 0 (no xdist) produces ~106 unrelated failures (mostly FileNotFoundError in worktree/session-launch tests) that do NOT occur under the default -n auto invocation -- this suite appears to depend on xdist's worker-per-process model for some fixture/path behavior; -n 0 is not currently a valid way to get a clean serial baseline for this repo. Worth a closer look separately.
notes: Delegating root-cause+fix to cx implement (worktree .worktrees/ai-cli-8zpm-bugfix, branch ai-cli-8zpm-bugfix).
close_reason: Fixed via commit 7e4c1d0 (pushed directly to main, personal-repo convention). Root cause: not an execnet-escaped-subprocess bug -- the test genuinely blocked on _await_peer_update()'s real 90s time.sleep(poll) wait loop, confirmed via git-stash bisection (unfixed test times out at main.py:847 with the exact reported execnet-stuck symptom). Fix patches the wait/poll constants down to ms in the test. Independently re-verified: 3/3 passed in 1.74s under xdist, ruff+pyright clean.

title: pytest -n auto has recurring cross-worker test contamination -- large random subsets fail together, pass 100% clean alone
description: During AI-CLI-fae.13 (security-fix branch) verification, multiple full-suite 'pytest' (-n auto, the project's own default addopts) runs each produced a different random-looking batch of failures (e.g. all of tests/test_session_launch_locality.py + tests/test_session_launch_integration.py together in one run; tests/test_bare_worktree.py's real-git-clone fixture in a long serial run; tests/test_session_launch_shell_resolution.py in another parallel run) -- but every single one of those tests passed 100% clean when re-run alone or as just that one file. This is consistent with either xdist cross-worker state contamination (real tmux session names / shared tmp state colliding between parallel workers) or test-order-dependent global state pollution (pytest-randomly reorders tests each run, changing which tests happen to share a worker/order). Distinct from the already-filed AI-CLI-91p4 (one specific always-the-same flaky test) and AI-CLI-wyit (one specific deterministic hang) -- this issue is about the general pattern of large, non-reproducible failure batches that make a single 'pytest' run an unreliable signal on its own. Worth investigating: whether real subprocess/tmux fixtures share global names/paths across xdist workers instead of using worker-unique identifiers (pytest-xdist worker id, os.getpid(), or similar) in tmp_path-derived resource names.
notes: Round 2 launched: cx implement (effort high, --sandbox danger-full-access) in .worktrees/ai-cli-6h4r-round2, investigating the new test_session.py Gemini-checkpoint cluster + residual worktree-test failures. Full sandbox access granted per Sergei's explicit request (real tmux sockets, unrestricted subprocess, no foreground time cap).
close_reason: Fixed via 2 rounds: Round 1 (fc6d259) isolated the shared ~/.claude.json trust registry; Round 2 (51784d9) isolated process CWD after a test os.chdir()s into and deletes a tmp_path, which was leaking a FileNotFoundError into the next test's checkpoint conversion (test_session.py Gemini cluster + 5 worktree tests). Independently re-verified: full-suite reruns (2565 passed/14 skipped) show zero remaining contamination in the originally-reported clusters. Remaining 5 failures are out of scope: 2 belong to AI-CLI-qt1e (reaper signal topology), 2 (test_remote.py, test_session_adopt.py) reproduce standalone on clean origin/main and are pre-existing unrelated bugs -- filed separately.

title: test_stale_session_reaper.py / test_session_launch_locality.py: real-tmux tests hang/crash under this sandbox, unrelated to AI-CLI-fae.13
description: During full-suite verification of the AI-CLI-fae.13 (F-19..F-26) security-fix branch, two tests crashed their pytest-xdist worker in a full parallel run: tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py::test_given_clean_child_exit_when_supervisor_finishes_then_tmux_session_is_removed, tests/test_stale_session_reaper.py::test_given_child_receives_ctrl_c_during_preflight_when_single_press_then_wrapper_survives_and_double_press_exits_cleanly[bash], and tests/test_session_launch_locality.py::test_given_a_new_worktree_when_launched_then_its_creation_is_announced[g]. Neither test file was touched by the security-fix branch's diff (only sync.py, config.py, session_script.py, main.py, notifications.py, cc_usage.py, direnv_setup.py, and CI workflow files were modified for F-19..F-26). These tests use the real_tmux marker (spawn a real tmux server on an isolated socket) and deal with Ctrl+C/child-process lifecycle -- this exact test file has a documented history of environment-sensitive flakiness in this repo (see the 39th-cycle AI-CLI-zjy2 Ctrl+C/reload-loop lockout saga). Hypothesis: this specific sandboxed Bash-tool environment lacks a real TTY/pty that these tmux-attach tests need, causing an indefinite hang rather than the expected clean pass/fail -- not a functional regression from the security fixes. Needs verification on a real interactive terminal (not a headless background Bash-tool subprocess) before concluding either way.

title: Unexplained live sessions on Framework: c-r-myprefix-1 / c-r-myprefix-unrecognized-1
description:
While deploying the self-heal + launch-logging fixes this session, two live tmux/CC sessions were
found running on Framework that I did not create: c-r-myprefix-1 and c-r-myprefix-unrecognized-1,
both at ~/projects/ai-cli-utils/.worktrees/myprefix-1 / myprefix-unrecognized-1, session-meta shows
project_prefix "myprefix" -- a name that reads like a leaked test-fixture placeholder rather than a
real project (ai-cli-utils' own test suite and CLAUDE.md's public-repo convention both use
"myproject"/"myprefix"-style generic names). Created ~20:47-20:48 the same day, right around when
"ai update --force" was run there via SSH -- timing correlation only, no causal evidence found.
c-r-myprefix-1 showed genuine active usage (ccWk 92%), so this is NOT an empty artifact -- it's a
real, actively-used session.

Flagged to the user live in-session; they had not yet confirmed whether this is their own
concurrent work (e.g. testing something on Framework from another session) or a genuine new bug
(a real leak from "ai update"/"ai c" accidentally launching sessions against a placeholder-looking
project name) by the time this session checkpointed. Not investigated further or touched.

## Acceptance criteria

- User confirms whether c-r-myprefix-1 / c-r-myprefix-unrecognized-1 are expected (their own
  work) or unexpected.
- If unexpected: root-cause how "ai update --force" (or another path) could have launched a real
  session using project_prefix "myprefix", and fix the reachable code path.
- If expected: close as no-defect.
notes:
2026-09-01 -- ROOT CAUSE FOUND (definitive, source-code-verified). Not a test-fixture leak: verified
tests/test_main.py:953-974 (test_when_project_prefix_flag_then_uses_it,
test_when_unknown_arg_then_used_as_session_name) both mock load_config()=={} and assert exit(1)
"because -R requires remote host" -- they never reach transport under pytest, confirming the
earlier refutation was correct.

The real mechanism: these two tests' exact argv literals --
  ai c --project-prefix myprefix -R
  ai c --project-prefix myprefix -R --unrecognized
-- if run for REAL in a shell (not through pytest's mocked load_config), behave differently.
Verified directly in src/ai_cli/main.py:2390-2392:
  if not name and extra_args:
      name = extra_args[0]
      extra_args = extra_args[1:]
When no positional name is given, the first unrecognized CLI token becomes the session name. So a
real "ai c --project-prefix myprefix -R --unrecognized" run (on a machine whose config.toml DOES
resolve a real remote host, unlike the test's empty mock) sets session name = "--unrecognized",
while the sibling command without that extra token gets a different default name -- producing
exactly the two observed sessions: c-r-myprefix-1 and c-r-myprefix-unrecognized-1. The "unrecognized"
suffix match is not a coincidence; it is this exact code path.

Conclusion: this is NOT a code defect. The CLI behaved exactly as designed and as its own tests
document. The leak's origin is that someone (human or an investigating AI agent -- most likely a
Codex delegation reading tests/test_main.py:953-974 while investigating this very issue's earlier
guard-gap thread, since the timing is 2026-08-31 20:47-20:48 and the ssh/mosh real-process-guard
gap for this repo's test suite was being actively investigated/fixed around then) copy-pasted or
reconstructed these exact test argv literals into a REAL shell instead of running them through
pytest, on a machine with a real resolvable remote host. No code fix is needed or applicable --
closing as root-caused, no defect. Cleanup of the two resulting live sessions/worktrees is a
separate, already-authorized action.
close_reason: Root-caused definitively via source-code trace (main.py:2390-2392): the two leaked sessions exactly match tests/test_main.py:953-974's argv literals run for real instead of through pytest's mocked config -- not a code defect, the CLI behaves as designed/tested. No fix applicable. Cleanup of the resulting sessions authorized separately by Sergei.

description:
