title: ai update silently converts an editable install into a copy, per source edit
description:
## Task details

`ai update` installs with `uv tool install <path> --force` and **never** `-e`, so any launch-triggered
install silently converts an editable install into a copied one. That destroys the live-edit workflow
at exactly the moment a developer is relying on it, and it happens with no output saying so.

### Measured on sem-kg-sagemaker 2026-08-14 — the install flipped mid-session

Two probes of the same quantity, 14 minutes apart, both real:

    18:30  dist-info ai_cli_utils-0.7.0.post20260814182650
           tool python -c "import ai_cli" -> .../uv/tools/ai-cli-utils/lib/python3.12/site-packages/ai_cli/__init__.py
           => NOT editable (a copied install, made by an `ai update` run at 18:26)

    18:44  dist-info ai_cli_utils-0.7.0
           direct_url.json  {"dir_info":{"editable":true}}
           _editable_impl_ai_cli_utils.pth -> <repo>/src
           tool python -c "import ai_cli" -> <repo>/src/ai_cli/__init__.py
           => EDITABLE

So the install oscillates between editable and copied depending on what last touched it. **What made
it editable at 18:44 is not attributed** — no `ai` code path installs with `-e`, so it came from
outside the tool. Do not assume either state is the steady state; probe it.

The decisive probe is `direct_url.json` plus resolving `ai_cli.__file__` through the tool's own
interpreter. A `*.pth` glob listing is easy to misread — that produced one wrong reading during this
investigation.

### Why this is worse after AI-CLI-make-ai-c-ytbw

Pre-fix, the launch reinstalled once per repo commit. The fingerprint signal that replaced it
(`_installed_source_fingerprint`, sha256 over `pyproject.toml` + `src/**`) fires on any change to a
packaged file, **including an uncommitted edit**. So on an editable install:

1. the edit is already live — a reinstall is not needed for it to take effect;
2. the reinstall runs anyway, because the fingerprint moved;
3. `uv tool install --force` without `-e` replaces the editable install with a copy;
4. from then on the developer's live edits stop taking effect, which is the original stale-version
   complaint reintroduced by the mechanism meant to fix it.

The blast radius is per-edit rather than per-commit, which makes it far likelier to be hit.

### Deferred design call

The implementing agent identified this and deliberately did not decide it, which was correct — it is
a behaviour question, not a bug fix. The candidate: skip the launch-time install when
`direct_url.json` reports `editable: true`, since a source edit needs no install at all in that mode,
while still installing when the change affects dependencies or entry points (which an editable
install does not pick up automatically). Preserving editability by passing `-e` on the reinstall is a
second option, but it changes what `ai update` means on machines that deliberately run a copied
install.

## Acceptance criteria

AC-1 WHEN the installed distribution reports `editable: true` and only packaged source files changed,
THEN the launch shall not reinstall.
AC-2 WHEN a change affects dependencies or entry points, THEN the launch shall still install even on
an editable install, because an editable install does not pick those up.
AC-3 WHEN an install runs against a distribution that was editable, THEN it shall not silently
downgrade it to a copied install — either editability is preserved, or the change is stated in the
one-line launch output.
AC-4 A test shall fail if the launch path converts an editable install into a non-editable one, and
it shall determine editability from `direct_url.json` plus the resolved module path rather than from
a filename glob.
close_reason: Codex delegation reviewed field-by-field against source, verified locally (ruff+pytest all green), shipped via PRs #81-86 (squash-merged directly, no admin bypass needed post AI-CLI-sz10 ruleset fix)

title: pyproject.toml is committed as CRLF, so ai update dirties it on every POSIX box
description:
## Task details

`pyproject.toml` is committed with CRLF line endings while every other file in the repo is LF, and
the repo has no `.gitattributes`. Consequence: `ai update`'s version-bump rewrite silently converts
the file to LF, so every POSIX machine carries a permanent phantom 172-insertion / 172-deletion
whole-file diff in `git status`.

### Measured, sem-kg-sagemaker 2026-08-14

    committed blob (HEAD:pyproject.toml)   CRLF 172, bare LF 0
    working tree                           CRLF 0,   bare LF 172
    git diff --stat                        172 insertions(+), 172 deletions(-)
    git diff --ignore-all-space --stat     empty          <- content is identical
    version line, both sides               version = "0.7.0"   <- NOT a stranded version bump

The version line matching on both sides is the control: this is purely an end-of-line difference,
not an interrupted update that left a `.post<timestamp>` behind.

### Two causes, both needed for the fix

1. **The committed blob is wrong.** `pyproject.toml` was LF for its entire history through
   `71db600`. Commit `d239bf5` (2026-08-12, authored on the Windows host) has the message
   "pyproject.toml: CRLF -> LF normalization (content unchanged)" but actually committed the file
   **as CRLF** — the exact inverse of what it claims. Verified by decoding the blob at all 10
   commits that touched the path: `d239bf5` is CRLF, all nine ancestors are LF.
2. **The update path rewrites line endings as a side effect.** `_do_update_or_deploy()`
   (`src/ai_cli/main.py:1484`, `:1495`, `:1504`) round-trips the file through
   `Path.read_text()` / `Path.write_text()`. `read_text()` applies universal-newline translation,
   so CRLF becomes LF in memory, and the `finally: pyproject.write_text(original)` restore writes
   LF back to disk. The file is therefore re-dirtied on **every** update run, forever.

`main.py:1424` runs `git checkout -- pyproject.toml` at the start of each update, so the dirt is
discarded on the next run rather than accumulating — which is exactly why this has stayed invisible
and unfiled. The live hazard is that any session running `git add -A` commits the EOL flip, and the
phantom diff has already been mistaken for another session's uncommitted work.

## Acceptance criteria

AC-1 WHEN the repository is checked out on any platform, THEN `pyproject.toml` shall have a single
canonical line ending enforced by a committed `.gitattributes`, so the flip cannot recur.
AC-2 WHEN `ai update` rewrites `pyproject.toml` to bump the version and then restores it, THEN the
restored file shall be byte-identical to the original, including its line endings.
AC-3 WHEN the version-bump write is interrupted, THEN the restore shall still preserve the original
bytes exactly.
AC-4 A test shall fail if the version-bump round trip alters any byte other than the version value —
it must assert on bytes read in binary mode, since a text-mode read normalizes the exact difference
under test and would pass vacuously.

title: Make ai c launch quiet: only reinstall when the installed code is actually stale
description:
## Original request (verbatim)

> okay, i resumed aih-3 successfully. also add a /beads-task to ai-cli-utils to not fully install / print out all this stuff everytime unless we actually have to re-install / update for new updates / version for ai-cli-utils and/or we need to refresh cache. i think the reason we did full reinstall everytime originally is because it was caching old versions when i would test if new changes were coming through for ai-cli-utils and so it would use older version of ai-cli-utlis. but i don't lik ehtat we print out all that stuff everytime. so maybe we can either clean up what is printed and make it more elegant like just the existing version and whteher its installing new versoin, checking cache for old versoin, or whatever we need to do here so this print statement stuff during `ai c` launch is cleaner. ship beads task and add cc tsak and then /delegate to opus to /implement this.

## Task details

`ai c <n>` dumps the whole installer transcript into the terminal before the session starts, on
almost every launch. Two independent causes, both measured on sem-kg-sagemaker 2026-08-14.

### Cause 1 — the staleness signal is the repo HEAD hash, so ANY commit forces a full reinstall

`_auto_update_if_stale()` (`src/ai_cli/main.py:539`) is called from the `ai c` launch path
(`main.py:2412`). It compares `git rev-parse HEAD` against the stamp
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/ai-cli-utils/last_update_commit.txt` and, on any difference, runs
`ai update --force`.

HEAD changes for commits that alter **no installed code at all** — a `.beads/issues.jsonl` sync, a
`docs/` edit, a roadmap note. Three commits landed in this repo today (`7973574`, `dd20b38`, and one
merge); each one armed a full pull-plus-reinstall for the next launch on every machine. Measured
state right after the 18:26 launch: stamp `dd20b381e4d12a3a85df1d70b235b47df426110b` == HEAD, and the
installed dist-info is `ai_cli_utils-0.7.0.post20260814182650` — i.e. that launch did pay for a
complete reinstall.

### Cause 2 — `ai update` is built so uv can NEVER no-op, and nothing captures its output

`_do_update_or_deploy()` (`main.py:1408`) unconditionally:

1. prints `Pulling latest from origin...` and runs `git pull --rebase --autostash`;
2. rewrites `pyproject.toml`'s version to `0.7.0.post<UTC timestamp>` and prints `Updating X -> Y`;
3. runs `uv tool install <path> --force` (plus `--reinstall` from `--force`) with
   `subprocess.run(..., cwd=project_path)` and **no** `capture_output`, so uv's full
   `Resolved N packages / Prepared / Uninstalled / Installed` block goes straight to the user's
   terminal, immediately before the CC session paints;
4. repeats that for every `[update] extra_venvs` entry via `uv pip install --force-reinstall`.

The unique `.post<timestamp>` version is what defeats uv's cache, and per the request above that is
**deliberate and load-bearing** — it is the reason a code change is always actually picked up when
testing whether new changes came through. Do not remove it blindly; the install is **not** editable
on this host (`~/.local/bin/ai` -> `~/.local/share/uv/tools/ai-cli-utils/...`, and `ai_cli` resolves
into that tool's `site-packages`, not the repo `src`), so without a real reinstall the running code
genuinely is stale.

### What good looks like

Keep the correctness guarantee, drop the cost and the noise. Both halves of the request are in scope:
do less work when nothing needs installing, AND make what is printed a single elegant line.

## Acceptance criteria

AC-1 WHEN `ai c <n>` is launched and the installed build already corresponds to the current source
code, THEN no pull, no version bump, and no `uv tool install` shall run.
AC-2 WHEN HEAD differs from the stamp but no file that affects the installed package has changed
(e.g. a `.beads/` or `docs/`-only commit), THEN the launch shall NOT reinstall.
AC-3 WHEN a reinstall IS required, THEN the launch shall print at most one concise line naming the
installed version and the reason (new version / cache refresh), and the underlying `git` and `uv`
output shall be captured rather than streamed to the terminal.
AC-4 WHEN a reinstall fails, THEN its captured output shall be surfaced on stderr in full, so
suppressing the success path never hides a failure.
AC-5 WHEN the operator passes an explicit verbose or force flag, THEN the full underlying output
shall be shown, and a documented escape hatch shall force a cache-refreshing reinstall on demand.
AC-6 WHEN a source file that IS part of the installed package changes, THEN the next `ai c` launch
shall install it — a test shall prove the running code is the new code, so the quieting can never
reintroduce the stale-version behaviour that motivated the unconditional reinstall.

title: direnv .envrc emits load_ai_core_secrets: command not found -- degrade gracefully and say secrets are unloaded
description:
## Symptom (verbatim, seen on sem-kg-sagemaker while launching `ai c`)

```
.worktrees/aih-2/.envrc
direnv: ai-harness environment loaded
./.envrc:11: load_ai_core_secrets: command not found
```

## Root cause — measured 2026-08-14 on sem-kg-sagemaker, not inferred

`load_ai_core_secrets` is a **direnv stdlib extension function**, not a script on PATH. direnv only
defines such functions if a `direnvrc` declares them. On this machine there is **no direnvrc at all**:
`~/.config/direnv/direnvrc`, `~/.direnvrc` and `/etc/direnv/direnvrc` are all absent.

The definition lives in the **`sergei` personal-profile repo** (`sergei/scripts/direnv/direnvrc`).
That repo is **not cloned on this machine** — 16 repos are present under the projects root and
`sergei` is not one of them. So the function is not "missing from ai-core" and is not gitignored:
it was never in ai-core. The `ai_core` prefix in the name is a misnomer.

`doppler` is also **not installed** on this machine, so even a correctly-defined function would fail
at the backend.

## Severity — the error itself is noise; the silent secrets gap is the hazard

Verified: direnv does **not** abort the `.envrc` after the failed call. `export
LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=false` on the following line still takes effect (`direnv exec . bash -c
'echo $LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2'` -> `false`). A control confirmed a variable exported *before* the
failing line also survives.

So the functional consequence is not a broken shell — it is that **every secret the loader would
have exported is silently unset**, with one `command not found` line as the only signal. Anything
depending on `NTFY_TOKEN`, `AI_CORE_DATABASE_URL`, `AI_CORE_JWT_*` etc. fails later, far from the
cause, with no diagnosis pointing back here.

## Done when

The call degrades gracefully instead of emitting a shell error:

1. Guard the invocation — call it only when it is actually defined
   (`declare -F load_ai_core_secrets >/dev/null`), so a machine without the profile repo produces
   **no** `command not found`.
2. When it is undefined, print one clear, actionable line naming what is missing and what the
   consequence is — that the Doppler-backed secrets are **not loaded**, so any secret-dependent
   command will fail. Do not print a secret, a variable value, or the environment.
3. The guarded path must be **loud enough not to hide a real regression** on machines where the
   loader *is* expected. Silence on a machine that should have it would be a worse failure than the
   current error.
4. Regression test that a `.envrc` evaluated with the function undefined exits clean, emits the
   informative line, and still applies the exports that follow it.

## Owning-repo caveat — read before implementing

Filed here per the operator's explicit instruction, because `ai c` is where the error surfaces. But
the code that emits it is **not in ai-cli-utils**: the call site is each repo's tracked `.envrc`,
generated from `project-template/template/.envrc.jinja`, and nothing in `ai-harness/install.sh`
distributes a `direnvrc`. A fix confined to ai-cli-utils cannot remove the message.

Confirm the true owner before writing code, and if the fix belongs in project-template or
ai-harness `install.sh`, say so and file there rather than bending an ai-cli-utils change around it.
Note also that `project-template/tests/test_template.py` **asserts** `load_ai_core_secrets` appears
in every generated `.envrc` (and `test_skip_if_exists_resurrection.py` treats it as protected
content), so the call is test-enforced while its definition is undistributed — that asymmetry is the
actual design defect and any guard must keep those tests honest rather than merely green.

## Related

The `.envrc` / `load_ai_core_secrets` portability gap is already documented as a scrub-inventory
correction in `ai-harness/docs/plans/aih-536-scrubbed-share-repo.md` (row 25): "it calls
`load_ai_core_secrets`, a function defined only in Sergei's profile — `direnv allow` errors in a
fresh clone." Fold into that framing rather than re-deriving it.

The cross-machine secrets-distribution question (Doppler per-machine environments, an
auto-generation script) is deliberately a **separate** issue in the ai-core store.

---

## Correction (2026-08-14) — blast radius was overstated in this issue's original text

The original description said "every repo in the fleet ships a tracked `.envrc` that calls
`load_ai_core_secrets`". That is **false**, and the measurement contradicting it was already in
hand when it was written.

Measured inventory of tracked `.envrc` files across the 16 fleet directories:

| repo | `.envrc` tracked | calls the loader |
|---|---|---|
| ai-core | yes | yes |
| ai-harness | yes | yes |
| aido | yes | yes |
| sw-bms-workspace | yes | yes |
| ai-cli-utils | yes | **no** |
| other 11 dirs | no `.envrc` at all | n/a |

So it is **4 of the 5 repos that have an `.envrc`**, not all of them. `ai-cli-utils/.envrc` already
carries a deliberate no-Doppler variant, which is evidence that a non-Doppler shape is workable and
should inform the design rather than be treated as an outlier.

The gap itself is unchanged and still real. Only its scope was wrong.

## Two additional findings from the design pass (verified)

1. **The failure is a false success, not merely a silent one.** `.envrc` prints
   `direnv: <project> environment loaded` **before** calling the loader, unconditionally. So the
   failing run emits a success line and an error line together. Any fix that only adds an error
   message leaves two contradictory statements on the same run — the success line has to become
   conditional on the load actually succeeding.
2. **`direnv` IS installed on sem-kg-sagemaker** (`~/.local/bin/direnv`) while `doppler` is not.
   That makes the state "actively evaluated and silently incomplete" rather than "not configured",
   which is the worse of the two and the reason it superficially looks like it worked.
close_reason:
FIXED and on origin -- but MISFILED here, and the delegate proved it rather than assuming it.

ai-cli-utils owns nothing in this defect. Its .envrc does not contain the
load_ai_core_secrets call at all: lines 9-12 are already the generic no-Doppler
form. It is the one consumer that never had the bug, so no change was possible
here, not merely unnecessary. Filing it in this store was my error -- I routed it
to where the operator saw the symptom (`ai c`) rather than to the code that emits it.

Where the fix actually landed:
- project-template `fe38acd` on main -- template/.envrc.jinja guarded, the existing
  "loader must appear in every generated .envrc" assertion strengthened rather than
  dropped, +6 behavioural tests. 130 passed / 8 skipped on the merged tree.
- ai-harness `d61f18b9` on main -- its own .envrc guarded, plus
  tests/test_envrc_secrets_guard.py (96 lines).

Both were needed because copier.yml lists .envrc under _skip_if_exists, so a
template change can NEVER reach an existing consumer -- every consumer's file is a
hand edit. That is the sharpest finding of the whole task and it was not in my brief.

Behaviour now, verified by me with a LIVE `direnv exec`, not from the report: one
`WARNING ... Doppler-backed secrets are NOT loaded ...` line, no `command not
found`, and TRACING=false still applied. The shipped file leaks no value and no
environment dump (0 matches for printenv / set -x / declare -x / export -p).

Deliberately no opt-out: the file cannot know whether a given machine is supposed
to have the loader, so a suppression flag would go silent on exactly the machine
where absence is a regression.

Correction recorded on this issue before closing: my original text claimed "every
repo ships a tracked .envrc that calls the loader". Measured, it is 4 of the 5 repos
that have one -- and the delegate further corrected the denominator, 13 git repos
under the projects root, not 16 directories.

Remaining work, tracked elsewhere, deliberately NOT folded in here:
- AIH-ai-core-aido-ffvt -- ai-core, aido and sw-bms-workspace .envrc files are still
  unguarded.
- AIH-install-sh-bootstrap-kmgw -- nothing installs a direnvrc at all. That is the
  definition side; this issue was only the graceful-degradation side. Both are needed:
  the guard makes absence safe, installing a direnvrc makes absence rare.

title: ai session-adopt — fails when session ran in worktree (searches repo-root CC slug instead of worktree slug)
ai c silently resumes the wrong (older, unrelated) session when the intended most-recent one is a live background agent
description:
Observed live 2026-08-12 (sergei's own machine, sw-6 fleet-coordinator session in the sergei repo worktree sw-6). A live interactive session (session id e708efd4-bdb7-4a55-a1c8-997e9747adc8, custom title sw-6) was exited normally by the user (intending to relaunch in bypass-permissions mode) but did not actually terminate -- it was instead left running as a detached background agent process. The user then ran `ai c 6` to relaunch, expecting it to continue that same fleet-coordinator conversation. Instead it silently landed on a completely different, unrelated older transcript (session id e2184270-60ed-44f2-b198-3b16abfa6dc3, an ad-hoc research conversation about Israeli-Palestinian negotiations) with no warning that the intended/expected session was unavailable.

Root cause (confirmed): `claude --continue` cannot resume a session that is already running live (confirmed via `claude --resume <id>` returning "Session <id> is currently running as a background agent (bg). Use `claude agents` to find and attach to it, or add --fork-session to branch off a copy."). Because the correct, most-recently-used session was busy, `ai c`'s continue-resolution silently fell back to the NEXT most recent transcript for that cwd instead -- with zero indication to the user that this happened. The user spent an extended troubleshooting session (with an assisting Claude Code instance) trying `-r`/`--resume` (which is `ai c`'s own tmux-reattach flag, unrelated to Claude Code's own session resume), the native `/resume` picker (worked, but required manually identifying the correct session by custom title among only 2 candidates), and finally `claude --resume <id>` directly (which surfaced the real root cause: the session was still alive as a background agent).

Two distinct problems to fix, potentially separable:
1. (ai-cli-utils, `ai c`'s launch/continue-resolution logic) When the most-recently-used transcript for a cwd cannot be resumed because it is a currently-running background agent, `ai c` should say so explicitly (e.g. "most recent session <name> is running as a background agent; falling back to <next-session-name>, or run `claude agents` to attach to it directly") rather than silently substituting a different, unrelated conversation with no warning.
2. (Possibly Claude Code itself, or a documentation/procedure gap) A session the user believed they cleanly exited was instead left running as an orphaned background agent -- worth understanding whether this is expected behavior from some launch flag/mode combination (e.g. bypass-permissions relaunch flow) or a genuine leak.

Both a Claude Code CLI /bug-report AND this internal bug doc were discussed; the CC-native bug-report flow requires explicit user invocation (locked from model-invocation per AIH-876) and has not yet been filed by the user. This doc captures the ai-cli-utils-side finding and reproduction for that separate track.
notes: Resolved AI-CLI-210 (commit 902581c on main): ai c now detects title-matched live Claude Code sessions via the local session registry (~/.claude/sessions/*.json, matched by sessionId), avoids touching or continuing them, warns with title+pid and recovery steps (claude agents / --fork-session), and starts a fresh session instead. The tmux path now delegates to the same Python resolver via a new 'ai internal resolve-continue-target' subcommand, removing the prior duplicate/buggy inline implementation. Full suite: 2309 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated tmux-server flake (confirmed not a regression -- passes in isolation with and without the diff). Problem #2 from the bug doc (why the original session didn't terminate cleanly) remains open, out of scope, tracked separately per the doc.

title: Newly created worktree/session/CC title inherit the fleet-registry prefix casing verbatim instead of always lowercasing
description:
Follow-up to AI-CLI-206 (AI-CLI-565q, fixed at commit 2519721). That fix
covers RESUMING an existing worktree/session when the current invocation's
prefix casing or remote-marker differs from what's already on disk/in tmux.

It does NOT cover the other half: when there is no existing slot to resume
and a genuinely NEW worktree/session/CC custom-title is created, the name is
still built verbatim from resolve_project_prefix()'s registry value
(session.py get_project_prefix(), consumed by build_session_name()). If a
project's registered fleet prefix is uppercase (as fleet-registry prefixes
conventionally are, e.g. for beads task ids), the new worktree directory,
tmux session name, and CC session's customTitle (iTerm2 tab/window title via
ai_name) all come out uppercase too -- e.g. worktree ".worktrees/APP-8",
tmux "c-APP-8", title "APP-8".

The user's stated expectation: only the beads task-id prefix should ever be
uppercase. The CC session, its custom title, and the worktree directory name
should always be lowercase, regardless of the casing registered in the fleet
registry for bd task-id purposes.

ROOT CAUSE (needs verification, not just trusted): get_project_prefix()
(session.py ~line 237) returns resolve_project_prefix()'s value verbatim,
and its own docstring already states "Worktree names and custom session
titles are both built from this value" -- so the fix likely belongs at that
single choke point (lowercase there, or at each of build_session_name()'s
three call sites in main.py), NOT in resolve_project_prefix() itself, which
must keep returning the registry's canonical casing untouched for any
current or future bd-task-id-prefix consumer. Confirmed this session:
ai_name/session_id from build_session_name() flow directly into
_iterm2._emit_iterm2_profile_setup() (main.py ~2192), which sets the CC
customTitle/tab title -- so build_session_name() is the single choke point.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A newly created worktree directory name is always lowercase, regardless of
  the fleet-registry prefix's registered casing.
- A newly created tmux session name is always lowercase (except the engine
  tag c/g and the -r- remote marker, which are already lowercase).
- The CC session's customTitle (iTerm2 tab/pane title, set from ai_name) is
  always lowercase.
- resolve_project_prefix()/get_project_prefix()'s return value is UNCHANGED
  (still returns the registry's literal casing) -- lowercasing happens only
  at the point(s) where the value feeds worktree/session/title naming, not
  at the source.
- No regression to AI-CLI-206's fix (case-insensitive resume matching must
  keep working for a legacy uppercase worktree/session that predates this
  fix).
- Regression test: a fleet-registry prefix registered uppercase; a brand
  new session launch (no pre-existing worktree/session for that slot);
  asserts the resulting worktree dir, tmux session name, and ai_name/title
  are all lowercase.
close_reason: Fixed and independently verified across 2 audit rounds at commit acf7ab4: newly created worktree/tmux-session/CC-title now always lowercase, resolve_project_prefix()/get_project_prefix() unchanged for other consumers, AI-CLI-206 resume matching unaffected. Round 1 (Codex audit, high effort) found 8 issues including a real shell-injection vector (F-1, unquoted remote prefix reaching a remote shell command) -- all 8 fixed and independently re-verified against the audit's own reproduction commands. Round 2 (fresh Codex audit) confirmed 7/8 fixes PASS; fixed the 1 trivial P3 (N-2, docstring) directly; deferred 1 P1 (N-1, remote named-session preview identity mismatch) to AI-CLI-209 after verifying it predates this fix entirely (pre-existing at commit 2519721^, unrelated to casing). Full audit trail: docs/audits/ai-cli-208-session-naming-casing-audit.md.

title: Session launch must accurately report whether it created a new worktree or reused an existing one
description:
_announce_worktree_isolation() (main.py:332) unconditionally prints "Creating
isolated worktree for this session: <path>" whenever the launch directory is
the repository root -- BEFORE create_worktree() (session.py:793) has actually
run and decided whether it is creating a brand-new worktree or reusing an
already-registered one at that path. The message is therefore wrong whenever
reuse happens -- exactly what fired in the AI-CLI-203 case-collision incident:
the log said "Creating isolated worktree ... SW-1" for a path that in fact
already existed as a live, registered worktree.

Separately, the announcement only fires when cwd == repo_root (main.py:340-341)
-- a bare-mode or non-root-launch session gets no announcement at all, new or
reused.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR: before entering the Claude Code / Gemini session (i.e.
before exec'ing into tmux/the engine), always print one line stating whether
the launch is creating a NEW worktree or using an EXISTING one, and the path
either way. Applies to both `ai c` and `ai g` launches, not just root-directory
launches.

Likely implementation shape: have create_worktree() report back whether it
created or reused (e.g. return a (path, created: bool) tuple, or check
wt_dir.exists() + registered_worktrees() membership once up front and thread
that boolean through), then print the accurate message at the existing call
site in main.py (~line 1938-1940) using that real outcome instead of the
current pre-emptive assumption.

RESOLVED 2026-08-10 at commit 23e8796: create_worktree() now returns
(path, created) via with_status=True, and main.py prints the accurate
outcome ("Creating isolated worktree..." vs "Using existing worktree: ...")
after the call, for both ai c/ai g and both root/non-root launches. Verified
by Codex audit Round 2 (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md,
JA-4/JA-5: PASS).
acceptance_criteria:
- Launching into a brand-new worktree prints "Creating ... <path>"; launching
  into an already-registered existing worktree prints something like
  "Using existing worktree: <path>" -- both before the CC/Gemini session is
  entered, for both `ai c` and `ai g`, not just repo-root launches.
- The printed outcome (new vs existing) matches create_worktree()'s ACTUAL
  decision, not a pre-emptive guess made before create_worktree runs.
- Regression test covers both paths: first launch (new) and a second launch
  reusing the same session slot (existing), asserting on the exact message
  content re: created-vs-reused and the path.
- No change to worktree creation/deletion behavior itself -- this issue is
  output-only. Behavior changes to the delete path belong to AI-CLI-203.

STATUS 2026-08-10: satisfied at commit 23e8796, independently verified by
Codex audit Round 2 (JA-4/JA-5 PASS). Closing.
notes: Close reason correction (audit N-6, 2026-08-10): the prior close reason overstated verification -- Round 2 audited 1bd495c (pre-follow-up) and reported 'Not ready'; it never verified commit 20a8436. Round 3 is the first pass to verify 20a8436, and found N-5 (worktree reuse after failed initialization, P1) in the shared create_worktree() path. AI-CLI-204's own ACs (JA-4/JA-5) remain independently PASS-verified; N-5 affects AI-CLI-203's concurrency scope, tracked separately.
close_reason: Fixed at commits 23e8796/b2072ca/20a8436; independently verified by 2-round Codex audit (docs/audits/ai-cli-203-204-worktree-launch-fix-audit.md)

title: Repair the broken local tmux install (loader error: libutempter.so.0 unresolved) so the 4 real-tmux launch tests run instead of skipping
description:
Follow-up from AI-CLI-201. The tmux binary on this machine is on PATH but cannot
execute — a broken appimage extraction with unresolved shared libraries:

  $ tmux -V
  tmux: error while loading shared libraries: libutempter.so.0:
        cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Also reported unresolved: libevent_core-2.1.so.7.

CONSEQUENCE, now that AI-CLI-201's guard is honest: the 4 real-tmux tests in
tests/test_session_launch_integration.py SKIP on this box (loudly, with the
loader's own message) instead of failing misleadingly. That is the correct
behavior, but it is still a real coverage gap HERE — those 4 tests do not
exercise the launch path on this machine until the install is repaired.
They pass normally on a healthy box.

PROVEN RUNNABLE with the right loader path (tmux 3.4 starts, all 5 tests in the
file pass, assertions untouched):

  LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/tmuxprobe/x/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:\
/home/sagemaker-user/.local/lib/tmux-appimage/usr/lib

That is NOT a fix: /tmp/tmuxprobe is a throwaway probe dir and will not survive
a reboot. Note libutempter is present as
/home/sagemaker-user/.local/lib/libutempter.so.1.2.1 — the wrong soname
(.so.1.2.1 vs the required .so.0), which is likely the whole problem.

OPTIONS (decide, do not just pick the quickest):
  1. Install tmux from the system package manager so the loader resolves it
     normally. Cleanest if permitted on this box.
  2. Repair the appimage extraction: place the needed libs in a PERSISTENT dir
     and set the soname/symlinks correctly, rather than leaning on
     LD_LIBRARY_PATH from a temp path.
  3. Accept the skip on this machine and rely on CI for that coverage — only
     acceptable if CI genuinely runs these 4 tests with a working tmux.
     Verify that before choosing this.

Do not "fix" this by relaxing the guard in the test file — the guard is correct
and was the point of AI-CLI-201.

title: Personal-machine check: rename the config section header if AI-CLI-189's old section is populated there
description:
FOR A CC SESSION ON THE PERSONAL MAC. This cannot be done from sem-kg-sagemaker: the file is on
another machine and no synced copy exists anywhere on this filesystem.

AI-CLI-189 renames a config-section key out of ai-cli-utils' shipped default config template, because
the old name is a private platform name in a PUBLIC package. The rename is clean and deliberate — pre-v1,
no compatibility shim (see that issue for the reasoning and the measurements behind the decision).

THE ONE THING THAT NEEDS CHECKING ON THAT MACHINE. `load_config()` writes `DEFAULT_CONFIG` only when no
config file exists (`src/ai_cli/config.py:272-274`), so an existing config is never rewritten, migrated,
or clobbered. Nothing on disk changes and nothing is lost. But if the old section is present AND
POPULATED, then after the rename `config.get(<new name>, {})` finds nothing and `ai cc-usage push`
silently stops pushing — reporting that keys must be set under a section the user's own file does not
have.

  grep -A3 '^\[<old-section>\]' ~/.config/ai-cli-utils/config.toml

Read the CHANGELOG's [Unreleased] / Changed entry for the exact old and new names; AI-CLI-189 is required
to record both there precisely so this task is actionable without any conversation context.

THREE OUTCOMES, and only one needs work:
  * both keys commented out (the untouched template default) -> genuine no-op, close this
  * section absent entirely                                  -> no-op, close this
  * keys populated                                           -> rename the section header in that
                                                                config.toml, then verify with
                                                                `ai cc-usage push --dry-run`

MEASURED ON sem-kg-sagemaker 2026-08-08, as the baseline this is checking against: the section exists
with BOTH keys commented out, and `cc-usage-cursor.json` does not exist, so the feature has never
successfully run here. The Mac is unverified and may differ — it is the machine where this feature would
plausibly have been configured.

DO NOT paste the key VALUES into any transcript, issue, or commit if they turn out to be populated. They
are credentials. The section NAME is all this task needs, and `[[ -n "${...}" ]]`-style presence checks
are the pattern for anything else.

DONE WHEN the Mac's config is confirmed to be in one of the three states above and, if populated, the
header is renamed and a dry-run push verified. Report which of the three it was — that closes the one
gap AI-CLI-189 shipped with, and it is worth recording rather than just closing silently.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING WHILE THERE, since the same reasoning applies: any other machine with a populated
config. This issue is written for the Mac because that is the one known unverified case, but the check is
the same anywhere.

title: Five .claude/worktrees checkouts have no .git, so they are invisible to git worktree list, prune, and VS Code alike
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-08 by two agents independently, on sem-kg-sagemaker.

Five directories under .claude/worktrees/ hold full repo checkouts but have NO .git file or
directory at all. Consequence: they are invisible to `git worktree list`, invisible to
`git worktree prune`, and invisible to VS Code Source Control. Nothing in the normal worktree
tooling can see or reclaim them. They consume 773M.

  aido/.claude/worktrees/agent-a5d2a8bd35914af44                            413M
  bms-semantic-knowledge-graph/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9a27875f2e110178     99M
  bms-semantic-knowledge-graph/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2e5372ae65701dd5     92M
  bms-semantic-knowledge-graph/.claude/worktrees/agent-a56cc92fd02c18192     90M
  bms-semantic-knowledge-graph/.claude/worktrees/agent-adb88157ceeea876e     79M

Verified two ways. First, a direct `-e <dir>/.git` test across every sibling: in the same two
parents, every OTHER agent-* directory HAS a .git and appears in `git worktree list` -- 2 real
worktrees plus 1 orphan in aido, 10 real plus 4 orphans in the kg repo. So the probe
distinguishes the two cases rather than reporting everything as orphaned. Second, the sweeping
agent blob-checked each orphan's source files against the parent repo's object database and
found 0 files missing in all five, with a positive control that correctly flagged 3 uncommitted
files in a different, live worktree -- so the "nothing unique here" finding could have come out
the other way.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ISSUE rather than part of the AI-CLI-196 sweep: the sweep's scope was
worktrees git knows about. These are not worktrees by git's definition -- they are the residue
of one, left behind when the .git link was removed (or was never written) while the checkout
stayed. That makes them a distinct failure mode with a distinct remedy, and it is why they went
unnoticed: every tool anyone would reach for to audit worktrees is blind to them by construction.

DELETION IS A HUMAN GATE ON THIS MACHINE and no agent may act on this without Sergei's explicit
approval. The recommendation is discard, on the evidence above, but the decision is his.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
AC-1  THE SYSTEM SHALL detect checkout directories under .claude/worktrees/ and .worktrees/ that
      lack a .git entry, in every repo under the projects root, and report path, size, and parent
      repo.
AC-2  WHEN such a directory contains a file whose content is not present in the parent repo's
      object database, THE SYSTEM SHALL report that file rather than treating the directory as
      safe to discard (failure-path AC).
AC-3  THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT delete any such directory without explicit human approval per
      directory, and SHALL print the total reclaimable size so the decision can be made on
      evidence.
AC-4  WHEN a directory IS approved for removal, THE SYSTEM SHALL re-verify AC-2 immediately
      before deleting, not rely on an earlier scan.
AC-5  THE SYSTEM SHALL distinguish an orphan from a live worktree by testing for .git presence
      AND cross-checking `git worktree list`, and SHALL report any directory where the two
      disagree.

NOTES
- Root cause is unestablished. Worth determining whether these are left by `git worktree remove`
  failing partway, by a killed agent process, or by a checkout created without ever registering
  the worktree. Without that, a detector treats the symptom and they will accumulate again.
- 773M is not the important part; invisibility is. A directory that no tool can enumerate is
  where uncommitted work goes to be lost, and that already happened once today with worktrees
  that WERE visible to git but hidden from VS Code.
close_reason:
RESOLVED 2026-08-08. All five orphaned checkouts are gone; a fresh sweep of every repo's
.claude/worktrees/ finds zero directories lacking a .git entry.

Sergei approved the discard explicitly. Split of who removed what, because it matters for the record:
  DELETED BY ME (2): aido/agent-a5d2a8bd35914af44 (413M), kg/agent-a9a27875f2e110178 (36M)
  REMOVED BY THE kg-1 SESSION (3): agent-a2e5372ae65701dd5, agent-a56cc92fd02c18192,
    agent-adb88157ceeea876e — that session was working the same directories concurrently.

VERIFICATION BEFORE EACH DELETE, re-run immediately rather than trusting the earlier scan: no .git
entry, zero entries in `git worktree list`, zero live CC sessions with that cwd, zero processes holding
it. Plus a blob check of every file against the parent repo's object database — 0 files not present,
across 533 files in the two I removed.

TWO THINGS WORTH RECORDING, both corrections to my own earlier reasoning:

1. I attributed the mid-sweep disappearances to CC's cleanupPeriodDays. WRONG — Sergei identified it as
   the kg-1 session doing its own cleanup. The tell was in my own measurements and I misread it: three
   of the five SHRANK while I was measuring them (92M -> 37M, 79M -> 16M, 99M -> 36M). A directory
   shrinking between two reads is a concurrent writer, not a scheduled sweep. I was racing another
   session on shared directories and should have asked who else was working them before acting. My
   "already gone, skipping" guard is what prevented that race from becoming an error.

2. ONE PROBE WAS INADMISSIBLE AND I NEARLY RELIED ON IT. For agent-a2e5372ae65701dd5 the blob check
   reported "checked=0, not-in-object-db=0". That reads as a clean pass but proves nothing — it was
   vacuous because the directory had already been emptied by the other session. Had I taken it as
   evidence of safety I would have deleted on no evidence at all. Same shape as the argv-ignoring
   validator earlier the same day: a check that RAN is not a check that could have come out the other
   way. A zero-denominator result must be treated as NO RESULT.

ROOT CAUSE REMAINS UNESTABLISHED and this closure does not address it. Unknown whether these are left
by `git worktree remove` failing partway, a killed agent process, or a checkout that never registered.
So recurrence is not prevented — only the current backlog is cleared. The detector proposed in this
issue's ACs was not built; if these reappear, that is the work, and root-causing it should come first
so a detector treats the cause rather than the symptom.

title: Sessions started outside ai c never get the stable task namespace, so they land in an ephemeral session-XXXX dir
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-07 by Sergei: the `ai` CLI IS installed on sem-kg-sagemaker (v0.7.0 at
~/.local/bin/ai, with `c`, `session-adopt`, and `cc-migrate` subcommands). My original root cause --
"the ai CLI is not installed here" -- was WRONG. The machine profile's "what does NOT apply" list says
`ai` commands are unavailable on this box, and I took that as current fact without probing. It is the
profile that is stale, not the CLI that is missing.

THE ACTUAL SITUATION, in Sergei's words: "ai cli is installed on this machine. I just haven't fully
operationalized it yet for all cc sessions. i think kg-1 and ai-cli-1 and maybe some others still need
to have their cc session jsonl transcript data and cc tasks and memory etc migrated over to worktree
path to use it."

So this is NOT a missing-mechanism defect. It is an incomplete-migration state: sessions started
OUTSIDE `ai c` (kg-1, ai-cli-1, possibly others) never got the pin, because `session_script.py:397`
exports CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID only on the `ai c <N>` launch path.

STILL-VALID MEASUREMENTS (correct, and they remain the symptom):
  [[ -n "${CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID:-}" ]] -> NOT SET   # this session, started outside `ai c`
  ~/.claude/tasks/ census: 905 ephemeral session-XXXXXXXX, 2 full-uuid, 4 NAMED
  (aido-1, aih-1, aih-2, kg-3 -- exactly the ones launched through `ai c`)
  This session's tasks live in ~/.claude/tasks/session-8f446e52/, keyed to a per-process run id.

4 named vs 905 ephemeral is therefore a measure of how much of the fleet has been operationalized, not
evidence of a missing feature.

SCOPE CORRECTION. `ai session-adopt` already exists to adopt a session started outside `ai c`, and
`ai cc-migrate` already moves a transcript between project paths -- so the remedy tooling exists too.
This issue reduces to two narrower questions:

Q1. Should a session that did NOT come through `ai c` still get a stable namespace automatically, or is
    adoption always a deliberate act? If automatic, the pin must move to a launcher-independent surface
    (an install.sh-managed export, or an AI_HOST+repo-derived name). If deliberate, this is really just
    documentation plus AI-CLI-152.

Q2. Can the namespace be changed for an ALREADY-RUNNING session at all? CC may resolve it before any
    hook or export can act. If so, no configuration retrofits a live session and adoption necessarily
    requires a restart -- which is exactly why AI-CLI-152 needs Sergei to exit the sessions and is not
    delegable.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Establish and record whether CC resolves the task namespace before hooks/exports can influence it.
This decides Q2 and whether any automatic retrofit is possible. A fix that silently no-ops is worse
than none: the panel would look correct while tasks kept orphaning.

AC-2 WHEN a session starts through a path other than `ai c`, THEN state the intended behaviour
explicitly -- stable namespace automatically, or ephemeral-until-adopted. Do not leave it implicit.

AC-3 The existing `ai c` pin keeps working unchanged. Regression-test rather than assume, since a second
mechanism would set the same variable.

AC-4 WHEN two sessions run concurrently in the SAME repo, THEN state the chosen behaviour -- shared
namespace or disambiguated. This is the case most likely to corrupt a task list.

AC-5 Correct the sem-kg-sagemaker machine profile, which wrongly lists `ai` commands as unavailable
here. That stale line produced this issue's wrong root cause, so leaving it would cause the error
again. Source is in ai-harness projects-wide-session-config/modules/; compile.py AND install.sh must
both run or the edit is a no-op.

AC-6 Do NOT migrate or delete any of the 905 existing ephemeral namespaces. Separately human-gated;
note the count and leave them.

RELATED: AI-CLI-152 (adopt the live kg-1 and ai-cli-1 sessions -- the operational half, not delegable
because liveness is a property of the process). The /task-panel skill documents namespace mechanics and
the orphan-recovery procedure.
notes:
AC-1 PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED, 2026-08-17, against the INSTALLED CC 2.1.233 bundle
(~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.233). Stating precisely what is settled and what is not,
because AC-1 itself warns that a fix which silently no-ops is worse than none.

## SETTLED 1 - the resolver precedence is UNCHANGED at 2.1.233

Extracted verbatim (minified names preserved):

    function r6(){
      if(V.CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID) return V.CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID;
      let e=xU(); if(e) return e.teamName;
      return pg()||Vy.taskList.leaderTeamName||qt() }

Structurally identical to the aV() documented from 2.1.222 in the load-task-panel skill: the env
var is branch 1, the highest-precedence branch, so it defeats both namespace rotation and the
all-completed sweeper. That skill's mechanics are still accurate 11 releases later - re-verified,
not assumed. The resolver is also CALLED per operation, not cached: an adjacent call site compares
r6() against a fresh value on each task write.

## SETTLED 2 - the HOOK route is impossible, and needs no measurement

A SessionStart hook runs as a CHILD PROCESS of the CC process. A child cannot mutate its parent's
environment; that is an OS-level property, not a CC design choice. So no hook can ever set
CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID for the session that spawned it. Any proposal of the form "have a hook
export the pin" is dead on arrival, whatever the resolver does.

## NOT SETTLED - whether a settings.json env block retrofits a LIVE session

This is the actual substance of Q2 and I am NOT claiming it either way.

Evidence FOR impossibility: the bundle NEVER reads process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID (0
occurrences). Access is only ever V.CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, where V is an envalid-style
validated-env object built from schema accessors (the key is declared Ge.str()), and Object.freeze
appears in the bundle. That pattern normally means a one-time parse at startup, which no later
change can affect.

WHY THAT IS NOT PROOF: process.env[ bracket access appears 50 times, so a lazy per-access getter
cannot be excluded from static analysis. A lazy getter would make V read the live environment, and
then a settings-env write WOULD take effect - CC applies its settings env into its own process, and
the rc-pair mechanism relies on a settings env change landing on the next turn for a different
variable. Static analysis is inconclusive here and I will not upgrade it to a conclusion.

## THE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and why I did not run it

Set env.CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID in a worktree .claude/settings.local.json, let one turn pass so
the settings reload lands, then TaskCreate and observe which directory under ~/.claude/tasks/
receives the file.

I did not run it on this session. The only session available to me to experiment on is this live
one, and a namespace change mid-run would move this session's own task panel and orphan its four
open rows. AI-CLI-152 already marks live-session adoption as needing Sergei and not delegable
precisely because liveness is a property of the process - running the experiment here would be
doing AI-CLI-152 unilaterally under the cover of measuring AC-1. The clean version is a throwaway
session, which is a separate deliberate act.

## CONSEQUENCE FOR Q1 AND THE ISSUE'S SHAPE

Regardless of how Q2 resolves, one thing follows from SETTLED 1 that reframes the fix: the pin is
LAUNCHER-INDEPENDENT. Branch 1 reads an ordinary environment variable, so nothing about it is
specific to the ai c code path - any launcher, wrapper, or shell profile that exports it gets the
stable namespace. So the remedy for sessions started outside ai c is very likely NOT a code change
in this repo at all, but an install-managed export or a documented convention. That makes Q1
(automatic vs deliberate) the real decision, and it is Sergei's.

AC-6 respected: the 905 ephemeral namespaces were counted and read only. Nothing migrated, nothing
deleted.

title: ai c worktrees default their upstream to origin/main even when the repo checkout is on a workspace branch
description:
When `ai c <N>` creates a worktree in a repo whose working branch is not `main`, the new branch inherits `origin/main` as its upstream. In a shared team repo on a PR workflow that points routine session work at the branch nobody is allowed to push directly.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 ~21:25 UTC in `bms-semantic-knowledge-graph`, whose main checkout sits on `sergei/dev-workspace` (a personal workspace branch), NOT `main`:

  worktree  branch    upstream
  kg-2      wt-kg-2   origin/main                     <- wrong
  kg-3      wt-kg-3   origin/sergei/dev-workspace     <- right
  kg-4      wt-kg-4   origin/sergei/dev-workspace     <- right (was origin/main, I repointed it)

kg-3 having the correct upstream while kg-2 and kg-4 did not is the interesting signal: this is not a uniform "always uses origin/main" bug. Two worktrees created by the same command disagree, so the upstream is being derived from something incidental -- plausibly whatever `origin/HEAD` pointed at, or the branch checked out at creation time, or a difference between an `ai c`-created worktree and a hand-created one. **Establish which before changing anything**; a fix aimed at the wrong mechanism will look correct and reproduce the bug on the next repo.

WHY IT MATTERS. `push.default` is unset in that repo, so it defaults to `simple`, which refuses to push when the local branch name differs from the upstream's -- `wt-kg-2` vs `main` differ, so a bare `git push` errors rather than pushing. That is luck, not safety: an explicit `git push origin HEAD:main` from the worktree goes straight through, and the repo is a shared BMS team repo where pushing `main` directly is forbidden and PR review is mandatory. The blast radius is an unreviewed force-of-habit push to a protected-by-convention branch, and the fleet cannot add server-side branch protection there yet.

DESIRED BEHAVIOUR: a worktree created by `ai c` should track the branch the session is actually working on -- the main checkout's current branch, or an explicitly configured workspace branch -- and should never silently default to `origin/main` when the repo's own checkout is on something else. Where no better answer exists, prefer NO upstream over a wrong one: an unset upstream makes `git push` fail loudly and ask, which is the safe direction.

Interim mitigation already applied by hand, purely local and not a substitute for this fix: the two upstreams were repointed, and `remote.origin.push` was set to `refs/heads/sergei/dev-workspace:refs/heads/sergei/dev-workspace` in that clone's `.git/config` so a bare `git push` can only ever update the workspace branch. That is one machine's local config, affects no teammate, and does not survive a fresh clone -- which is exactly why the default belongs in the tool.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 A worktree created by `ai c` in a repo whose checkout is on a non-`main` branch gets that branch as its upstream, not `origin/main`. Verify with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{upstream}` in the created worktree, on a repo fixture whose checkout is deliberately not on `main`.

AC-2 A worktree created in a repo whose checkout IS on `main` keeps working as it does today -- no regression for the common personal-repo case.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: when the intended upstream cannot be determined, the worktree is created with NO upstream and the situation is surfaced to the user, rather than falling back to `origin/main`. Prove it with a fixture where resolution genuinely fails; a silent fallback to `origin/main` fails this AC.

AC-4 Establish and record WHY kg-2 and kg-4 differed from kg-3, since a fix that does not explain that difference has not found the mechanism. If the difference turns out to be pre-existing worktrees created by an older code path, say so explicitly and show the evidence.

AC-5 Configurable per repo, not hardcoded: a repo must be able to declare its workspace branch (config over code). Do not special-case any repo name, and do not hardcode `sergei/dev-workspace` -- ai-cli-utils is a PUBLIC package, so no personal branch names, usernames, or account-specific paths in source, tests, or docs. Use generic placeholders (`workspace`, `myproject`) in fixtures.

AC-6 Both short and long option forms if this adds a CLI flag, per the repo's CLI conventions -- no long-only flags.

AC-7 Docs updated in the same commit as the behaviour change, including a one-line statement of what a session author should expect their new worktree to track.

RELATED CONTEXT: worktree creation and lifecycle are governed by the fleet's worktree procedure; this changes only which upstream is attached, not where worktrees live or how they are cleaned up.
close_reason:
Fixed in b413776, verified on origin/main by content. Base+upstream now resolve together from the repo's integration branch: [worktree_upstream] config table first, then the main checkout's branch; repo on main unchanged. Resolution failure attaches NO upstream + warns, never falls back to origin/main; branch-nowhere / detached HEAD / no-origin fail loudly. AC-4 MECHANISM: the lead's 'incidental derivation' hypothesis was FALSIFIED -- ai c was uniformly wrong. The set-upstream-to=origin/main call has been unconditional since 121c9c9, predating all three kg worktrees, and reflogs show kg-2/kg-4 'Created from refs/remotes/origin/main' vs kg-3 'Created from HEAD'. kg-3 is the anomaly: its 25-entry reflog carries 8 'pull --tags origin ' + a workspace merge, refspecs NO ai-cli code path emits, so it was repointed outside ai c. Fourth sample wt-kg-7 (untouched by the manual mitigation) tracks refs/heads/main. Also found a SECOND undocumented upstream writer by probe: git worktree add -b
sets an upstream itself via branch.autoSetupMerge, so declining one must actively clear it. Third site fixed: workspace.py drift check hardcoded origin/main, so it flagged every correct worktree and stayed silent about the wrong one. Failure-path proof two-sided in the same clone (assert 'origin/main' == 'origin/workspace'). Suite 2194 -> 2211; ruff clean. Docs updated same commit (README, architecture.md, and the BUG-004 open question this resolves).

title: ai-cli-utils' .beads/issues.jsonl has 5+ records absent from the local Dolt store -- bd export refuses to overwrite
description:
Discovered 2026-08-07 (sw-6 session) while trying to link AI-CLI-112 to ai-harness AIH-764. Running 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' printed: 'Warning: auto-export skipped: .beads/issues.jsonl contains 5 JSONL-only issue record(s) absent from the local Dolt store (AI-CLI-9r4c, AI-CLI-liur, AI-CLI-m7uh, AI-CLI-srye, AI-CLI-uln5); refusing to overwrite.' Despite that warning, the export command still proceeded and wrote a 179-issue file that DROPPED those 5 plus several more (AI-CLI-u9x, AI-CLI-c5f3, AI-CLI-sf5c, AI-CLI-1d2, and a handful of raw-UUID-only records) that git diff showed as removed -- caught before committing, reverted via git checkout, no data lost in the committed history, but the live Dolt store and the committed JSONL are now confirmed diverged in a way a plain 'bd export -o' cannot safely reconcile.

Needs investigation: why does the local Dolt store lack records that exist in the committed JSONL (a prior sync gap? a local Dolt DB that never fully caught up to a push/pull? a partial 'bd init --from-jsonl' that was never completed?), and a safe reconciliation path (bd's own suggested 'bd init --from-jsonl' may be right, or may itself be lossy in the other direction -- verify before running it). Until resolved, do NOT run a bare 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' in this repo -- it will silently drop real issues from the committed file.

title: pytest-timeout is declared in [dependency-groups], not [project.optional-dependencies], so `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` silently omits it and --timeout becomes a no-op flag
description:
Found 2026-08-07 by a sub-agent setting up an environment for this repo, and worth pinning because the failure is silent in the direction that matters.

`pytest-timeout` is declared under `[dependency-groups]` in pyproject.toml. That is a valid PEP 735 location and `uv sync --all-groups` installs it correctly. But the extras-based install path — `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` — does not read dependency groups, so it resolves and installs WITHOUT pytest-timeout.

WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY MISSING DEP. `--timeout` is not a flag pytest ignores gracefully in every configuration. In a repo where the plugin is absent, passing it can make pytest exit 0 having collected and run NOTHING — a real false green, already observed once elsewhere in the fleet. So the failure mode is not "tests error out because a plugin is missing"; it is "the suite reports success without testing anything", which is the single most expensive way for a test-infrastructure gap to fail.

The asymmetry: whoever set the environment up with `uv sync` sees the plugin present and the flag working. Whoever used the extras path sees a flag that appears accepted. Both then make claims about the same repo, and the one who measured with the broken environment has no signal that anything is wrong.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE DECLARATION IS WRONG. `[dependency-groups]` may well be the right place for it. The defect is that two documented-looking install paths produce different test capability with no error, and nothing in the repo says which one is required.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 A single documented install command produces an environment where the full suite runs as intended, and the repo says which command that is.

AC-2 The divergent path either works too, or fails LOUDLY. An install that silently yields a weaker test environment is the defect; making it error, warn, or be explicitly unsupported all satisfy this, silently working does not.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: prove the false green is closed. In an environment built the extras way, run the suite with `--timeout` and show it either runs the tests or fails visibly — never exits 0 with zero tests collected. Show the current behaviour first, so the fix has something to be measured against.

AC-4 Do not fix this by simply removing `--timeout` from wherever it is invoked. That hides the environment gap instead of closing it, and the next flag with the same property will reproduce it.

title: A session carrying a stale worktree binding relocates its transcript on worktree exit, and there is no standalone repair for one already in that state.
description:
Established 2026-08-07 while fixing the adopted-transcript relocation (see the issue this depends on). The fix there neutralises the stale binding AT ADOPTION TIME, which covers every future adoption and the one known broken case. Two gaps remain, both deliberately left out of that fix's scope:

GAP 1 — no standalone repair. A session adopted by the older code still carries `worktree-state` records with a live `worktreeSession`. Today the only way to clear one is to re-run the adoption, which also re-moves the transcript and rewrites 5000+ cwd fields — far more than the situation needs. There is no "just neutralise the binding where it sits" surface.

GAP 2 — the hazard is not specific to ADOPTED sessions. The relocation is CC's own behaviour: on leaving a worktree it returns the session to the recorded absolute `originalCwd` and renames the transcript into that directory's project dir. Any session that ever ran EnterWorktree carries such a record, adopted or not. Agent worktrees live under `.claude/worktrees/` and are transient — they get cleaned up — so those absolute paths go stale as a matter of routine, not as an edge case. A session whose transcript is already where it belongs can still be moved somewhere unexpected.

MEASURED SCOPE at filing time: of 11 titled sessions fleet-wide, exactly one carried worktree-state records (19 of them, 38 records total once `relocated` stamps are counted). So the population is currently small — which is the argument for doing this before it is not.

WHY IT IS WORTH A SEPARATE ISSUE rather than folding into the fix: the two have different shapes. Neutralising at adoption is a write the adopter already owns. Repairing in place is a new operation on a file no one asked to move, so it needs its own dry-run, its own idempotence, and its own answer to "what if the worktree still exists and the session is genuinely in it" — a live binding is not always stale.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 A session carrying a stale worktree binding can have it cleared WITHOUT re-running a full adoption (no transcript move, no cwd rewrite).

AC-2 The operation distinguishes a STALE binding from a LIVE one and refuses, or skips, the live case. A binding whose `worktreePath` still exists and whose session is genuinely inside it must not be silently cleared. State which signal is used and why it is sufficient.

AC-3 Idempotent: running it twice changes nothing the second time, and reports zero records changed rather than rewriting the file. An unnecessary write is a real filesystem event to anything watching the path.

AC-4 FAILURE PATH: prove it against a session that is NOT adopted and whose transcript is already in the right project directory — show the transcript does not move, and that a subsequent worktree exit does not relocate it. Then show the same scenario DOES relocate on unfixed behaviour, or the probe cannot come out the other way.

AC-5 Surfaced where a human will find it: reported by `ai session-audit` (a session carrying a live binding is a fact worth showing), with both short and long option forms per repo convention.

AC-6 No data-loss path: temp file + atomic replace, original intact on any failure, and a test that asserts no debris is left behind.

NOTE ON DURABILITY. The probes behind all of this ran against Claude Code 2.1.223 only. If a future version moves the rename from the worktree-exit path into the resume path, both this and the adoption-time fix would need re-verification — so any fix here should record the version it was established against rather than presenting the behaviour as timeless.

title: ruff-check pre-commit runs --fix, so widening select would mass-autofix unreviewed
description:
The `ruff-check` pre-commit hook runs with `args: [--fix]` (.pre-commit-config.yaml:62, verified 2026-08-06). That is fine for the current narrow rule set, which reports "All checks passed!" — there is nothing left to fix. It becomes a defect the moment `[tool.ruff.lint] select` is widened.

THE MECHANISM. Widening `select` is not a neutral config edit while `--fix` is on. Newly-selected families do not surface as a reviewable list of findings; they get AUTOFIXED, file by file, inside whatever unrelated commits happen to touch those files next. So a rule-set change lands as scattered mechanical edits across many commits, attributed to whoever was working on something else, with nobody ever reviewing it as a change.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG WAY ROUND. The tracked lint-adoption work carries an explicit constraint: do NOT bulk-autofix, because the concern is a mass mechanical change nobody reviews. But `--fix` does not prevent the autofix, it only removes the review. One deliberate, reviewable commit that applies a phase's fixes in full is strictly BETTER than the same edits dribbling through unrelated commits. The constraint as written protects against the visible version of the problem while the invisible version is already wired in.

MEASURED CONTEXT (2026-08-06, this repo, `ruff check --select <F> --statistics src/ tests/`):
  current select E4,E7,E9,F -> All checks passed (0)
  phase-1 candidates I,UP  -> 229 findings, 228 of them autofixable
So the very first adoption phase is ~99.6% autofixable, which is exactly the case where `--fix` would silently do all the work before anyone looked at it.

Note also that the finding counts alone mislead about scope, which is a separate reason to want the diff reviewable: SIM's 441 findings are 375x SIM117 (stacked `patch()` in tests), and PLC's 513 are 512x PLC0415 (deliberate lazy imports, which that rule's own documentation concedes as legitimate). A family total is not a work estimate.

WHAT THIS ISSUE IS NOT. It is not a proposal to adopt any rule family — that decision is tracked separately and is the user's call. It is also not a claim that `--fix` is wrong in general; for a stable rule set it is a convenience with no downside. The defect is specifically the interaction: `--fix` plus a widening `select` equals an unreviewed mass rewrite.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Widening `select` cannot cause unreviewed mechanical rewrites. Either `--fix` is removed from the hook, or an equivalent mechanism ensures a newly-selected family's fixes land as one deliberate reviewable change rather than piecemeal through unrelated commits.

AC-2 Whatever the mechanism, `ruff check` still FAILS the hook on a genuine violation. A fix that makes the hook merely report and pass would be worse than the current state — prove the hook still blocks a commit that introduces a violation.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: prove the unreviewed-rewrite scenario is actually closed. With the new arrangement, add a rule family to `select`, then commit an unrelated one-line edit to a file carrying findings from that family, and assert the commit does NOT silently rewrite that file. This must be demonstrated, not argued — the current behavior and the fixed behavior look identical on a clean tree, so a probe on a clean tree proves nothing.

AC-4 The developer experience is documented: whoever adopts a phase should have a stated, discoverable way to apply that phase's fixes on purpose (an explicit `ruff check --fix` invocation is fine — the point is that it is deliberate and reviewable, not automatic).

AC-5 Do not adopt, widen, or narrow any rule family as part of this fix. Config scope stays exactly as it is; only the autofix behavior changes.

CONTEXT. Surfaced 2026-08-06 by the lint rule-set selection research (docs/research/ruff-ruleset-selection.md), which flagged it as its own open question after finding the hook's `--fix` flag. Nothing in the original lint-adoption issue anticipated it. Independently verified at .pre-commit-config.yaml:62. This is a PREREQUISITE for any rule-set widening, so it should be resolved before the first adoption phase, not after.
close_reason: Fixed in bfc9aa4: ruff-check hook is report-only; verified on origin by content, both probe directions, 2183 tests pass

comments.author: Sergei Wallace
comments.text:
RESOLVED in bfc9aa4, verified on origin/main by content (not by push output).

FIX. Dropped `args: [--fix]` from the ruff-check pre-commit hook, so lint is report-only. `ruff-format` deliberately keeps its rewrite: formatting is not rule-set-scoped, so widening `select` cannot change what it does, and its diff is whitespace only. That asymmetry is now stated in the config comment so a later "consistency" cleanup does not strip the formatter's rewrite too.

AC-1 MET. `--fix` is gone from the hook. A newly-selected family now surfaces as a reviewable list of findings that fails the commit, instead of being rewritten piecemeal.

AC-2 MET, with a real positive control. Staged a module containing a deliberate F821 undefined name (a violation under the CURRENT unwidened select, so this does not depend on any widening):
  hook exit=1, `ruff check ... Failed`, `F821 Undefined name`
  `git commit` exit=1, and `git log --oneline -1` still at a6f4b0d — nothing landed.
NOTE ON MY OWN PROBE: my first attempt at this AC recorded `commit exit=1` and I nearly reported it as proof. It was not — the output said `[ERROR] Your pre-commit configuration is unstaged`, i.e. pre-commit refused to run at all. That exit code would have been identical had ruff-check been passing everything. Re-ran with the config staged; only then did the block come from `ruff check ... Failed`. Recording this because the failure mode is exactly the one AC-3 warns about: two situations that print the same thing.

AC-3 MET, demonstrated in BOTH directions on the same file, because the two configurations are indistinguishable on a clean tree.
Probe: widen select to ["E4","E7","E9","F","I"], append one unrelated comment line to src/ai_cli/layout.py (which carries an I001 finding at line 10), stage it, run the ruff-check hook.
  BEFORE (with --fix): `ruff check ... Failed`, `- files were modified by this hook`, `Found 1 error (1 fixed, 0 remaining)`. md5 went ffe77a11 (pristine) -> 5ae493cd (my edit) -> c69dc909 (hook's rewrite). The hook had deleted a blank line inside the import block — a change unrelated to my edit and never reviewed. Re-staging and re-running then reported `Passed`, so the rewrite lands committed. `git diff origin/main --stat` showed 2 insertions/1 deletion where the developer authored 1 insertion.
  AFTER (no --fix): identical steps. `Found 1 error. [*] 1 fixable with the --fix option.` md5 after-my-edit == md5 after-hook (5ae493cd both). File byte-identical; the finding is reported, the commit is blocked, nothing is rewritten.

AC-4 MET. CONTRIBUTING.md gains a "Lint autofix is deliberate, never automatic" subsection under Code Style: it explains why the hook is report-only while the formatter is not, and gives the three-step deliberate flow — `ruff check --statistics` to see full scope, `ruff check --fix` to apply, `git diff` to review, committed separately from feature work.

AC-5 MET. `select` is untouched. `git diff pyproject.toml` is empty; the whole change is 3 files (.pre-commit-config.yaml, CONTRIBUTING.md, tests/test_ruff_pin_integrity.py), +139/-2.

REGRESSION TESTS — four, in tests/test_ruff_pin_integrity.py (the existing home of the "a config change silently redefined the gate" family, BUG-006):
  1. the ruff-check hook's args contain no `--fix`
  2. ruff-format's rewrite is still allowed (pins the asymmetry so it is not "cleaned up")
  3. end-to-end: a fixture module with an I001 finding is NOT rewritten by `ruff check` without --fix, and the test first asserts the fixture genuinely carries a finding, so it cannot pass vacuously
  4. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the same fixture IS rewritten under `--fix`. Without this, test 3 could pass merely because there was nothing to fix.
Mechanical check performed: restored `args: [--fix]` and confirmed test 1 goes RED (`AssertionError: assert '--fix' not in ['--fix']`), then removed it and confirmed GREEN. A guard I had not watched fail would not have been evidence of anything.

GATE. Full suite 2183 passed, 0 failed. `ruff check src/ tests/` -> All checks passed. `ruff format --check src/ tests/` -> 90 files already formatted.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RULE-SET DECISION. This was the stated prerequisite for the first adoption phase, and it is now cleared: widening `select` will produce a reviewable list of findings rather than a silent rewrite. The choice of which families to adopt remains open and is the user's call.

title: ai session-audit: survey titled CC sessions fleet-wide and drive adoption reproducibly
description:
`ai session-adopt` (AI-CLI-168, shipped 2026-08-06) adopts ONE named session per invocation, and `-a/--all` only sweeps titled sessions inside a single source directory. There is no way to answer, or to act on, the fleet-wide question: "which titled CC sessions exist anywhere, where does each one actually live, and which are not resumable by `ai c <n>` from their repo root?"

That gap cost real time on 2026-08-06. Doing the AI-CLI-151 adoptions by hand required an ad hoc Python one-liner over `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` to extract `customTitle` per transcript, plus manual cross-referencing against `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` for liveness and against each repo's `.worktrees/` for the destination. Two concrete defects surfaced only because of that manual survey:

1. **A recorded location was simply wrong.** Both AI-CLI-151 and AI-CLI-168 stated that `aih-1` lived at the ai-harness repo ROOT. It did not — the root transcript is `aih-2`. `aih-1` was in `.claude/worktrees/aih-657-profile-correction`, an AGENT worktree. A title-based adopt from the repo root failed with "no transcript titled 'aih-1'" until `-s/--source` was pointed at the real directory. Nothing in the tooling could have surfaced that; it took a hand-rolled scan.

2. **A title collision was invisible until adopt refused it.** Two transcripts both claimed `kg-3` (419 lines at the kg repo root, 2708 lines in `.worktrees/kg-3`). The collision gate correctly refused and proposed a free index, but there was no way to see the collision coming, or to see that it was the only one, without scanning every project directory by hand.

MEASURED FLEET STATE (2026-08-06, this machine): 187 transcripts total, 11 titled. After the AI-CLI-151 adoptions all 11 titles are unique fleet-wide and 0 collisions remain. Titled sessions: aih-1, aih-2, aih-3, acto-1, aido-1, ai-cli-1, kg-1, kg-2, kg-3, kg-4, proj-1.

WHY A COMMAND AND NOT A ONE-OFF SCRIPT. This is not a migration that happens once. New sessions are started outside `ai c` continuously (a plain `claude` in a repo root, a CC agent worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`), so the fleet drifts back out of adoption on its own. The survey is also the natural place to catch the two failure modes above BEFORE an adopt is attempted, rather than discovering them from a refusal. A reproducible command with explicit options for where to look and what to do is the difference between re-deriving the survey by hand every time and running one thing.

SCOPE NOTE. This is the SURVEY-AND-DRIVE half. The adoption mechanics already exist in `session_adopt.py` and must be REUSED, not reimplemented. In particular the unconditional title-collision gate must keep working exactly as it does now: it is the safety property that prevented a nondeterministic `ai c` resolve, and `-y/--yes` must never cover it. The live-session refusal must likewise stay intact — adopting a live session moves a transcript out from under a running CC process. Note both live-session and collision refusals are CORRECT behavior, so a bulk driver must report them as expected outcomes and continue, never treat them as errors to work around.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 A new `ai` subcommand surveys titled CC sessions across the fleet and reports, per session: the title, the transcript path, its line count, the repo the transcript's cwd belongs to, whether it is already in the correct worktree slot, whether it is currently live, and whether `ai c <n>` resolves it from its repo root.

AC-2 The survey discovers sessions in ALL the places they actually occur, not just repo roots: repo roots, `.worktrees/<name>`, and CC agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/<id>`. The `aih-1` case above must appear correctly, attributed to ai-harness, without the caller supplying its path.

AC-3 The command reports title collisions (one title claimed by more than one transcript) as a distinct, named condition, with every claimant listed, BEFORE any adoption is attempted.

AC-4 The command has an option to drive adoption for everything it finds that is safe to adopt, delegating to the existing `session_adopt` code path rather than duplicating it.

AC-5 A dry-run option shows exactly what would happen and writes nothing. Verify by asserting the filesystem is byte-identical before and after a dry run, not merely by reading the output.

AC-6 Options exist to control WHERE it looks and WHAT it acts on (at minimum: restrict to one repo, and restrict to one title), so the command is usable narrowly and not only as a whole-fleet sweep.

AC-7 FAILURE PATH: when a session is live, or its title collides, the command reports that session as skipped with the specific reason and a non-zero-signal in the summary, continues processing the remaining sessions, and does NOT adopt the refused one. A refusal for one session must never abort the batch.

AC-8 FAILURE PATH: the unconditional collision gate and the live-session refusal both remain in force through the new path. Prove each by attempting an adoption that should be refused and asserting it was, including that `-y/--yes` does not bypass the collision gate.

AC-9 Every option has BOTH a short and a long form, per this repo's CLI convention. No long-only flags.

AC-10 The command works on a machine with zero titled sessions and on one with zero repos, without raising.
