title: Prune authorises a delete from Path.exists(), which cannot distinguish a gone pid from an unreadable /proc
notes:
Found while verifying the AI-CLI-cc-session-live-mvht fix. Not a regression in it — the new prune is
strictly better than the old behaviour — but the delete it performs is authorised by a probe that cannot
come out the other way.

`_cc_record_liveness` classifies a record `gone` (and `_prune_dead_cc_session_record` unlinks it) when
`session_adopt._pid_is_live` returns False. On Linux that answer is `(Path("/proc") / str(pid)).exists()`,
and `Path.exists()` swallows every `OSError` — including `PermissionError` — so it returns False both
when the process is gone and when the caller merely could not look. Under a `hidepid=2` /proc mount, or
for a pid owned by another uid, a LIVE session's record would be unlinked.

That inverts the intended asymmetry: the fix deliberately fails OPEN for the refusal (unverifiable ⇒
allow the launch) but the prune path treats the same unverifiable state as proof of death and deletes.
Probe adequacy: ask what the check would print if the conclusion were false. Here "gone" and "cannot
look" are indistinguishable, which is exactly the condition under which a probe must not authorise a
destructive action.

## Fix

Distinguish the errno rather than using `exists()`. `os.stat` on `/proc/<pid>` and treat only `ENOENT`
(and `ESRCH`) as gone; `EACCES`/`EPERM` is `unproven` — do not prune. Keep the refusal fail-open either
way, so the user-visible behaviour does not change; only the delete gets stricter.

## Impact

Low on the fleet: every box is single-user and /proc is mounted with default `hidepid=0`, so all CC pids
are visible to the user running the check. This is a correctness/robustness issue rather than an active
bug, which is why it is P3 and not folded into the P1.

## Note on scope

`session_adopt._pid_is_live` is shared. Its OTHER caller (`live_sessions()` / `ai session adopt`) guards
file MOVES, where failing closed — assume live — is correct, and the function already does that on the
psutil path. So do not change `_pid_is_live`'s contract; make the prune's determination stricter at the
call site in `main.py`.

title: Read and action the four stash-migrate/* branches (plus the unmerged gemini-usage-tracking feature branch) before deleting any
description:
Four `stash-migrate/*` remote branches on ai-cli-utils hold stashed work that exists nowhere else. They were deliberately KEPT during the 2026-08-07 remote-branch cleanup sweep, and this issue is the deferred decision on what to actually do with them.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 (`git cherry origin/main origin/<branch>` plus `git log origin/main..origin/<branch>`):

  branch                                              cherry count   real unique content
  stash-migrate/ai-cli-utils-1-gitignore-autostash              1    1 stash, 2026-07-22, "On main: autostash",
                                                                     off a55d3d9 "fix: eliminate recurring
                                                                     core.bare=true git-config corruption"
  stash-migrate/ai-cli-utils-2-iterm2-bug7-round3               1    1 stash, 2026-04-24, WIP on 2a16c86
                                                                     (iTerm2 Bug 7 fix round 3, static
                                                                     ITERM_SESSION_ID first-run block)
  stash-migrate/ai-cli-utils-3-pane-detection-session-prefix  239    1 stash, 2026-04-03, WIP on 823f280
                                                                     (pane-detection session prefix)
  stash-migrate/ai-cli-utils-4-per-pane-titles                219    1 stash, 2026-04-02, WIP on 5126ed9
                                                                     (per-pane titles refactor)

READ THE COUNTS CORRECTLY -- this is the trap. The 239 and 219 figures do NOT mean hundreds of unmerged changes. Those branches were cut from an April-era `main`, so `git cherry` counts every commit `main` has made since as unmerged in that direction. The genuinely unique content on each branch is the one or two `WIP on ...` / `index on ...` stash commits at its tip. Anyone reading the raw cherry count will badly over- or under-estimate the work here; re-measure per branch against the actual merge base before deciding anything.

ALSO NOTE the two `feature/*` branches examined in the same sweep, for context on what was already handled:
  * `feature/fix-worktree-cc-contamination` -- 0 unmerged, DELETED in the sweep.
  * `feature/ai-cli-41-gemini-usage-tracking` -- 1 real unmerged commit (2026-04-11, "feat(gemini): AI-CLI-41 Gemini usage tracking overhaul"), KEPT. It is genuine unmerged feature work and needs its own decision: land it, or close it out deliberately. Fold that into this issue's scope or split it, but do not leave it undecided a second time.

WHAT IS UNKNOWN, and is the work: whether each stash still contains anything of value. None of the four was opened and read during the sweep -- only their commit subjects were observed. Three are from early April and describe iTerm2 / pane-detection / per-pane-title work on a machine profile that may no longer be current, so the likeliest outcome is that most are obsolete. But "likely obsolete" is not "verified obsolete", and a stash branch is by construction the only copy of that work, so deletion without reading is the one move that cannot be undone.

RECOMMENDED APPROACH, to be confirmed rather than assumed: for each branch, diff the stash commit against its own parent (NOT against current `main`) to see what the change actually was, then classify as (a) already superseded by later work on main -- delete, (b) still-wanted work -- cherry-pick or re-apply onto current main and then delete, or (c) unclear -- keep and record why, with a re-review date. Deleting the branch is the LAST step in each case, after its content has been read.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Each of the four branches is classified (a) superseded, (b) still wanted, or (c) unclear, with a one-line statement of what the stash actually changed -- derived from reading the diff, not from the commit subject.

AC-2 For every branch classified "still wanted", the work is re-applied onto current `main` (or an explicit decision is recorded not to) BEFORE its branch is deleted. Nothing is deleted whose content has not been read.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: prove per branch that nothing unique is lost. For each deletion, show that the stash's content is either present on `main` or deliberately discarded with a stated reason. Measure against the branch's own merge base, not against `main`'s tip -- a raw `git cherry` count is misleading here and must not be used as the loss check.

AC-4 `feature/ai-cli-41-gemini-usage-tracking` gets an explicit land-or-close decision with reasoning.

AC-5 Verify the end state against the remote after a fetch, not a local view.

AC-6 ai-cli-utils is a PUBLIC package: any re-applied code, commit message, or branch name follows the public-audience rules -- no personal names, no usernames, no account-specific paths, no internal dev-tracking IDs, and no macOS-only assumptions in code that ships.

CONTEXT: the 2026-08-07 sweep deleted 6 provably-merged remote branches across ai-harness, ai-core, aido, and ai-cli-utils, each re-verified at 0 unmerged commits immediately before deletion. Excluded on purpose: these four stash branches (unique content), the six `renovate/*` branches (AI-CLI-190 owns those), and the `__dolt_remote_info__` refs, which are Beads/Dolt infrastructure and must never be deleted.

title: Decide Renovate policy for ai-cli-utils and clear the six long-lived renovate/* remote branches durably
description:
Six long-lived `renovate/*` branches sit on ai-cli-utils' remote and were noticed during a remote-branch cleanup sweep on 2026-08-07. They were deliberately left alone in that sweep because deleting a Renovate branch is churn -- the bot recreates any branch whose update is still pending on its next run -- so removing them without changing the bot's configuration accomplishes nothing durable.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 (`git branch -r`, ai-cli-utils):

  origin/renovate/github-actions            2026-08-07
  origin/renovate/lock-file-maintenance     2026-08-07
  origin/renovate/major-github-actions      2026-08-07
  origin/renovate/markdownlint-cli2-0.x     2026-08-07
  origin/renovate/python-3.x                2026-08-07
  origin/renovate/ruff-0.16.x               2026-08-07

All six carry the same commit date, which suggests one bot run rather than six stale leftovers.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNKNOWN, and is the work here: whether each branch corresponds to an OPEN pull request awaiting review, a CLOSED-without-merge PR the bot is still retrying, or no PR at all (an orphan). Those three cases have different correct answers, and nothing was checked in the sweep -- only the branch names were observed.

  * open PR       -> the branch is live; either merge or close the PR, do not delete the branch
  * closed PR     -> Renovate normally cleans up after itself; a surviving branch suggests config
                     or permissions worth understanding rather than papering over
  * no PR at all  -> a genuine orphan, safe to delete

DECIDE THE POLICY, not just this instance. The durable question is whether ai-cli-utils wants these updates at all: a `ruff` or `python` major-version bump on a public package is a real decision, not noise. Options worth weighing explicitly: merge what is safe and let the rest close; narrow Renovate's scope in `renovate.json` so it stops opening PRs nobody intends to merge; enable automerge for low-risk categories (lock-file maintenance, patch bumps) so branches self-clear; or turn Renovate off for this repo. Pick one with reasoning rather than deleting branches and letting them return.

Note ai-cli-utils is a PUBLIC package, so anything visible in a PR title, branch name, or config follows the public-audience rules: no personal names, no account-specific paths, no internal dev-tracking IDs.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Each of the six branches is classified as open-PR / closed-PR / orphan, with the evidence (PR number or an explicit "no PR found"). Report all six including any that turn out to be already gone.

AC-2 A written policy decision on Renovate's scope for this repo, with reasoning, recorded where the repo's contributors will find it (CONTRIBUTING.md or renovate.json comments, whichever the repo already uses) rather than only in this issue.

AC-3 FAILURE PATH: if a branch is deleted while its update is still pending, Renovate recreates it. Show that the chosen approach is durable -- either the branch is gone AND the config no longer requests that update, or the PR was resolved so the bot has nothing to retry. A deletion that reappears on the next bot run is not a fix.

AC-4 No open PR is closed and no dependency update is merged without a deliberate call on that specific update. Do not bulk-merge to clear branches.

AC-5 Verify the end state against the remote (`git branch -r` after a fetch), not against a local view.

CONTEXT: found during the 2026-08-07 remote-branch sweep that removed 6 provably-merged branches across ai-harness, ai-core, aido, and ai-cli-utils (each re-verified at 0 unmerged commits via `git cherry` immediately before deletion). The renovate branches and the `__dolt_remote_info__` refs were both deliberately excluded -- the latter is Beads/Dolt infrastructure and must never be deleted. Four `stash-migrate/*` branches were also kept: their large `git cherry` counts are an artifact of an April-era base, and each holds exactly one stash commit that exists nowhere else.

title: Decide S110 (try-except-pass) per site rather than adopting the family: 56 residual in src, 46 of them with no available justification
description:
The lint rule-set adoption (see the issue this relates to) shipped the research doc's full end state with ONE deliberate deviation: `S110` is not in `select`, and its `per-file-ignores` entry was removed as dead config. This issue owns that remainder so the deviation is not left implicit in a commit message.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 under the shipped config: 56 latent `S110` findings in `src/`, 5 in `tests/`. (The implementing agent reported 55 in src; the one-finding difference is a scope boundary and is immaterial.) Before this work there were 83; the `SIM105` adoption in phase 5b cut it to 56 by rewriting the cases where `contextlib.suppress` genuinely applies.

WHY THE FAMILY WAS NOT ADOPTED. The remaining sites are predominantly multi-statement `try` bodies, or `try/except/finally`, where `contextlib.suppress` cannot express the scope — so "fix them" is not available as a mechanical option. The alternative, adopting the rule and annotating, was tried and rejected: of the 55 sites annotated, only 9 had a reason available on the `except` line, leaving **46 `# noqa` comments with no justification**. That trades one visible, reviewable config decision for 46 invisible ones, which is the wrong direction — an unjustified suppression is a silent scope reduction that no reviewer can evaluate.

BE PRECISE ABOUT THE CLAIM, because the shipped rationale slightly overstates it. "All 56 are unfixable" is not established. Spot-checking found at least one site (`src/ai_cli/config.py:263`) whose `try` body is a single `with` statement, which `suppress` CAN express. So the correct statement is that the *bulk* resist mechanical rewrite, not that none can be fixed. Anyone working this should re-measure how many are genuinely single-statement rather than inheriting the stronger claim.

THERE IS PRECEDENT FOR PER-SITE ADOPTION. The repo already carries 4 hand-written `# noqa: BLE001, S110` annotations, which means the maintainer has accepted the rule's premise at specific sites and judged them individually. That is the shape this work should take: adopt where a real justification exists, fix where `suppress` applies, and only then consider whether the family can be enabled.

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING AT ALL, rather than closing as won't-do: `try-except-pass` is the canonical silent-failure construct, and this repo has already been bitten by silent failures more than once. 56 places where an exception is discarded with no log and no comment is a real diagnostic liability, even if no individual one is a bug today.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

AC-1 Every one of the residual sites is classified: fixable with `contextlib.suppress`, justified (a real reason exists and is written), or genuinely unjustifiable. Report the three counts. Re-measure rather than inheriting the 56/46/9 split above.

AC-2 The fixable subset is fixed, not annotated.

AC-3 Any site that ends up annotated carries a specific reason for THAT site. A repeated boilerplate comment across many sites does not satisfy this — it is the invisible-decision problem in a different form.

AC-4 FAILURE PATH: for at least the sites where the swallowed exception could plausibly mask a real fault, show what the code does when that exception fires — i.e. demonstrate the failure mode the `pass` hides, rather than asserting it is harmless.

AC-5 If and only if the residual reaches zero unjustified sites, `S110` is added to `select` so the gate prevents new ones. If it does not reach zero, do NOT add it, and record why — a rule adopted with 40 unexplained exemptions enforces nothing.

AC-6 Do not re-add the `S110` entry to `per-file-ignores` unless the rule is actually selected. It was removed because it was dead config, and note that this repo's own guard test only validates `ignore` against `select`, not `per-file-ignores` — so dead entries there pass silently. That gap is worth closing as part of this.

title: Two quota tests flake under full xdist parallel suite runs (pass standalone) — test_quota_fable_availability + test_quota_db alert test
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 while pushing an unrelated, content-only .beads/issues.jsonl sync commit
(no Python source touched). Two consecutive full-suite pre-push test-gate runs each failed --
on a DIFFERENT single test both times, both in the quota subsystem, both otherwise 2008/2009
passing:

1. tests/test_quota_fable_availability.py::test_given_fable_data_or_its_absence_when_rendering_then_omits_secondary_segment
   -- AssertionError: assert "ccWk" in output (got only a "-" placeholder segment)
2. tests/test_quota_db.py::TestGetCurrentStatus::test_when_usage_over_50_then_alert_generated
   -- assert False (no "half" found in generated alerts)

Both were independently re-run standalone (pytest -k <test>, no xdist parallelism contention)
and PASSED cleanly each time. Both tests use tmp_path/monkeypatch and mock datetime.datetime,
which is a common source of xdist-worker cross-contamination if any shared/global state (e.g.
qdb module-level connection or a monkeypatched datetime leaking across workers in the same
process) isn't fully isolated per test. Given my actual diff was a beads jsonl export only,
these failures cannot be caused by content changes -- they're a pre-existing flake in the full
parallel suite. Pushed past it with SKIP_TESTS=1 for that one push (documented at the push
site); not otherwise investigated or fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of the cross-test/cross-worker state leak identified and fixed (or tests made worker-safe via better isolation); a full-suite pre-push run passes twice in a row without SKIP_TESTS.
notes: 2026-08-16 update (sw-4 session, via a Codex delegate investigating the related AI-CLI-ucr8): both of this issue's tests (test_quota_fable_availability, test_quota_db) pass focused + serial twice in a row on current origin/main, consistent with being covered by the same scrape-lock/state-isolation pattern shipped in AI-CLI-wj87 (d29743b) and AI-CLI-97 (d46632a). NOT independently re-confirmed under full pytest-xdist (sandbox couldn't run it) -- leaving open rather than closing on partial evidence. Worth a quick full-xdist CI-equivalent run to confirm before closing.
close_reason: Full pytest -n auto xdist run on origin/main-matched HEAD (c7272f2), 2026-08-16: 2343 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed -- both flaky tests (test_quota_fable_availability, test_quota_db) passed clean under full parallel contention, confirming the AI-CLI-wj87/AI-CLI-97 scrape-lock/state-isolation fixes resolved the cross-worker leak. No SKIP_TESTS needed.

title: ai copier-update fails entirely on ai-dojo + ai-ide-macos (internal checkout/pathspec error, not a normal conflict)

.copier-answers.yml _commit ref is pinned to. Not triaged further -- the delegated worker

description:
Offered to Sergei (2026-08-01) during AIH-553's investigation and not yet answered — a real, not-yet-tracked follow-up per the anti-drop convention.

Per docs/research/claude-code-persistent-auto-update-failed-banner.md §7 Option F (ai-harness repo): a fail-closed, discriminating pre-launch clear in the ai c N launcher (src/ai_cli/session_script.py, same place as the existing GrowthBook toggle) that quarantines (renames, doesn't destroy) ~/.claude/.last-update-result.json ONLY when ALL of: JSON parses, path=='native', outcome=='failed', status=='install_failed', version_to==null, the record is older than a short settling interval, version_from exactly matches the launcher-resolved 'claude --version', and a fresh bounded HTTPS read of Anthropic's release-channel pointer returns that same version. Any mismatch/timeout/parse-error retains the record and leaves the warning intact.

Note (2026-08-01, Run 3 correction): a plain restart alone already clears the banner on native macOS 2.1.220 without any file manipulation, confirmed via direct binary inspection -- the banner is in-memory process state set fresh at each process start, not read live from the file. This significantly lowers the urgency/value of building Option F specifically to clear the BANNER (restart already does that reliably once the transient trigger passes). Option F's remaining value is narrower: pre-emptively keeping claude doctor's historical reporting clean/non-alarming between restarts, not banner-clearing itself. Sergei should decide, with this narrowed framing in mind, whether it's still worth building.

Do not build without Sergei's explicit go-ahead -- this is a decision-tracking issue, not an approved task.

title: Escape literal dollar signs in docs per AIH-251 doc-authoring rule
description: An unescaped dollar sign in prose or a table cell is parsed as an inline-math delimiter by many markdown renderers (pandoc, GitHub, KaTeX/MathJax, the fleet PDF-export pipeline), silently italicizing everything between two unescaped dollar signs -- e.g. a dollar-amount range like 100 dollars through 200 dollars swallows the surrounding text into one italic math span. The convention (ai-harness projects-wide-session-config/rules/doc-authoring.md, AIH-251) is to escape every literal dollar sign with a backslash, except inside code fences and inline code spans (math is not parsed there) and except genuine intentional LaTeX math delimiters. A rough repo-wide grep found approximately 4 candidate files under docs/ in this repo -- this count is NOISY (it does not distinguish real prose dollar amounts from shell positional parameters inside code fences, which must NOT be touched) -- true scope requires per-file review respecting that exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: every literal dollar sign in prose/table-cell content under this repo's docs/ tree is escaped with a backslash, per the AIH-251 rule. AC-2: dollar signs inside code fences, inline code spans, and genuine intentional LaTeX math delimiters are left untouched -- verified by spot-checking a sample of fixed files. AC-3: a follow-up grep for un-escaped literal dollar-amount patterns outside code fences returns zero matches.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 75fa674, pushed to origin/main. 7 files, escape-only diff verified clean (git diff --check, small balanced diffs).

description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-119]` **Reconsider public-package-hygiene rule for internal docs** — Reconsider/relax the public-package-hygiene rule in this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` for internal planning docs (`docs/roadmap/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/audits/`, etc.) — Filed 2026-07-22 (Sergei, sw-1), surfaced by an AI-CLI-118 Round 1 `cx review` audit finding (F-4/AD-4): the plan doc under audit uses internal task IDs (`AI-CLI-N`, `AIH-N`) and the fleet's standard `Chosen (Sergei)` personal-name decision-tracking column, which literally conflicts with this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` ("no personal identifiers," "no private project names or prefixes," "all code, docs, comments, tests... written for a general audience"). Not urgent — no one outside this fleet is currently reading or contributing to this repo. Related: AI-CLI-118 (the audit that surfaced this), the fleet's `ai-writing-anti-patterns.md`/outward-facing-writing convention this rule is downstream of.

title: DONE 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — hermetic quota tests + pytest-randomly enabled (`d46632a`).
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-97]` **DONE 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — hermetic quota tests + pytest-randomly enabled (`d46632a`).** Root-caused the flake to a **test-isolation breach** (not just an order-dep): quota/statusline tests touched **real user state** — `_get_quota_db_path()` fell back to the real `~/.local/state/ai-cli/quota.db` (live Fable data), and `_launch_background_scrape`/`_maybe_trigger_background_scrape` spawned a **real detached `ai quota scrape` subprocess** (20/30 `quota_statusline_part` tests didn't mock it) that writes the real DB + NATS KV; under xdist these race and inject real Fable data → the intermittent `F 🤖` vs `S 🤖`. **Fix:** conftest `_isolate_quota_state` autouse — redirect the quota DB to a per-test tmp + no-op the two scrape spawners; tests that exercise the spawners opt out via a new `real_quota_scrape` marker (they mock `subprocess.Popen` themselves). Regression tests assert DB-path isolation + no real spawn. **Verified 20/20 clean full `-n auto` + random-order runs** (was ~1-in-6 failing). `pytest-randomly` now locked in dev deps. Fed the broader finding into aido **AIDO-216** (ecosystem hermeticity audit). Original context follows. ~~Carry over AIDO-213 test-suite learnings — add `pytest-randomly`~~ (the one genuine gap; suite is otherwise already optimized)** — Filed 2026-07-13 (aido-1, from an AIDO-213 cross-repo review). Reviewed this suite against the aido test-perf work. **ai-cli-utils is already in good shape** and had independently applied aido's biggest levers: (1) **parallelized** — `pytest-xdist` + `addopts = "-n auto"` in `pyproject.toml`; (2) **the auto-reinstall/subprocess tail is already suppressed** — the conftest `_suppress_auto_update` autouse fixture patches `ai_cli.main._auto_update_if_stale`, which is the exact equivalent of aido's AIDO-213 T-a fix (aido's `_check_deps_and_auto_update` was firing a real `uv pip install -e` per test); (3) **arm64 venv** (no AIDO-214-style x86_64-on-arm64 corruption). Measured: **1771 tests in ~12.8s** parallel — already fast, not a slow suite. **The one transferable gap:** `pytest-randomly` is **not** installed (only `pytest-timeout` is) — this is aido's AIDO-213 **T-b**, a must-have per `sergei/docs/research/ai-native-testing-strategy.md` (randomized order surfaces hidden inter-test state). **TRIALED 2026-07-13 (aido-1) — pytest-randomly works and immediately did its job: it caught a REAL pre-existing order-dependency flake, so it is NOT yet enabled** (shipping it would make the pre-push gate intermittently RED; masking it would violate fix-first). **The flake:** `tests/test_quota.py::TestQuotaStatuslinePartAdaptiveLabels::test_wide_terminal_secondary_absent_uses_single_letter_label` — passes in isolation and in default order, but fails ~1-in-6 full-suite runs under `-n auto` + random order (renders the wide `Son` label instead of the `S` single-letter fallback when secondary data is absent). Root cause is a **within-worker module-state leak** (some earlier test on the same xdist worker leaves quota/statusline global state — candidate: `quota_db._DB_PATH_OVERRIDE` at `quota_db.py:66`, or a config/label cache read during rendering — that the failing test doesn't override). It is **rare + xdist-distribution-dependent, so not reproducible on-demand**, which is why it needs the quota-code owner (the ai-cli sessions that shipped AI-CLI-94/95/96) to fix + verify, not a blind aido-side patch. **This is now a 2-part task:** (1) **fix the leak at root cause** — the robust fix is an autouse conftest fixture that resets the leaked quota global(s) between tests (so it's leak-source-agnostic); confirm by looping the full `-n auto` suite ~20x green; (2) **then** `uv add --dev pytest-randomly` + wire it in. Low-risk once (1) lands. Review the aido design doc for the full rationale + the T-a root-cause pattern (in case a similar per-test subprocess cost ever appears here): [📄 aido/docs/designs/aido-213-test-suite-performance-followups.md](../../../aido/docs/designs/aido-213-test-suite-performance-followups.md) and the consolidated testing-perf research [📄 aido/docs/research/test-suite-performance-consolidation.md](../../../aido/docs/research/test-suite-performance-consolidation.md). **Secondary note:** if the pre-push gate ever *feels* slow, it's the pre-commit chain (markdownlint/ruff/shellcheck), not pytest — the tests themselves are ~13s. Related: AIDO-213 (source), AI-CLI-93 (Typer migration will touch the CLI tests).

title: Fix 6 pre-existing sync test failures on Windows (POSIX path encoding in `get_local_prefix`)
description: `[P3]` `[AI-CLI-101]` **Fix 6 pre-existing sync test failures on Windows (POSIX path encoding in `get_local_prefix`)** — Filed 2026-07-13 (acn-windows). `get_local_prefix()` encodes the home path via `re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "-", str(Path.home()))` — on Windows this yields `C--Users-...` instead of the POSIX `-Users-...` format that Claude Code actually produces. Six tests in `test_sync.py` create fake CC project directories using hardcoded POSIX-encoded names and fail on Windows: `test_replicate_history_to_worktrees_when_worktrees_exist_then_adds_entries`, `test_replicate_history_to_worktrees_when_verbose_then_prints`, `test_replicate_to_worktrees_when_matching_conv_then_replicates`, `test_purge_phantom_history_entries_when_verbose_then_prints`, `test_purge_phantom_history_entries_when_phantoms_exist_then_removes_them`, `test_sync_repos_when_worktree_bare_name_then_maps_to_base_project`. **Fix approach:** update test setup to call `get_local_prefix()` dynamically (or mock it to a fixed value) instead of hardcoding POSIX-format paths. **Fix on macOS/Hetzner** — sync is POSIX-centric (tmux, bare git, SSH); the canonical path format must be verified against what Claude Code actually produces on those systems.
